Others teach how to make images similar to those whom they signify, — in whom *whatever is inflicted, they suffer* — of which are the *images of Trithemius'* *Cabala*, — the mode and reason of which he transmits: — by *characters, seals, figures, admiring words*, impossible things by others can be perfected; — magic indeed *Cabalistic* can be shown, — he teaches, — that anyone could hear a voice over the sea, — from someone living in the West speak with someone standing in the East, etc.

To this magical art much today attribute the *disciples of Paracelsus*, who magnify it greatly, — with splendid *title of light of nature and insignia*, — of which is the *proverb* (as *Baronius Nachtergallus* *the master of that magic pre-eminently recensets*): *supersedes ceremony*, — that either at the ministers, — tempests to excite, — forests to transfer; — heads to take off men, — again to re-impose; — in a single moment magical *canvasses* to exhibit; — to loosen sleep; — to drink from a sieve; — to shed men long since defunct; — with three arrows from a bow, or with balls emitted from bombards, whatever you want even not seen to confect; — to see all in mirrors — present and future and set — either read or hoped for, thought; — to heal over the greatest distances, — to speak with him who is in *Persia*, when you are in *Spain*, — on the *moon* to read the writing of him who is a thousand miles distant, — and many other things of this genus, which read in the place cited near *Zanchius* can be found.

These arts today many, as pious and good, useful to men, preach; — *Paracelsus* also *by some arguments defends*, — and dares to free magic from the imputation of crime, — the restitution of which see near *M. D. Danielem Sennertum* (in *De chymicorum cum galenicis consensu et dissensu*, cap. 18, p. 4).

All these to *illicit magic* we count, and are certain, that no one with *good conscience* can either *exercise* or *usurp* these things, — whether for the good or the evil of others they be done. Therefore anyone who bears the *Christian name in fact*, who wills God to be propitious, who wills to hold his good conscience unstained, — from these arts must *utterly abstain*.

**Foundations of our sentence** we have as *infallible*:

**(1)** *God has prohibited in the law*: *Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.* (Exod 22:18); *Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards, to be defiled by them: I am the LORD your God.* (Lev 19:31); *And the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits, and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people.* (Lev 20:6). Similar things see Num 24:26, Deut 18:14, and Ps 108:37.

**(2)** *The origin of magical arts* is *from spirits of Baal-Zebub*, — as writes *Clement* (of *Peter*, lib. 4 *Recognit.*), — *they taught these arts of certain evil natural things*. First however among men is said to have been *Cham son of Noah*, who taught this art to his son *Mercurius*, — whom the gentiles *Zoroaster* called; — whom *Pliny* (lib. 30 *nat. hist.* cap. 2), *Apollo*, and most of the gentiles, as also *Augustine* (lib. 21 *De civit. Dei*, cap. 14), first called *magus*; on account of this infamous origin therefore *Christians* with these arts *nothing to be admixed* debere.

**(3)** *Venefices* are numbered by the Apostle among the *works of the flesh* which *exclude a man from the kingdom of God* (Gal 5:20), — in which place in Greek *pharmakeia*, — which voice denotes both *natural venom* and *sortilege*, — or *magical art*, as above we have shown.

**(4)** *We have all bidden farewell to the works of the devil in baptism*, therefore also from these *venoms and magic arts we abstain* — *no association is there of Christ with Belial* (2 Cor 6:15). Now however it is certain, that the works of illicit magic are of the devil, — since neither from the force of nature, nor by special aid of GOD do they happen; — always accedes either *tacit or express invocation of the devil*, for the confirmation or obligation of whom are adhibited certain *symbols external* — as *words, characters, images*, or *natural things*, — in which there is no force at all of producing those effects which magi are wont to produce.

Writes *Paracelsus* (lib. 1 *philos. sagac.*, cap. 6): *nature has imposed her forces into words, as into herbs and roots: images and characters he has said to be the seals*, *in which he preserves the powers of the stars*.

But the pious hold those images and characters as *seals and figures of the devil*. *Paracelsus* also thinks it *integral to accept from the very devil remedies against desperate diseases*: — but this indeed cannot cede with unaffected piety. — For all works of the devil are suspicious, — who when most he seems to profit, chiefly *harms*. And if most he profits always, — against confidence however in God it is from him to *seek help*.

Most just therefore is the cause, why the *magical arts* we ought neither to *pursue* nor to *usurp*, — since they are *diabolical*, whose *inventor* is the devil, and *have their efficacy from the devil*.

**(5)** *Magic even by the Ethnics has been condemned*: *Plato* (lib. 11 *De legibus*) decrees the *capital penalty* on *priests and haruspices* (thus were called the *magi*, according to *Josephus*, lib. 1 *antiq. Judaic.*), — who by sacrifices, ligatures, incantations, or other sortileges shall have killed a man, — a law which he inscribes *hos an pharmakei einei chrainēphontikei*. And although magic in general was permitted among the ethnics (Lev 20:14), the wiser however finally noticed the abomination of these arts: — therefore in the *laws of XII Tables* it is prohibited, and among the *infamous arts* referred; — with *Virgil* (lib. 3 *Georgic.*) *evil sagae* are called *inverse*.

**(6)** *Laws civil also condemn magical arts as diabolical*. For the *law Senatusconsultum de sicariis of the Cornelian law* holds under penalty him who shall have made or had *bad sacrifices*, — that is, *detestable sacrifices of the magi* — *not however of the pagans*, — as *Accursius* transmits in the *gloss*, — since the author of the law himself was a *pagan*, — and by *L. ult. de maleficis C.*, — *worthy of death are judged those who exercise the magical arts*, — which laws *Philo Judaeus* joins with the *law of God* (Exod 22:18): *the law of God*, — he says, — *abhors from magi and venefici*, — who by *modes and arts to be condemned* perpetrate a thousand evils, — *them, as soon as they shall have been intercepted, to be dispatched with death he bids* — as *has L. ultima de maleficis C. Ne quis magum retegerit, immediately to public be drawn*.

**(7)** *Finally accedes the multiplex damage*, which through magic is inflicted upon the *neighbor*. *Magic* can so *fascinate a man's soul*, that with *true religion denied*, he associates with *false*, — beyond any probable cause, — as of *Simon Magus* it is read (Acts 8:9), that he *had seduced the people of Samaria*, saying that he was some great one, — whom all listened to, from *the least to the greatest*, saying: *this is the virtue of God which is called great*. In Greek is *dementia deiciens sanam mentem*. Thus *Elymas* *magnus plenus fuit dicitur omni fallacia*, who used impostures in the business of salvation, *to divert the pro-consul from the faith* (Acts 13:8, 10). Of the *Galatians* *D. Paul* writes: *ye have been fascinated, that ye should not obey the truth* (Gal 5:1).

*Magic* the *souls of men* also in other matters so binds, that either they remain in a fixed place, or love even unwillingly, — either they abhor someone without cause. By which means *philters and love-potions* have rendered many *insane and furious*, — very often *spouses without cause* pursue each other hatefully to death — even judges sometimes are so demented, that they *cannot arbitrate for the party*, though it have an *unjust cause*.

*Magic* inflicts diseases most-lethal on the body, and by other modes harms the body, — of which see *Chrysostom* (in his oration *De pulchritudine et uxore*).

*Magic commits many* thefts, robberies, — money, garments, and similar things by its arts snatches away — of which see *Augustine* (lib. 8 *De civ. Dei*, cap. 17).

*Magic intercepts the fecundity of spouses*, induces sterility. *Amianfus Cal.* writes (lib. 2 *daemonio.* cap. 6) *of a certain* saga of old *in Athens*, who by *aspect or by praise killed men, whom Solinus, Ademonstrat, Plinius, Gellius, and Isidore* also confess.

*Magic prestrings the eyes of men*, so that they seem to see marvelous things which are not, — by which reason it deludes the senses of men, and *from truth makes falsehood*, — which indeed by rigor of divine laws (which do not allow even *prestigators* to live) is worthy of penalty.

*So many incommodities magic brings with it*, — which therefore to exercise and to usurp is *impious* and utterly alien from the *Christian name*.

**Objections** by the cultors of magical arts are made:

**(1)** *Utility* which some claim to gain thence. *For in this way, they say, we can drive out the devil and diseases, avert incantations, and be immune from many perils*.

But in general it must be known that *My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.* (Ps 121:2). To driving evils, medicine is provided by God, — who wills us to honor the physician, not to adore the devil. In which sentence *Chrysostom* wrote: *martyrs, who for healing the sick admit the medicines of sagae, do not permit themselves to be persuaded*.

**(2)** *Pleasure*, which they think they have from the exercise of magical arts, — of which sort are *praestigiatores*, who *many incredible things seem to do* — devour a hay-wagon, cut a whetstone, drink water from a sieve, present dainties confected with marvelous art, represent persons long since dead, and similar things, — with which some others they *delight*, — some of which by wondrous celerity are performed, some without doubt are *works of the devil*.

But this is not *liberal and praise-worthy pleasure*, which is either prepared by the devil's ministry, or seems to be prepared. For to all works of Satan the pious man has renounced, — whether they bring some utility or only *delectation*. Therefore, whoever exercises such works or is delighted by them, is the *adversary of Christ* and *minister of Satan*. *He that is not with me, is against me*, says Christ (Matt 12:30).

**(3)** *Worst of all are* those who from magical exercises reckon Christ himself the *emulator*. There are indeed not only Jews who blasphemed that *Christ's miracles were emitted by benefit of magic*, — of whom see *D. Luther* in *Shem-Hamphoras* (Tom. 8, *fol.* 106 seqq. edit. german.). But also *Anthippus* writes of certain gentiles who boasted to have seen and read *some books of Christ to Peter and Paul*, in which were written the summary of the whole magic art, — from whose knowledge Christ, while he lived, so many miracles did — which blasphemy *Augustine* (lib. 1 *De consensu Evangelistarum*, cap. 9), gravely refutes.

*Nothing therefore is there whereby the magical arts can be palliated or excused even in appearance*: — from which then those who fear God, not without merit abhor with their whole breast.

**Casus II. Whether by magic — illicit — against injury of globes and iron of enemies, can one render one's body immune?**

*Reply.* Of similar things is the same judgment, and what belongs to the genus, pertains also to all its species. Since therefore *magical arts* simply all are adverse to God and to true piety, — of them indeed otherwise we cannot judge, — but that those who by certain arts make themselves immune from strokes and *globes of bombards*, act against God and piety, — as this art today is most familiar to those who follow the camps.

God so created the body of man, that with vehement force he should suffer *dissolution of continuity* — which follows more grievous pain: — to receive globes of fire with the hands, or to receive iron with a *naked and unharmed body*, — is against the order divinely instituted to things.

To use things divinely created *otherwise than they are created* by *God*, is *magic*: to serve the body from a lethal instrument gravely struck, — from a wound however to preserve, safe, — is a *diabolic mode of preserving*, by which Satan permitting God preserves men in his own cult and devotion.

For that such preservation is from God cannot be said, — who without a miracle does not change the order of nature, — nor is it from men, since they cannot produce such unusual effects. Nor is it from those media which in the act are adhibited, — for they do not have so much force of averting what is natural. Therefore it is *from the devil*, with whom the admirers of these arts, either tacitly or explicitly, are *comrades*.

For even though not all who use this art have the intention of gratifying the devil, — and many think they have no commerce with the devil in this art, — yet the first *inventor* of the art without conspiration with Satan *could not have thought out these preternatural things nor brought them into effect*. The rest afterwards, to whom this art pleases, — even unwilling — enter into *conspiration* with the devil, — and to his *cult they consent*. Therefore in no time was any of the pious in the people of God, — where the most difficult wars against various enemies were waged, — read to have used this art. Nor is it credible that it was to them either unknown or already too much culled, — if it were of God, — when God has sufficiently provided otherwise for his people in necessary things.

If also *the media* you consider, whereby the effect is produced, — they are either *words*, or *characters*, or a similar thing, to which God has not given so great powers, marvelous, — and against the constitution of the natural body — of *producing an effect*.

Just as therefore is *magic* to *turn great and swift bullets aside in flight*, — to *conjure bombards* not to be exploded, — to make *armaments, shields, and Martian globes*, whereby at least *hostile forces be foiled* — so, from magic *to be alien it cannot be, to make one's body immune from globes and impact*.

Those who therefore *fear God*, let them leave these arts to those who lean on human or diabolic protections. *Ours is however to say with David*: *I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.* (Ps 91:2).

*What is just, we justly pursue*, — with arms and legitimate media let us protect ourselves, — the rest let us commend to God, — in whose hands are our lots, — and without his will *not even one hair falls from our head*. For as *Prudentius* the Christian poet speaks:

*If pleased Christ is present, — nothing at all shalt thou fear:
If wherever Christ is absent, — no medium shall be more secure.*

**Casus III. Whether *words* are to be numbered among *media* of magic — through which certain marvellous effects are attempted, or performed?**

*Reply.* Among all the ceremonies of magi and sagae, nothing is more used than *words*: — whence also the magi are called *incantatores*, since they use *charms*, wherewith they think they can even *bring down the moon from heaven*, — as *strix* boasts in *Horace*.

Hence there are many even *Rabbis*, who think that the *Hebrew words* — that language in which God spoke with the Patriarchs, — *Osanna*, *Alleluja*, *Selah*, — are in *ecclesiastical hymns* and in the *Gospel retained*, — since some natural force is in them, — which into other tongues cannot be transferred.

This same reason also they think, — since *exorcists* use *certain conceived words*, and in *the name of Jesus* things are done, — since in these very letters *and voice-sound* the *force* and *efficacy* of *repelling demons* is.

And on account of this efficacy which they *attribute to words alone*, it is thought that the *angelical salutation and prayers* are made once, or three, or five, or fifty, or more times to be repeated, — since in the very *recitation* of the holy words is (as they think) *salutary force*.

*Physicians also of oldest antiquity* attribute to certain *verses* some force of *expelling diseases*. So *Aetius* refers, that *Homer* *inhibited the great flow of blood in a wounded head with certain verses*; — from *Theophrastus* he refers that ischiadic *pains were healed by charms*, — from *Cato* that of dislocated limbs help came from *verse*; — from *Varro* that *charms* profit against podagra; — *Trallianus* (lib. 9, cap. 4) and *Aetius* (lib. 3, cap. 20) write: *the beetle-bone in the neck to hang on hemitritian fever*, — with *Serenus Sammonicus* is a certain charm-remedy for pouring out the utterance-of-two-thousand-words — *let it not do vibrate under nails*.

The general opinion of many, among whom is *Plato* (in *Cratylus*), that *natural things names are imposed by nature*, — since a natural force of operating in nature they have, — but not all speak in the same manner of the *names of things*. *Theophrastus Paracelsus* (lib. 1 *Phil. sagac.*, cap. 6) writes: *nature has infused her forces into words, as into herbs and roots*. *Albertus Magnus* (lib. 2 *De mirabilibus mundi*) much attributes to the curation of diseases *by words*, — on that basis, that the *experience of the ancient physicians has approved*. The *efficacy of these* however he does not ascribe to *words*, but to the *consent of souls* both in the physician and the patient, — for *great is the force of the soul* *considering, and with the physician conspiring*. If however the sick doubts, or holds the remedy ridiculous, — or has bystanders who elevate the *faith*, and the *remedy* before him make into contempt, — the incantation gives no force, — since he has an *opposing soul* by that persuasion.

The *words* however which in this genus are used are not of one kind. Some are *Hebrew*, some *Greek*, and *foreign plants*, — like what near *Quintus Serenus* is read: *the voice inscribed in a certain mode, — "Abracadabra," — and by a charter included, and suspended on the neck, cures the hemitritian fever*.

Some *words* are *understood* certain; some *unknown*: some are *certain prayers*, wherewith are evoked the *demons in aid*, — like near *Fortunianus* (De *deis Qmidii*) is read, and near *Ovid* (De *illa*, — sometimes are, however, the name of *Jehovah*, of Jesus the Father, of the Son and Holy Spirit, — names of the *Blessed Virgin*, of the twelve *Apostles*, of the three *Kings*, whereby also characters and signs are adhibited, — through which *God is offended*, blasphemed, and mocked.

*Therefore they invoke the devil chiefly*, to whom also the effects which are produced must be ascribed, — for which same cause any of the pious should from such arts *abhor*.

**Casus IV. Whether *consecrations and benedictions* (as they call) of salt, oil, palm, candles and other things in the Papacy usual, for *magical incantations* should be held?**

*Reply.* It is usual in the *Papacy* to consecrate oil, water, altars, wax candles, breads, cheese, meats, garments, and arms: — and this is done through certain *prayers* and *conceived words*. And of these things consecrated they say, that they are not only *more healthful* than others not consecrated, but even *have spiritual effects*, — for the wiping out of venial sins, for the binding of demons, and for driving away diseases. Of which see *Bellarmine* (lib. 3 *De cultu sanctorum*, cap. 7).

But not from the matter these rites among the *magical incantations* we number: **(1)** since to the words adhibited for this purpose they attribute a peculiar force and efficacy of producing *preternatural effects*, — as *Franciscus Valles* (in *Sacra Philosophia*, cap. 9) writes: *the Church commands exorcists to use conceived words, in which is that force of driving out demons, — which whither may pertain if any say, — that of the Gospel: in my name shall they cast out demons*. For not now in the fasting alone of *ordinary sermon*, but *in my name*, — as if in the very *name-designation* is placed *efficacy*, — this the ancients had.

**(2)** *Effects to things blessed peculiar in common life* they attribute, — even spiritual not excepted, — which *Bellarmine* in the place before cited confesses, — where he writes: *nothing of us to salt, oil, or wax bread benediction, — that of these — supernatural things should be produced, — but that force they have of things blessed from prayers of the church, and devotion of the users*. Thus in the consecration of the wax it is said: *deign to bless and sanctify this creature of wax*, that any of the faithful — the incense from it — *of the divine benediction of grace, — and of the grace of thy saints, — be filled*.

In general also of any creature they say: *thou, O Lord, send thy Holy Spirit into this creature, — that whoever tastes from it, may profit unto eternal life*.

**(3)** *The creatures* which by conceived words they are said to sanctify, — of themselves and by their nature they estimate to be *impure*, — and *under the power of the devil*, — whom by *adjurations of this sort with conceived words they presume to expel*, — which the formulas of *consecrations* teach, whereby *the creature is exorcised, — that all force of the adversary from this creature be adjured, and put to flight*.

Which certain *words nothing differ from magical incantation*, in which likewise the *devil* is either invoked, or in *creatures* is imagined.

However greatly therefore that *benediction* of *creature*, being religious, may be held for *most-religious*, — for the reasons said we prefer it to those incantations in which the *name of God* is taken in vain, — and which are prohibited by God in the law (Deut 18:10).

**Casus V. Whether magic can effect that in the midst of a crowd of men from their sight-conspectus one be able to be removed?**

*Reply.* This is not the last part of magical operations, which however many hold as *sport and jest*. *Pliny* also from *Democritus* (lib. 28 *nat. hist.*, cap. 8) [remarks] — *the left foot of a Chameleon in the frying-pan of an iron torch heated with the herb which is called by that name Chameleon*, — and both macerated in ointment, collected in the manner of a pastille, and put in an *ignescent vessel*, — and that he who bears this vessel, even if he verses in the midst openly, — cannot be seen*. This *Augustine* rebukes (lib. 10 *nat. hist.* cap. 1) and *he writes it to be of ridiculous vanity*.

Which indeed is true if to the *operation* itself of the Chameleon and *heart* thou attendest, — to which to ascribe that effect is *vain* and *ridiculous*. Meanwhile however it cannot be denied that the *improbable* by this art with certain *media*, — although *to this distance many are inept*, — from the sight of others *to lead themselves away* are wont.

But he who fears God and *abhors from the works of the devil*, meritoriously also from this art should abhor. God so created the body of man, that as long as in this mortality it is, — in *pure and perspicuous air* from sound eyes and just distance from the body *distant naturally cannot fail to be seen*.

To *glorified bodies* is another reason, — which by eyes of mortals not clarified cannot be seen. Therefore since the bodies of men are not yet clarified, and are still in this age *crass and terrestrial*, — from those also who are present to them, are not seen, — this happens either by *dispensation of God*, — who *holds the eyes of onlookers*, by which a body *aspectable is made unaspectable*, — as in the history of *Moab* (Elisha) *the Syrians*, in whose midst *he* was, *did not see*, — since God struck them with blindness (2 Kgs 6:18); and in the history of the *Emmauntic disciples*, — where *Christ* to two disciples became *aphantos*, that is, *unseen* (Luke 24:31); — or it is a *work of the devil*, — who by his *prestiges* *deludes the eyes of others*, through those who profess this art of making themselves *invisible*.

For since the *sense of the eyes* is thus moved, that the *air*, which is between, is affected by either light or darkness, — the demon, to whom power over the air has been attributed (Eph 2:2), — easily can vary the air, and the very *sphere of the air* can so *obscure*, that all *aspectus* — even to the most attentive — he takes away: — just as through *circulators many incredible* and naturally impossible things are put before the *eyes of men*, — for the *demons effect them, — as if there were nothing existing, in the manner of what is not, — to be seen by men are made*. Similarly, they can make say, that those things which are exist, — from the *aspect of men* remove them.

Since therefore the *works of the devil in whatever way*, and to *whatever end*, are utterly alien from piety, — no one by these arts should be *delighted*, — even if it be done only for the sake of *jest*.

God in the *law* judged *prestigatores* to death, — that is, *those who fascinate the eyes of men*: *thou shalt not suffer a prestigator to live* (Exod 12:18): since therefore these arts also are *prestigial*, — according to the sentence of the Lord *they are worthy of death* who exercise them.

For the things which are *adhibited externally* cannot have this force, — for who can believe that the *stir of the Chameleon* — of which *Pliny*, — of the *body of man* from the sight of others present *naturally* is able to take away?

This is a *custom of the devil*, and of those who *follow him*, — that in *prestiges* and *incantations* their *external something*, which known-seeing-adhibite for deluding men, — although the demon knows well, that for producing that effect it is not *apt*.

Moreover by this art many *most-present damages are inflicted*, *rapines and adulteries* impunely perpetrated, — from all which not only *its utility*, but even *its impiety in this life* is recognized.

**Casus VI. Whether the *pact* between the *magi* and the *sorceresses* and the devil, — which is said to be, — is by *express convention* with the devil, — or is *only imagined* by *sagae*?**

*Reply.* That the devil entices *magi and sagas* by *blattering words*, promises of wealth and riches, *libidines* and pleasures, — and by these *illicit charms he snares his own tenacious*, — no one denies. That however an *express covenant with him* they enter, and *God having been renounced and their Savior*, — through the ministry of the devil against God are hostile, — this not all admit but many *deny*.

That the *convention with the devil is exact*, and *voluntary*, they do not deny. The *devil* however with man really to enter into a pact they deny, — since *nothing of right in a man he has*, — nor uses *speech* by which he could promise anything and in turn require: — the *matter* also of the pact — which as *stipulation* is drawn — is of that *difficulty, impiety, and turpitude*, — that no one *of sound mind* would desire it, — nor if greatly he desired, would be able to accede.

But these are not moments of such weight, that the matter proven by experience (of which testify hundreds) they can take away. *All faith* rests upon experience, — faith therefore we have of the *sagae*, who confess to have entered *such a pact with the devil*. Let there be seen examples of this thing near *Danaeus* (in *Lameriar*), *Bodinus* (lib. 2 *daemonom.* cap. 4), *Nicolaus Remigius* (lib. 1 *daemonom.* cap. 2). In which places three things about this matter are taught:

**(1)** That the devil those whom he binds to himself, — before their postulations they attain, — an *instrument of obligation* to be made, and to be subscribed with their name, — orders, — if they can write, — the rest by *bare stipulation of words* he binds.

**(2)** Not seldom he also demands *subscription made with blood*, — and this obligation sometimes is for *certain years*, sometimes for the *whole time of life*.

**(3)** If the devil fears that the *magi* might defect from his cult, — he impresses *certain marks*, — sometimes for the whole time of life, sometimes sufficiently conspicuous, — mostly in the *right shoulder or thigh* or even in *the top of the forehead*, in the occiput, in the breast, — sometimes less conspicuous in hidden places, — or between the lips, under the axillae, under the eyelids, etc. — Which place noted by the *diabolic stigma* is said to be *bloodless* and *deprived of sense*, — so that not even a needle even very thickly stuck causes pain, — or draws forth the least of blood, — which so is compact by the *punishers of capital-things*, — from which they often make beginning of the question and of the *torments*.

Just as of old in the *people of God servants and maidservants* who *refused their liberty*, had *their ears bored and fixed to the doorposts of the house*, in a sign, — that by their consent they were perpetually made *slaves* — so also the devil his own slaves he wants *marked*, lest they forget the *pact entered with him* to all the years of his life. Sometimes also the magi, for confirmation of this *convention with the devil*, — allow themselves *to be baptized again in the name of the devil*, whence for the most part they are of *two names*, refers *Bodinus* in the place cited.

However then more strictly to bind themselves to the demon they can, — which crime is by far *most-grave*, and, as by so many examples and confessions of the sagae themselves is confirmed, — cannot be denied, — so in no way ought it to be excused.

Rather is to be *acknowledged the malice of Satan*, who by so many modes strives to lead men away from their Savior and to enslave them to himself, — to whom therefore we must *greatly resist*, and *pray*, lest God desert us, nor to the devil permit anything of right in us.

**Casus VII. Whether magi and sagae by the devil can be carried in body to their conventions, — which they call *sabbaths* — for the sake of *commestations*, of *choruses*, — or for other reasons — as many affirm?**

*Reply.* Much on this question has been *disputed among the erudite*, — some stating that the magi and sagae by the devil, sitting on wooden staves, through many miles are carried to the *conventicles of their companions*, — others however denying it, — attributing whatever the *sagae* say has happened to them elsewhere-in-place, — to *illusion of the senses* by insomnia of *sleepers*, — in which opinion is *Wier* (lib. 3 *De praestig. daemonum*, cap. 12), — to whom is opposed *Danaeus* (lib. 1 *Demonom.* cap. 4) and in *peculiar treatise against Wier*.

Since however this question touches upon the *devil's power and guile*, and how great is the *peril in which those expose themselves who either enter into a pact with him or delight in his works*, — in a few words what in this genus is thought and in *the schools of Theologians* is more familiarly discussed I will teach.

**First** therefore is to be denied *simply*, that the devil *very often deludes the senses of men*, and their *phantasms* so directs, that they seem to themselves to be *in desired places*, — with the body meanwhile at home lying, — which body Satan covers with his shadow, — so that it is *conspicuous to no one*, — until the work — for which the *magus* is thought to have gone forth — is not perfected, — thence, with the shadow taken away, — with its own motions the body he permits to be moved. For, as *Augustine* speaks: *men of other pursuits eager, by some occult judgment of God are delivered up to be illuded and to be deceived, — after having merited by the will of Christ, — by them illuding and deceiving *prevaricators-forsakers-of-God angels*, — by whom this world according to a most-just judgment of the same holy Trinity is administered* (lib. 5 *De Trinitate*, cap. 8).

Yet, so that we say this always to be done through *illusion*, no reason compels us. In the *second place* therefore we say: — the devil *without doubt of his own magi souls only exports* to places where the *magi* have their *conventicles*, — with bodies meanwhile without sense and motion and reason left, — whence returning to themselves they narrate marvelous things which elsewhere they have seen and done, — which afterwards were found to be true. And this *raptus* of the devil the *Doctors* call *ecstasy* or *melancholic sleep*, in which the forces of the soul are so *buried*, that the man *seems dead*, — by which mode *Silvester Girardus* (as he himself boasted) when he wished — through *ecstasy without his body was raptured*, — so that the body remained *without a movable-nerve*. And *Bodinus* in the place cited brings forth examples of *sagas*, whom in this mode Satan carried into distant places, whence with *great pain* they returned, — and sometimes brought back needles, knives, letters, — and this is done to those who *fear lest they be discovered*, — thus by leaving the body at home from the conventions of the adepts *they can excuse themselves*.

Lest anyone this with *Baptista Porta* (in *lib. De magia naturali*) *narcotic and soporiferous potions attribute*, — we must know that *not all magi* use such potions, — and those who use them *usually never wake up*, — sometimes three or four days they always sleep, and *remember nothing*. But the magi through *ecstasy without body raptured* often return after four or five hours, and what things have been done in their *conventicles* elsewhere-in-place they can *recite*, — persons also with whom they have conversed, — even not before seen.

Add that magi through *ecstasy raptured feel no cruciates in the body*, — of scourges of the sky, of fires subjected to those *parts which most avail sense* — perceive nothing at all — nor awake, until the soul returns to the body, — which certainly does not happen in *sleepers*, who even by lightest torment adhibited, from pain *awaken*.

This *ecstasy Augustine* could not deny. For (lib. 18 *De civ. Dei*, cap. 18) he writes of the father of *Praestantius* — that *turned again into a horse — meat into camps* — that his own commeatum in camps with other beasts of burden he had borne, — with his body meanwhile at home lying. It is manifest therefore from what has been said that the devil through *ecstasy* the souls of his ministers exports to distant places, — with the body at home *quasi-dead lying*.

**Third** it is not to be denied that the devil sometimes *the very bodies of his own slaves* to places distant *bears*. That he can do this from thence it is certain, that the *good angels* at the command of God do this. *Philip the Apostle* by the *Spirit of the Lord* was raptured and translated to *Azotus* (Acts 8:39, 40). Similarly *Prophets* by the Spirit are translated *even to Babylon to Daniel*, as in the *Apocryphal Daniel*. If this the good angels could do, rightly we gather that neither is it *impossible for evil angels*, who indeed are with them of the same *nature and potency*: — and what those by God's *jussus* do, these by his same *permission* can do.

Nay in *Christ the Savior* himself the devil for his own impudence *tried to prove his own potency*. For to him permitting into the *pinnacle of the temple* he transferred his body, — not leading by degrees, but suddenly snatching, — into the *pinna templi* he *stood him*, is read (Matt 4). Whence some collect, that given *possibility* in one, — by consequence it is given in all others, — which are of the same weight and magnitude. And of *Augustine* is the sentence: — that to *angelic nature and spirits* it is not contrary, — that *bodies*, — whither God permits, — they may bear (lib. 3 *De Trinitate*, cap. 8).

That however what in this genus *Satan* can do, he even has done, — testify examples ancient and more recent. Among ancient is memorable what near *Philostratus* is read: — *Apollonius Tyaneus* under *Nero* was in *Ethiopia*, — in a brief space he was *transported to Rome*, thence to *Corinth*, *Smyrna*, *Ephesus*.

*More recent examples* in number are more, — partly because *sagae* have confessed themselves to have been in *conventicles of their complices*, which not through illusion was done, — marvelous *effects* have they proved to be; — partly because *waking from sleep* by *incantation* they had adjoined *ointments* — and *pertinaciously certain matrons* to their homes accompanied, — and to *choirs* they went, — where by chance in the meantime *awoke*, — whom their spouses *thought them to be there* — as noted *by exempla probable* is *Remigius* (lib. 1 *De demonolatria*, cap. 12); — partly also that these *exportations* neither by ointments nor by ecstasy but *truly in body* they have experienced, — for having taken up the ointment for this purpose prepared, — and pronouncing certain words, — they too suddenly *in that place, where the magi* their *conventicles hold*, without themselves *were found there*, — whence with *God's help invoked* — and with the *coetus of demons dissipated* — *naked to themselves they returned*, — and not without peril and difficulty through a long space of journey they returned to their own, — of the sort of examples from probable authors many are adduced by *Bodinus* (lib. 2 *De demon.* cap. 4).

**Fourth** it must be noted for what causes the devil *transports his slaves to conventicles*, which they call *sabbaths*. **(1)** To *restore in-integrum pact* with him. For just as the devil is *ape of God* in other things, so also in this genus he *imitates God*. Just as therefore God renews the covenant entered with us in baptism as often as we use the Sacrament of the Supper, — so also Satan in these *sabbaths of the magi* does, that those who once dedicated themselves to him — with a great multitude of those serving him around them being seen — the more constantly in his ministry may persevere, — in which so wondrous *contentibus* Satan in the form of a *goat* appears, or in that of a *homini mortuus* — indeed but *magnifice* attired, — before whom prostrating themselves they renounce God, and *osculate the pudenda of the goat*, — and to perpetrating many innumerable evils are bound. In witness and sign of the *diabolic grace* — with a most-lavish banquet received by the demons — that day with great hilarity they pass.

**(2)** That from the devil they receive *renewed power of harming*. For Satan after departure with horrible voice thunders: *ye shall harm, or ye shall die within a year*. And this is done thrice in the year, — with the imitation of the *sacred divine offices*, to which male-lambs are compelled to gather three times a year, by the force of the divine law (Deut 16:16).

**(3)** That in the convention *magi* the *reports of their evil-doings* to the devil render — what they have done, — are exacted. Here he expects effects — from him to have inflicted or that tree, — that nothing has done — often approaches to the plant of the feet is despised by all others.

In these conventions also *criminal parents dedicate their children to demons*, — and that into the *infelicity of the same* — the demon receive them, — beseech, — as *Bodinus* refers about a certain saga, — whom her daughter had accused, — that *she in the conventions had led her mother, and to the devil for scourging had handed her over*.

**(4)** By these conventions the *disciples of the devil are edified*, — so that with alacrity they serve the devil. Just as *David* with singing and dancing preceded the ark of the Lord, when he was leading it back to the house of the Lord, — and the *Hebrew women* — with their choruses accompanying at the altar sang, — so the magi *saltations* institute in those *conventions*, — that they attest that they *studiously and alacritously the cult to the devil render*.

These things about the *raptus of magi to their so-called sabbaths* or *conventicles* it has pleased to annotate, — that this genus of men we more vehemently detest, — who to the beck of the devil rather than to God the Creator and Savior wish to live, — which to believe is better than to experience, — or a matter sufficiently proven into doubt to call.

**Casus VIII. Whether magi by their art can transform men into beasts?**

*Reply.* Even this question is not lacking in *difficulty*; in whose explication caution is necessary, lest against the *piety* which we owe to God and neighbor be committed.

Always have the *erudite* on this matter gone into diverse sentences, — both among Ethnics, and among Christians.

Among Ethnics not a few *believed the magi with certain adhibited words and herbs can transform men into beasts*, — never however were any of the *beasts converted into man* they said, — thus *Virgil* writes:

*By these herbs I gave venoms deliberately picked out from Pontus, —
That I have seen — most often the wolf-flesh transformed with herbs.*

Of the same *sentence* are *Pomponius Mela*, *Solinus*, *Strabo*, *Varro*, — examples they add — *Herodotus*, *Homer*, *Petronius*, *Ovid*.

Of *Ammonius* the Philosopher it is read that *an ass ordinarily attended his lectures*, — whom they think to have been a man transformed into an ass, — with the *rational soul* left in him. But *Pliny* laughs at the *credulity of men*. For when from *Everathus* the *Greek writer* and from *Coppas* he had recounted, — what he had written of the *Arcadians*, who traversing a certain lake of that region *were transfigured into wolves*, — he refers however to a *fable*. Thus he writes (lib. 8 *nat. hist.* cap. 34): *men into wolves to be turned, again to their state to be restored, — that it is false we should confidently think*, — either believe all things which have been *fabulous through so many ages* we know. And again: *marvelous is how far Greek credulity proceeds; no lie is so impudent that it lacks a witness*.

Among more recent on this question *among themselves duel*, chiefly *Bodinus* and *Wier*, — of whom the former (lib. 2 *De demonom.* cap. 6) *affirms* — men by magic art are transformed into beasts, — chiefly wolves, cats, asses; — the latter however denies these *metamorphoses* (lib. 6 *De praestig. daemon.* cap. 10) — and whatever there is of this, — that it is *phantasmatic* — he says.

*Bodinus* has for himself patrons — and in these *Olaus Magnus*, *Paracelsum*, *and Militaes*: *Wier* also his — very many Theologians as well as physicians.

*Bodinus* whatever *mutation of men* — even that which the *word of Christ* signifies — *how by way of assumption*, — *true* to *be affirms*, — with the changed at least *external figure* and *sensitive soul*, — with the *rational soul remaining*, — done to be teaches, — and *ancient and new authors*, whoever wrote against, *by number* to *confirm all* — confidently writes. So he thinks *Nebuchadnezzar was truly changed into an ox*, — for *seven years* to have eaten *hay after the manner of an ox*. What *Ovid* (De Lycaone) writes as into a wolf changed, *not incredible* he says:

*Terrified himself he flees, and — the deserted rural stillness having gained — the woodland places — new himself he uttered — into a wolf.*

*Examples* also *more recent* he adduces, — *how in Livonia men are converted into wolves*: — *annotates* however toward the end of *December some nebulones* to be there, — who by magic-tools they excite, — that in the place said the arriving-thither might arrive, — and if they be found — by the devil with blows of an iron rod they are urged — so that on all sides they *drive* into a river, — and by that traversing they are *changed into wolves*, — upon men and cattle they fly, — and *innumerable damages import*. After twelve days in the same *river* swimming, they receive human form.

From the *libro of Fincelius* he adduces *Wolfshirtus* to have been discovered, — to whom the wolf-feet had been stripped off, — and immediately with hands and feet *of a truncated wolf* to die.

Of *Gemerio Lucanus* also is written, that *transformed into a wolf* he carried off *a girl of 12 years*, killed her, and devoured the flesh of her thighs and arms.

More of this genus are held near other authors — of whose some also *Bodinus* in the place cited recites. And *Augustine* (lib. 18 *De civ. Dei*, cap. 18) writes: *in a certain region of Italy it was said there were some tavern-women very evil-having, — who by cheeses tempered gave to what travelers they wished, — into whom in the manner of *jumentum* immediately they were turned, — and *necessary things* would carry, — after through *evil-fatigued labors* they had returned, — into their own again would return, — nor yet in the mind bestial-be, but rational and human they remained*.

But *Augustine* himself doubts, whether *true things they are or feigned*, saying: — *either* — *so unusual are those things, that they are worthy not to be believed*.

Certain is that the devil neither *any new creature can create, nor one thing change into another*: — this indeed is of *divine potency alone*.

*Yet* it must be thought, — says *Augustine* — *that these transgressor Angels* — *to the nod serve* — *of the visible-here matter of things*, — *but at the will of God alone*.

For as to what is *objected* about the *rods of the Egyptian magi* converted into serpents, — this is vainly explained: — of all however the safest is with the same *Augustine* to *believe*, — not truly to have been made *change of one creature into another*, — but *true frogs and serpents by the magi produced* to have been produced, — but *from occult of frogs and serpents seeds*, — (lib. 3 *De Trinitate*, cap. 7).

*Transformations therefore in Lycanthropia — what certain thing shall we hold?* — According to *Chrysostom*, transformations of things are not of one genus. Some are *plainly fabulous* and fictions of *poets*, — in which not so much to that which is said to have been done, as to *moralia* which thence are deduced is to be noted. Of which genus is the *transformation of the companions of Ulysses into satyrs*, — whom by *Circe* — of whose insane loves they desired, — into swine, — is said to have converted. *Augustine* — neither denies the fact nor simulates, — but the *transformation* — as if by *appearance done* to be — he writes: — to the same class I refer the *lycanthropia of men in Arcadia*.

*Chrysostom* about the *companions of Ulysses* — *that not the body was changed*, — he insinuates, — but *reason alone was abjected*, — and *made brutish*. *So it may be, — the malefic Circe thus with brute pleasures the companions Ulysseans satiated as if they were swine*.

Some are *truly done — not save by omnipotent God's virtue*, — either for the declaration of his *justice*, in punishing crimes, — or for showing the omnipotent goodness of *God* to men, — such is the *conversion of Lot's wife into a pillar of salt*, of *Moses' rod into a serpent*, of *water into wine at the nuptials of Cana*.

Some are *physical*, — as the *mutation of caterpillars into butterflies*, — the mutation of green-caterpillars into wasps, — of which from *Pliny* treats *Bodinus historian* (annal. cap. 15).

Finally are *magical transformations* — in which in no wise one creature is turned into another, — for this potency is neither *proper to the devil*, — nor by God to him permitted, — but reserved solely to *his divine virtue*, — just as the force of producing creatures from *nothing*, — which even distinguishes the devil from the divine *genius* (Jer 10).

*Magical transformation happens*:

**(1)** *By suppression of things* — one seems changed into another. Thus of the *companions of Diomedes* is written (lib. 4 *metamorph. Ovidii*), that *into birds they had been changed*, — because *Venus and Mars* had been wounded at *Troy by Diomedes*. But *Virgil* writes (lib. 2 *Georgic.*), that these birds ran to meet Greek ships in flight — mindful of their genus, — but to barbarians hostile, — because *Diomedes was killed by Illyrian pirates*. In the same place he writes, that these birds by *Greeks are called ianis*, — while *Ovid* — *aut a herondia* — turns into a stork, — *Solinus* — Ciconiam thinks to be, — or similar to it. Of that *transformation of the companions of Diomedes* thus writes *Augustine*: *the birds are said to be Diomedes, which as if a bird's kind by his companions his prophane pages demonstrate*, — *not from those men to have been made, — but subrogated in place-of-them by pretense-so-happens to have been supplied — just as a hind for Iphigenia daughter of Agamemnon king*. This deceit however was not for angel-difficulties: *since even the girl afterwards live has been found — subrogated for-her a hind to have been*, — is easily known. *Companions* however of *Diomedes*, — *because they suddenly did not appear* — *by the vengeance of angels rendered destruction-suffered had been*, — *to have been converted*, — believed to have been *into those birds*, — since for them from other places occultly, where is this kind of birds, that place has been produced, and suddenly *substituted are they believed to be converted*. *But that they bring the darts to the temple of Diomedes with the beak, and sprinkle*, — that *fondle Greek-birthed*, — *the foreign-birthed persecute*, — is not to be wondered at, done by demons' instigation, — *of whose interest is to persuade — God to have been made — of Diomedes, — that Deus he be through many pieties* — *deceived in his own — from divine cult*, — *to false gods honor* to the crown, etc.

**(2)** *Magical transformation happens by fascination and deception* [of the eyes]: — just as when the devil in *goat-form* appears, or in a species of a *dead man* — but *magnifice* — before whom they prostrate, and pretend to reverence.

Nothing prevents us from saying the same of *lycanthropes*, or of those who *say themselves changed into beasts*, — where nothing has changed *Satan through magi*, but the eyes of others he has *fascinated*, — so that they think the man has been changed into a wolf or an ass, — even the man himself who suffers such things, — thus with the *phantasy troubled*, — so that in the woods he runs around and thinks himself to be a beast, — men and cattle he can devour, — who yet at home is *elevated by deep sleep* — laid down.

Of this certainly is the sentence of *Augustine* (lib. 18 *De civ. Dei*, cap. 18), whom many Theologians follow.

Whether *ecstasin* he keeps to be, — the mind in a sound body — always by the Word preserves us, — with a docile and obsequent soul let him grant, — lest of the devil's *sport* and of others' *offense* we become.

**Casus IX. Whether *sagae* by their art can move *thunderstorms, hail, and other tempests*, and inflict diseases and calamities on others?**

*Reply.* General is the aphorism of the *Prophet Amos* (3:6): *there is no evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done*.

Since therefore even *tempests* are *penalties of evils*, whereby the sins of men are punished, — before all things we must look to *God*, who has *all elements in his power*, and rules them by his will.

For which cause Scripture, as often as it treats of tempests, makes *God the author of them*. *Job* himself made the *way of hail*, and the paths of sounding thunder (Job 28:26); *at his voice* he gives *a multitude of waters of heaven* (Jer 10:13); he gives a most-vehement course to the *thunder*, and a *way to the sounding thunders*; *he sends lightnings*, and they go: — *Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go and say unto thee, Here we are?* (Job 38:35).

When of *Moses in Egypt* the plague of hail he sent, — from God command was that he stretch out his hand over all Egypt on men and beasts, and provoked hail (Exod 9:22).

This work God so *reserved to his own power*, that not even the devil in this genus anything can according to his own whim, — much less men, — the physical mode of acting you consider, which depends on the law of nature, — since neither the devil, nor any woman, — or any other minister of Satan, has the faculty of *constituting the elements*, — nor the words which he pronounces, nor the herbs which he cooks, have that force of producing so great *effects*, whereby suddenly damage is done to fruits and animals. For production of hail, of lightning, and of similar tempests is a *species of creation*, which is owed to *God alone*.

Therefore to *Job* God says: *Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?* (Job 38:28–29). Before, however, in v. 22, he had said, *that he prepared the treasures of snow and hail*.

Even if therefore the devil's zeal to harm men entirely inclines, — himself even by himself is *cunning* and *astute* enough, — nor of potency of matter, — which even in *commotion of the elements he sometimes exerts*, — whence *prince of the air* he is called (Eph 2:2), — not as if he had *condit-air*, — or *inhabits the air*, — but since he *moves and disturbs the air*, — and in it *meteors of that kind for time produces*, — is he *deprived*, — yet he cannot for his own *whim* — otherwise long ago we would have all perished, — but has *potency limited by the will and nod of God*, — without which not even a *needle* [may he produce], — nor swine may he harm, — as from the history of *Pharaoh* is compact (Exod 8:18), — from the Evangelium *Matthew* (cap. 8, v. 31), — chiefly however the *history of Job* offers a most-illustrious example of this thing (Job 1 and 2).

Uses however God *sometimes the malignant spirit as if his executioner* — in punishing the sins of men. Therefore when in the *history of Job* fire from heaven was sent, and a *most vehement wind rushed on his house*, and swept away his sons, — is said the *tempest-of-God, and turnings-of-fires*, — although through *evil angels* is done, — has the term *Almighty-of-God*. Thus, when God the fruits of the *Egyptians* with rust, — and the vineyards with hail struck, — that this was done through evil angels is said in Ps 105:17.

*Power therefore having received from God, Satan is most-prompt to be secured, — thus however, that no tempest, without pre-existing some matter, — he may produce, — but vapors into the air with much celerity gathers, — and from natural causes* (only in *preternatural mode* and in *unaccustomed time*) — *lightning, hail, and similar things*, — whereby it is possible to *harm the fruits*, — as *most-skilled physicist* produces.

To *the consortium of his own works* he readily *admits and adds his pious* — those *sagae and lamias*, whom he bids to cook herbs, to write certain characters, to pour water into a pit dug by them, — to use certain words and gestures, — although *from natural causes*, though *in preternatural mode produced* — already immediately-to-approach the tempest he sees, — so that the miserable *sagae* think it done *by their art*.

*Not to Satan alone* however we should refer this thing, — but since *permission* he has from God to harm men, — he uses *his ministers*, — chiefly *sinergists*, — not only in *inciting tempests*, — but even in procuring *sterility, diseases, and other noxious things*, — which among other things thence is compact, — that with the *sagas removed*, suddenly cease those *harmful effects*, — which *Bodinus* teaches by *some examples*, in the appendix of the *Book of Demonomania against Wier*, — that not therefore *sagas alone*, — but also the devil, this-thing does.

Prompt indeed are *improbable men — organs of Satan* — to this thing, — since by that reason they *take occasion for vindicating themselves against their enemies*, — than which nothing they have *dearer*, — whereby also in this business they are also *satisfying-service to the devil*, whom they cult, — who in his conventions declares to them: *ye shall harm, or ye shall die*.

Even from *Imperial Constitutions* it is compact that *sagas by magical arts disturb the elements*, — the life of infants weakens, and *with naked hands they dare to fan*, — that with which each may confect his enemies: — for which cause capital-penalty he decrees, — and by *L. multi tam. cur*, caution has been added, — *him who by incantation shall make void the crops of another, — as guilty of poisonings — as if it were reasonable that these could do this*.

*Augustine* also (in Ps 42) writes that *elements by permission of God can be shaken by magi*. For what they themselves *do — do not — that with the aid of the Devil — with God permitting they effect*.

It must be noted however, that the devil *often supplies such media to his ministers as are not apt for producing an effect*. *Bodinus* refers (lib. 2 *De daemonom.* cap. 8) among *Iaskonians* and *Piolosants* to have been the custom of *dragging crucifixes and images to a river*, for impetrating rain.

[*That certain crucifix boys of Thok-fani* — *lignum tremp aut per aquam trahentes-massam*.]

Thus *sagae* often kill cattle with *powders laid under the threshold*, — which force these powders cannot have, — else other-things primarily to sagas, — who bear them, would be killed, — but this is the *work of the devil*, who can harm in a thousand modes, when God has permitted him. Thus with the *powder of toads* — either *nude foot* or *touched with hand* — *saga is said to have inflicted abortion or death*, — which cannot happen by these means: — but the devil persuades them, — so that man he compels to serve even foulest animals.

They *baptize* those *toads*, names they impose on them, and *consecrated host* — they procure to be handed to them. Thus Satan subjects his cultors even to *most-noxious beasts*, with a horrid abuse of sacred things, — that at last all *religion and reverence of the divine numinis* he may root out of their souls.

Nor however do those *media* which by *sagae* are adhibited *of themselves harm*, — but *the sagae prayers stirred Satan* himself does this, with GOD permitting, — persuading afterward the *sagae* that of medicine so great was the efficacy, — only, so that in the *superstition and devotion which they are devoted, they may be preserved*.

**Casus X. Whether *sagae* can steal *milk* from the *udders* of humans and of cattle?**

*Reply.* On this thing easily judgment can be made from the preceding. *God is he who guards men and beasts, and blesses their udders*. But when the devil is permitted the power of harming, he can steal not only milk, but also gold and silver, fruits from the field, and other goods of a neighbor.

And here again he uses the *labor of his ministers*, not as if he needed it, or they of themselves could effect anything of these things, — but so that in *devotion* he may retain them. For even if none of the sagae by the devil's help has ever been enriched, — yet he promises them the goods of a neighbor, or at least persuades the *vengeful old-women* that by *subtraction of others' things* they can *vindicate themselves against those whose things they were*. Therefore Satan bids to *adhibit various media* — with knives, nails, or with *scissors*, distaff, and similar instruments, he bids to *emulct milk*, — whence also it seems to flow: but it is *delusion of the devil*.

Assumption from these instruments does not follow: rather elsewhere the devil, whom the *sagae imbibe*, from a cow or hen — with marvelous celerity substitutes, — meanwhile the old-woman is *left in her opinion*, as if she herself had *emulcted*.

Sometimes also not so much in cows, but even in *nurses* Satan the *receptacles and canals of milk* can *impede*, — no otherwise than in *spouses*, with the Lord permitting, he impedes the *natural congress*, — where the *instruments* which by his ministers are adhibited, — have no faculty of producing this sort of *effect*, — the devil however *truly using them, deludes his ministers*, — so that they *think it done by their art*.

Thus *Bodinus* in the *Appendix of the book De demonomania contra Wier* mentions a certain woman of *Bibrac*, — who threatened a certain *woman lactating* — that she would never lack milk, — which even was done, — having drunk the milk the woman dried up, and although she bore many children, her breasts however always dried up; — but when the *saga was burned*, her milk continually abounded. Thus the devil truly harms in cows, — and yet before the *senses of his ministers* their *prestiges* *he sets*.

Therefore in vain it is that *sagas* expect *great riches from the devil*. He *rather ruins* what others *natural is* by lies, that they may serve his ministers.

**Casus XI. How by the devil through *sagae* — against magi — sinful — inflicted mala — with what remedies may be resisted?**

*Reply.* By many modes for our destruction is Satan intent, — and, if God has permitted him, he does much harm. With *unusual tempests* he kills the crops, sends diseases, induces *sterility on spouses*, *fascinates infants*, infests dwellings, — so that no one can safely inhabit them, — with milk of cattle, — with wealth *robs men*, etc. To all of which — to him and to his organs — is licit to resist, — provided in a licit mode.

Many men however in this part *fail*, — since not lawful is-it, — to use *media*, whereby indeed evil from body and from fortunes they drive off, — but *peril* to constituted-conscience and to soul they attract. There are indeed those who wish to *cure like by like*, — that is, *evils inflicted by sortileges or magic arts* they wish to *lift by similar arts*: in which genus much avails *Papistic superstition*, which to *consecrated creatures ascribes some marvelous force against the power of Satan*: — against hail and tempests they hurl *hail-stones from a hail-heap into the fire with invocation of the most-holy Trinity*; — with the *Lord's Prayer* and the *angelic salutation* they recite these three times, — the *fasting of St John the Baptist* they undertake, — and adjoin *the sign of the cross everywhere against the tempest, before and behind and on every part of the earth*, they inter, — diseases they cure with *sortilegial charms, with herbs and with words, with ligatures and characters*, — *fecundity of spouses lost by sortileges some superstitiously wish to repair — by nuptials repeated with prior ceremonies*, — some ridiculously suspend a *wax-image of virile member on the altar of the Mass*, — some also *impious by certain characters written on virginal paper*, over which is read seven times *Ps 104: snatch me from an unjust enemy*, — and bind that *paper to the man's thigh* [against magical impotence]; — for impeding *fascination* they hang a *squill above the doorpost*; — in *infested* dwellings they inquire in the *thresholds of doors — wax images, seeds, bones*, which by chance sagae have applied, — and with these removed, — the *houses no longer infested* they think; — for lost milk of cows by sortilege, cows *in the name of a thousand devils they bid to go out and return with milk*; — others use other *remedies*, which here to recite is not needed.

Nor lacking are those who through *cribration and other magical media magi* discover, — which some think can be done without sin, — since by another reason those malicious men cannot be detected. Similar *antidotes*, if not plainly magical, yet ridiculous and superstitious, see near *Pliny* (lib. 28 *nat. hist.* cap. 12, lib. 27, and elsewhere), — always there have been those who used the *works of demons against demons and their organs' evil-doings*, — which is not to be wondered at, — since it is *pleasing to Satan*, either in this mode, — *under species of some magic to draw* into his service — those whom by *cupidity of harming* others he could not enslave.

But this is wondrous — that is found among *Christians* who this *medium of driving-out the devil approves and commends*. Among these is *Scotus*, who (lib. 4 dist. 34) writes: *superstitions there are, if anyone shall state — that no maleficium by superstition is to be dispelled*. *Christian emperors* also by their laws punish *magi and venefici*, — but those who use *incantations and venefices* against *rains, winds, and hail*, — them not only they do not punish, but also *with rewards adorn*, as *L. eorum C. De maleficis*.

*Yet however to Christians* all *arts of demons* rightly should be suspect, — and it should be *certainly held* — whatever is *magical*, this is *adverse to God*, and *alien from true piety*, — even if some great commodity thence should come.

**(1)** Certain is the *Apostolic axiom* — *evils are not to be done, that good may come* (Rom 3:8), — which the more true it is, the greater execration deserves, — because *Nicholas I Pope conceded to a certain bishop* — that he might use the *labor of the saga for recovering his health*, — with this clause added to the dispensation, that *of two evils the lesser might be chosen*, as *Jacobus Sprangerus refers Bodinus* (lib. 3 *De daemonom.* cap. 5).

**(2)** *Certain is that they serve the devil*, who use *diabolic arts for driving off evils whatever*, — for having abjected *confidence in God*, they trust *to obtain aid from the devil*. For which cause also *unlawful it is judged*, — to *inquire in the thresholds of doors — seeds, bones, wax images*, and *similar nugae*, which *magi are thought to have applied* for killing men and cattle. For those who with these things removed *think Satan to cease*, — by that very fact to these things *forces of harming* (which however they do not have) they attribute, — and *God passed over*, — from whom alone death or diseases are sent, — to *diabolic organs they seek aid*. Therefore *Hilarion*, when Satan spoke in a possessed girl, — and said he would not go out, unless the *brass image* which the girl's mother had subjected to the door were removed, — he was *unwilling to do this*, — but by *prayers* he freed the girl, — as is near *Hieronymus* (in *Vita Hilarionis*).

**(3)** Certain is this also, — and by the word of God proved, — that *no power on earth can resist the forces of Satan*: — this indeed *God to Job* attests (cap. 41), — under the name of *Leviathan*, — that is, of the *devil*. What therefore should *pulveres, characters, words, or prayers of miserable little old women* accomplish? Hence experience has proved, that the *devil by these arts assailed cedes indeed, but not always*, — sometimes when by *his flight he can procure some greater evil*. Nor ever *benefit-does he to men*, but where more he may harm. He *removes sortilege from a horse*, and puts it on a servant; he *removes disease from a young man*, transfers it into a wife, and casts it on the husband; *he takes disease from a king's minister*, and *sends it on the king's son*; *body he restores to health*, and *meanwhile perishes the soul*, — as all by examples he has proven (Bodinus lib. 3 *De demon.* cap. 2).

**(4)** *This also is compact*, — that *magi and sagae* can remove by their art *only that disease or evil* which was inflicted by themselves, — not every one, nor always: — it is necessary however *something be at hand*, to which the disease or evil they may transfer, — otherwise the evil *falls back on themselves*, — and *diseases arising from natural causes they cannot cure*. Even if therefore it were licit to use the *works of sagae* in curing diseases (which however no pious has said) — no one however could do this, — unless certainly he knew, *the disease to be from sortilege*.

**(5)** *Diseases inflicted by magi* are not cured with natural things, — mostly in this cure is adhibited the *venomous brain of a cat*, *head of a raven*, and similar thing, from which nature *abhors*: — or words are adhibited, whereby is *abused* the *most-sacred name of the holy Trinity*, — or even in the *name of the devil* the *evil* is *propelled*, — whatever however of names *divine is abused*, or *nominally of names diabolic is used, — is impious and blasphemous*.

**(6)** Compact is from *sacred letters* that *God abominates those who consult magi in whatever matter*: *the soul which shall have declined to magi and ariolos, and shall have fornicated with them, — I will set my face against her, — I will cut her off from the midst of my people*, says the *Lord* (Lev 20:6). Therefore *Ahaziah* king of Israel perished, since having despised the true God in his infirmity he *consulted Baalzebub the god of Ekron* (2 Kgs 1:6); — and against *Manasseh* and his people the *Lord was greatly angry*, since he *tolerated the magi* (2 Kgs 17 and 21). *Saul* however, that he might avert from his people the penalties of *consulters of magi* dictated in the law, — *all magi and ariolos he took away from the earth*, and *slew those who had pythons in the belly* (1 Sam 28).

**(7)** *Even Ethnics abhor from this mode of curing diseases and averting other evils*. *Roman Emperors* still alien from the *faith of Christ* have taken *palm* in this genus over many Christians, — while by *hatred of the magical arts, with capital punishment they afflicted those who exposed a fugitive-thief by magical arts, — nor would they suffer faith to be given to such arts*, — as is in *L. sicut leg. Labeonem § si quis, — dolegus, injuriis ff.*; and *Hippocrates* (in his book *De morbo sacro*): *worthy of hate are those who deceive themselves — the comitial disease will cure — by the power of the demons, — whom he himself calls *nebulones*, — and *audibly separates* those *most-wicked purges*, — *once free*, they extol themselves. — *Also the Fathers detest these arts*: *sagas they abhor, and their aid to their health they do not use*. *Better it is*, says *Chrysostom* (hom. 8 *in epist. ad Coloss.*), *for a Christian man to undergo death, than to buy life by ligatures*. *Augustine* (lib. 10 *De civ. Dei*, cap. 10): *all remedies and amulets against diseases he prohibits*, — beside *prayer* and *penitence and medicine* — *whatever in words, characters, ligatures, and other vain things* placed — *he calls nets of Satan*. And in the book *De doctr. Christ.* he writes: *to this genus pertain the ligatures of execrable remedies*, — *either vows*, — *or whatever other things* — *to be suspended and bound*, — with which, when *faith is adhibited*, *illicit is idolatry*. Similar things has *Basil* (in Ps 45); whose sentence *Thomas Aquinas* followed (in lib. 2 *sent.* dist. 7): *to idolatry and apostasy he transmits* — if one uses *the aid of devils and magi* — for *impeding or expelling evil-doings*.

*Constantine* the *Emperor* believed indeed that by *magical arts* aid could be adhibited, — lest for the maturing vineyards rains or winds should be feared, — and by *hail-lapidation* they should be corrupted. But afterwards, as *Theodoret* (hist. 2) noted, punished were those who *made such magic*, — even if for the sake of *obtaining any good of another*, — and on account of *fecundity of fruits it be perfected*.

*By so many reasons* therefore we judge *impious and abominable in the eyes of God*, — either *tempests, or diseases, or any other evils*, — to expel by the *aid of malefices*, — since any Christian from the *sacred code* should be taught, — that *health and disease, goods and evils, are from God*, — whose same *hand* can *both wound and heal*, — from whom alone is *all our aid*, — which who *does not patiently expect from him*, — has *denied the faith*. There are however some other things whereby against the *malice of Satan* and of his *organs* we can best consult, — of which I will add a few.

**Firstly** — let us not *easily believe* that either *tempest*, or *diseases*, or other *calamities of ours* are from magi. The pious know that in the hands of God are our lots, — who tempers the affairs of all men, — as Scripture testifies, — *health, life, death, and diseases are from God* (Sir 11:14).

That if greatly *magi* have done something, — we know however that they *are not the power on earth which can resist the strengths of Satan*, — much more of God, — *without whose permission* they can do nothing. Therefore let us not care for the devil or the saga, — nothing let us reckon of their aid, — but wholly hang on God with serious penitence, praying that *he may crush Satan under our feet*. For no more efficacious *armor is there against the devil, than prayers poured out from a contrite heart*.

**(2)** *Let there be frequent in our mouth the name of Jesus*, — which alone with true *fiducia of soul pronounced*, many works of the magi have been *impeded*, — so that even *devils* have been *cast out of the possessed at this name* (Matt 6, etc.).

**(3)** Let there be *assiduous reading and meditation of the divine word*, which the devil cannot bear, — who *at the praises of God and mention of divine works shudders*; whence let us make the *word* and the *workshops of piety*, — and accustom us and our family to prayers and study of piety, — and not permit frequent *mention of the devil*: — for there are not lacking examples that the *devil has carried off alive those from whom he was invoked*, — which see near *Bodinus* (lib. 3 *De daemonom.* cap. 3, p. 415). *True is the German adage*: *the devil is not to be painted on a wall, — for by himself he comes*.

**(4)** *Let us have firm faith in God as our unconquered fortress* to which we confide. He is *stronger than the devil and all magi*, — to whom he sets *limits*, which by all their *art and astuteness* they cannot pass. Whence experience testifies, — that magi cannot harm all, — but only those against whom God permits them power, — either to *chastise for sins*, or to explore, — after however he has *found them in faith and patience*, — with his blessings he later *augments them*, — which the *example of Job* teaches.

**(5)** *If our homes and the beasts and men that are in them, from-injuries of the devil are to be safe, we must supplicate — of them without God's permission nothing can they do*. Therefore let us not care for the devil or the saga, — nothing let us do about their help, — but wholly let us hang on God with serious penitence — praying, that *he himself may bruise Satan under our feet*. No armor is more efficacious against the devil than *prayer poured out from a contrite heart*.

**(6)** *In the name of Jesus, — with true soul-fiducia pronounced*, — the works of the magi have been *impeded*, — even devils from the possessed have been *cast out at this name*.

**(7)** *The devil is not to be too much feared, or his organs*, — nor should anything happen for their sake. For above we heard, that the *devil is a most-proud spirit*, — who cannot more easily be put to flight than by *contempt*, which arises from *true faith in God*. Injurious he is against *God himself*, who fears the devil and his ministers. Therefore in the *law* the Lord cautions, that from the *gods of the gentiles* (which are demons) we should not fear, — who neither with good nor with evil can affect. Thus *Gregory* inhibited by contempt of the devil a great spirit from infested things.

By *six modes* thus, the *diabolic works of sagae* are most-happily resisted, — and evils by *divine permission* imminent, — with unharmed conscience either *tolerated* or *overcome*.

**Casus XII. Whether *magical books*, and those in which the arts of sagae are taught, should be handed over to *Vulcan* (fire)?**

*Reply.* *Nothing is more pernicious than a book*, says *Erasmus*. There are indeed *dumb masters of books*, — which if they are evil, but *elegantly and methodically written*, — venom by some occult *pipe* they *instill*. As venoms *dressed with sugar* are more avidly drunk, and more difficultly guarded against, — so a book *ingenious with elegance of style*, novelty of things, and good order, *more strongly penetrates the souls of men* — nature-eager of novelty. This especially of *magical books* and those teaching *sortilege* is *true*.

Therefore to all *good men* it has always pleased, — that as *venomous serpents* in first sight they be *bruised*, — from the hands of men, and from memory utterly, — as far as it can be done, — in whatever mode *removed*.

This is done by the example of the *primitive Church*, where at *Ephesus*, — with the Apostle *Paul preaching*, — many, who had followed *curious arts*, brought their books together, — and *burned them* (with the prices of them being computed, they found the value of *fifty thousand denarii*, Acts 19:19).

The Romans also willed *books of incantators to be burned by senatusconsult*. So *Livius* writes (lib. 39): *how often was this business given to magistrates from our fathers and grandfathers age, — that they should search out vaticinial books, — and burn them?* *Augustus Caesar* burned more than two thousand *vaticidic books written in Greek and Latin*, as *Suetonius* attests (in *Augusto*, cap. 31). *Honorius and Theodosius the Emperors* decreed *mathematical books* — that is, magical books — *to be consumed by flames under the eyes of bishops*. *Athanasius* refers (in the book *De incarnatione verbi*): *those converted to the Christian religion — impious of vanity books* — *committed to fire*. *Nicephorus* is author (lib. 10) that *Iovinianus* a certain *young man* — *by much punished by exile*, — and his goods *published*, — because he *had described a magic book*.

By so great severity of old, — animadversion was made against *the admirers of curious things*: whose example imitating we too from *reading of such books* should abstain, — and take care that they be *snatched* from the hands, chiefly of youth.

**Casus XIII. Whether magistrates should punish *sagas and magos*, — that from their own works have been described — with *lex talionis*, — that is, with fire?**

*Reply.* Acrid on this thing is the contention among learned men, — chiefly between *Bodinus*, to whom is joined *Nicolaus Remigius*, — and *Wier*, who has the *opposite parts*. That one affirms that *sagas should be afflicted with capital punishment*: this one denies. Each has his own reasons.

Even though it is not ours to *put an end to lawsuits*, — yet lest anything in this genus be done with *doubting conscience*, — what in this genus most safely may be done, — I will briefly indicate.

I presuppose however those things of which already in the preceding I have treated, — as *pre-known*, — namely, that *pact with the devil is entered by them*, — voluntary desire of harming or vindicating oneself by *illicit media* they have, — Satan's works they exercise, — by the permission of God, — in the *ruin of others*, — or at least by that they *strive to do*.

By these premisses with *Bodinus* I decide, — nothing from *piety* alien, — but rather *a work of justice done*, — those judges who take care that the *worst men of these* are removed from the midst.

**Reasons are these:**

**(1)** *God* long since has borne *sentence* on this kind of men, — namely *maleficos, pythones, sagas, and incantatores*: *Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.* (Exod 22:18); *A man also or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones: their blood shall be upon them.* (Lev 20:27). *Chartummim* is called, — which not only *venefico* notes (as *Wier* wills), — who by venoms harms others, — but all who *stir up prestigations* — just as the *Greeks call magi Iaras* (*epōdias-t-astakaris*), — with which voice the LXX interpreters use, — as above in the preamble of this chapter we have noted. *All therefore magi and sagas the divine law bids to be killed*, — whether they cast *prestiges*, or use *divinations*, or in whatever other way they *harm or wish to harm the neighbor*. And this law in the people of God was always in *green observation*, — which the example of the *pythonic wife of Endor* testifies, who *feared king Saul*, — who mindful of the divine law had *prohibited magic under a capital law* in his kingdom.

**(2)** With this divine law consents the *law of nature*, which the *wiser of the ethnics followed, subjected all who devote themselves to magical arts to the capital penalty*.
