## Chapter IX. Cases of Conscience concerning the Administration of the Lord's Supper

*De casibus conscientiae circa administrationem coenae Dominicae.*

### Preamble

The *sacrosanct use of the coena of the Lord* consists in *rite acception* and *rite distribution*.

Hence *two kinds of men* are around this sacrament busy: — first the *minister distributing*, — then *the receivers or communicants*.

**The words of the institution** — for which reason they are handled — that a *faithful minister* — with them profane-things not treat.

Concerning the *communicants* above we said (lib. 2 c. 11); — here of *ministers distributing* we act.

What therefore is fitting-to-know — around this office may fall in doubts, — in this chapter we shall see.

### Casus I. Whether the minister of the Church can with good conscience admit a *public sinner* to the sacred coena

*Reply.* If the *sins of the impenitent* are still *hidden*, — so however that no one else knows of them, — and no scandal may be moved for private persons — none is to be *kept-off from the sacred coena*: — but here the *gradus of admonitions* are to be respected.

**But if one of those sins** — not yet openly accused, — nor sufficiently confessed to the ministers or their conviction-anticipators — is to be admitted-however, — lest in prodigious care of his soul with our treasure removed, — for admonitions however, — in whatever way it can be done, — that suspicion may be alleviated. — Here indeed has place the saying of the Apostle: *offend not the Church*.

**If the sins are indeed known, but only to the pastor**, — not yet held-for-notorious, — therefore such sinners are not simply to be repulsed from the use of the sacred coena: — but if they wish to approach, — diligently by the pastor to be admonished of the peril, — and, — that seriously they repent, — to be exhorted, — with the means also by which to *true repentance* they can be led, — shown.

**If however they have not obeyed** — but have approached communicating among others, — not immediately to be repulsed, — but tolerated — because the crime is still *hidden*: — the pastor indeed knows of it, — but ought not to reveal — nor is he-to-betray the delinquent — in confession or under the *seal of confession* entrusted: — therefore in such a case he treats him deservedly as an *occult sinner*.

**But he should aggravate to him privately his delict**, — and lest a slave-of-God's-fear-he-flees — that he may open his delict *in another way*, — should admonish.

**If however some crime**, — for example, — *fornication, adultery, homicide* or similar in the Church has become publicly known, — nor from author of that is denied, — nor any signs of repentance appear, — and nevertheless that wicked-one asks to be admitted to the sacred coena: — with good conscience he cannot be admitted — for these reasons:

**(1) Because Christ in his institution never intended or willed** that *impenitents* — to what extent such they are — should be admitted to this sacrament: — because sacraments either impart or confirm faith, — which in impenitents — insofar as such they are — is not. — But no one *at a sacred action against the intention of Christ ought to do anything* — lest anything in vain and against Christ be seen to be done.

**(2) Because those only are to be admitted** — *who can prove themselves* (1 Cor 11:28) — for which cause infants also from this sacrament are excluded. — But impenitents *by no means prove themselves*, — else they would not be such: — since true probation with serious *grief for the admitted sin*, — with true faith in Christ, — and with the *purpose of emendation always conjoined* is.

**(3) It is the office of ministers of the word to beware** — lest anyone of the hearers to himself contract *judgment and eternal damnation*. — Now the Apostle Paul is a plain witness — *unworthy and impenitent sinners eat judgment to themselves*, — and of the body and blood of Christ *guilty they become*, — if to the *Lord's supper unworthily they approach* (1 Cor 11:28-29). — How therefore can they with pious admit-them, — with good conscience, — with own-office-safe? — For in this manner they would not only *confirm* the impenitent in his impiety, — but themselves would become guilty of the body and blood of Christ, — while they do not impede the impenitent sinner in his evil purpose.

**(4) General is Christ's prohibition:** *give not what is holy to dogs* (Matt 7:6) — that which is holy, — if that sacred coena is: — dogs the impious impenitents-persevering are.

**(5) Christ wills reconciliation to precede this sacred action** (Matt 5:23-24). — In impenitents however no reconciliation can precede — either with the Church or with neighbor: — how then do they seek reconciliation — who were never affected with grief-of-sin?

**(6) He who admits impenitents to the sacred coena** — is a *liar in the face of God*, — and both deceives himself and the communicant. — For the sacred coena is *confirmation of faith*, — and *absolution from sins*: — and while the minister distributes, — it is the same as if he said: *receive the pledge of forgiveness of sins* — and yet knows that sins are not forgiven to the impenitent: — announces the *grace of God* to him — who is still under wrath. — This is *lying to the Holy Spirit* — an example of which is punished in *Ananias and Sapphira* — and to the impenitent hearer whose sins are not remitted (Ezek 13:19).

**(7) The office of the minister** — is not only of *absolving*, but also of *binding*, — of the *bound-under*, — according to the power given to him (John 20:23) — and to *indicate to them the iniquities and unrighteousnesses which they commit*, — who impenitents admit to the sacred coena. — But these become *partakers of others' sins*, — and incur the punishments — which the Lord threatens them (Ezek 33:8): *when I say to the impious, impious you shall die by death, — and you have not announced it, that he may turn from his way, — the impious in his iniquity shall die, — but his blood I will require at your hand*.

**(8) Concerning impenitents Paul says** (1 Cor 5:11): *if the brother named to you is a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner, — with such an one not to eat*: — much less does he will to be admitted to the sacred coena of the Lord — because far harder is that separation from *communion of holy banquets* than the vulgar communion of the living.

**(9) In 2 Thess 3:6 the Apostle writes**: *withdraw yourselves, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not according to the tradition which they received of us*: — to walk *disorderly*, is to live *contrary to the ordinance of the divine word*. — If therefore from communion with such even in *civil conversation* every-one must abstain, — how much more the ministers of the Church of the word ought to beware — that in the *sacred communion* they admit themselves not — of which it is convenient — *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* (2 Cor 6:14).

**(10) Here accede the testimonies and examples of the saints Fathers and bishops**, — who also gravely exhorted the ministers of the Church, — that they should not admit any impious of those whom they know to be *impenitents* — to the sacred coena.

*Chrysostom* homily 83 in Matt writes — how *he who admits unworthily to the Lord's table*: (in *homil. 60 ad populum Antiochenum*, hortator of Church ministers): *no small danger, — says, — hangs over you, — if to any known to you a partaker of this sacred banquet you concede: — his blood from your hands shall be required*: — gravely inveighs into those who are angry, — that to them for their impenitence the sacred coena is denied. — Cries out, — I say — *often* — *let no one impenitent, — no one wounded, entire flesh violated approach — nor promptly of the Lord's body — with hands defiled to accept, — or with polluted mouth the Lord's blood to drink, — sacred is-known priests, — the reason of Antichrist to be committed*. — Thus far *Chrysostom*.

*Cyprian* lib. 3 epist. 14 — when indeed in time of persecution faith they had denied, — and nevertheless without penitence the sacred coena they sought, — reprehends the *priests* who administered it to them: *before undertaken penitence, — and before *exomologesis* of gravest delict done, — to give the Eucharist, — that is, — to profane the *holy body* of the Lord to dare: — since it is written: whoever eats bread, — or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily, — guilty shall be of the body and blood of the Lord*.

*Augustine* (lib. 3 contra litt. Parmen.) — him who — the impenitent — either from some grade of honor or from the communion of sacraments removes, — *with love of correcting, — not from hatred of persecuting, — most-fully-filled office not only of most-innocent, — but even of most-diligent severity has fulfilled*.

Thus *Athanasius kept Emperor Theodosius* — though otherwise pious — for the *slaughter of Thessalonica* done at the instigation of his counselors, — from *sacred communion*.

Of the same sentence also is *D. Luther* in cap. 3 Joel: *If it be manifest to the pastor* — says — *that someone lives in some impiety, — this altogether he is-bound-to-do: — that such is not to be admitted to the Eucharist, — unless they do penitence, — that is, — cease to sin, — and by true confession show, — that they *damnate and hate their sins*. Prevail — how — sinner-emendation must precede — through the *word of God*: — which if pastor does not do, — publica scandals with grave animadversion he does not press-down, — gravely sins. — If moreover he still adds this, — that he impedes ecclesiastical censure, — and *scandalizers*-patronizer becomes, — proper — from a servant of God to a slave of Satan degenerates*.

**By these causes the minister of the Church** — impenitents to the sacred coena — ought not to admit, — even if of the *world's odium*, — of the *very magistrate's* — he-would-incur: — for since *God is more to be obeyed than men* — no man's wrath ought to be so great — that its very reason our fear of God in us extinguishes, — and against duty or against our conscience anything to do or permit compels.

**Since however it can easily happen** — that the minister of the Church incautious from *precipitation of judgment* suddenly communicates with one, — of whose impenitence he was not yet exactly-certain, — therefore in the *ecclesiastical constitutions of our Electoral* it is cautioned — that such persons — whom sacraments they judge unworthy — they refer to the *Consistory*, — and this maturely, — before they seek the sacred communion, — and to its cognition the delinquent either is to be admitted or removed: — but by *proper and private daring*, — and in the very act of communion, — this is permitted to no one. — See *Constitutio Electoralis ecclesiastica in genere* Butis art. 10.

**Objection from the example of *Judas the traitor*.** — Some however defend the *admission of impenitents* to the sacred coena from the *example of Judas the traitor*, — to whom Christ, — even to himself well-conscious of that crime — the *sacrament of coena* gave. — Where it is not to be denied that *Judas* interfered in the coena-action — for the contrary is sufficiently clear from Christ's words: *But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.* (Luke 22:21). — *Augustine* (tract. 59 in John) writes — *Judas ate the bread of the Lord against the Lord*.

**We concede therefore that *Judas* was first at the coena**, — and equally as the other *Apostles*, the *body of the Lord* ate. — But this does not hinder our sentence. — For that deed of *Judas the traitor* was not yet at that time notorious. — For no one in the church knew that, — except only Christ. — The *Pontificals* and *Pharisees* indeed also knew — because with *Judas* concerning the *reward of iniquity* already they had agreed. — But nothing had this to the church: — *to the Apostles* it was unknown. — Nor *Judas* himself confessed this deed, — but still *dissimulated*: — nor simply by Christ was he admitted, — but with *previous serious admonition* — which all can most fully be applied to our case, — where the treatment is of such a wicked man, — who confesses his crime, — and by that name is known to all, — and yet asks the *sacred coena* to be given to him — lest unworthy of the name of Christian he be held.

**Such** — even if he be of great authority, — nay even the *magistrate himself* — who thinks to compel the minister of the Church, — is to be excluded from perception of the sacrament, — until he does *serious penitence*, — for the causes above indicated.

**The same reason is of those** — who *pertinaciously adhere to Papism, Calvinism* or similar errors in doctrine, — and refuse to hear better teachings, — who by this pertinacity of theirs *themselves-excluded from usurpation of sacred coena*.

### Casus II. Whether even to those who *seek the sacred coena*, — but through the vehemence of disease have lost the use of reason and every sense, — so that what is agitated with them they do not understand, — the sacred coena is to be given

*Reply.* Those who in the *ultimate agony of life* seek the sacred coena — are in *two-fold difference*. Either they are *plainly impious*, — who while they enjoyed health *contemned* the word and Sacraments, — and now dying seek the *sacred Eucharist* to be given to them only — because they fear the *ass's burial*, — if without it hence they depart. — To these — as *impenitents contemners of sacraments* — nothing is to be immediately-gratified, — much work indeed is required — that they be led to true acknowledgment of their sins and serious penitence. — These therefore, as *impenitent contemners of the sacraments*, — are to be left to the *judgment of God* — lest what is holy be given to dogs, — nor from the sacrament be made *opus operatum*, — with no distinction between worthy and unworthy.

**Some however are *holy and pious men***, — who while they enjoyed health, — diligently heard the word of God, — reverently used the sacred coena, — and lived their life *holily*, — as much as could be done in their imperfection. — And these when they are constituted in the agony — are again of two kinds: — *some so weak* — that indeed *they can hardly understand few things spoken*, — by disease also so debilitated is their memory — that little they retain of the things which with them are treated: — *only some pauci words if they emit, — by which they signify their desire for this sacred banquet*. To these help is to be given diligently, — and if even by *nod alone* they testify of their desire, — and to the things which to them are read out, — they nod, — to these the *sacred coena is not to be denied*: — for these *external gestures* are indication of *interior desire and devotion*, — in the manner in which nor to *mutes or deaf* — if by gestures they emit some testification of holy desire, — they are-denied, — as above (lib. 2 c. 11 sect. 7) we proved. — Yea if anyone yet in right of use asked, — that the *minister to him in agony* — when he can no longer *use the tongue*, — should acclaim to him *absolution*, — this is not to be *refused* — because that external desire and devotion is instead of *prolix confession*, — if especially his former *piety* and *devotion of religion* was known to all.

**Some however by disease so debilitated are**, — that neither reason nor use of external sense makes-office-anymore, — nor do they hear, nor understand, what to them is said, — nor sign of contrition or of faith emit, — nor the *host or wine received* — can retain — without peril of ejection: — to these the sacred coena cannot be given, — but either to be waited for — until they have somewhat better, — or so to be left. Concerning them the saying of Augustine is to be used: *believe, and you have eaten* — as concerning the *abstemious* above we taught (lib. 2 c. 12 tit. *Trebatur*).

**Rationes for our assertion:**

**(1) In the sacred communion must be done *commemoration of the Lord's death***, — as the Apostle teaches (1 Cor 11:26). — In such communion this cannot be done, — since the dying-one understands nothing of this.

**(2) In the sacred communion the Apostle proves that *each communicant probe himself*** — and this in such a communion is lacking. — What indeed himself does he prove, — who what with himself is done, — is *most ignorant*?

**(3) To the sacred communion we ought with *pious desire of this most-holy banquet to approach*** — in such however a communion no indication of pious desire appears, — but with a dying man, — as with a dead man is done, — not without *profanation of the sacrament*.

**(4) It is to be feared** — lest from such communion be made *opus operatum*, — as though the nude *usurpation of the sacrament* sufficed for salvation, — without the good movement of the one using — the very thing in the *Pontifical* we are wont to reprehend.

**(5) Security too it would foster in the impious** — and confirm that opinion of theirs — that it is the same, — whatever from man is believed or done, — provided all in the ultimate agony finally *most-precious partakers of this treasure* can be made.

**Wherefore each minister of the Church ought to admonish his own** — that a matter so sacred *let him not defer* to the ultimate moment of his life, — but this treasure let him gain for himself while he is yet of *entire mind*, — and with pious devotion can-sit-with the *table of the Lord*: — if however by *sudden death* they are pre-occupied, — of their salvation nothing-less — even without the *use of Eucharist* certain — since not the *privation but contempt harms*.

### Casus III. But is the sacred coena to be given to those who through *this usurpation* wish to purge themselves of *crimes*

*Reply.* This manner of purging oneself of crimes *by the celebration of the Mass* and *usurpation of coena* — the *Pontificals* invented around the year of Christ 868. — For as note the *Magdeburgenses* (cent. 9 p. c. fol. 234) — with the ceremonies of the Mass being finished, — the *Pontifex* invited the *Roman king Lotharius* to the table of Christ, — and with the body and blood of the Lord received in his hand, — thus to him he speaks: *If innocent you-recognize-yourself to be from prohibited-and-interdicted incest of Waldrada with Nicholas of Rome, — and this with a fixed mind you have determined, — that never after this life-and-you-touched-yourself-lest-be-polluted, — pretended-your-hollow to lie in nefarious concubinage, — but by faith accede, — and the sacred body of eternal salvation which for you and for the remission of sins is offered, — to yourself receive. — But if from *bad conscience* it accuses you, — and by a mortal wound is proclaimed, — or *iterum to return to yourself with adulteresses* — you have disposed, — do not by any means presume to take, — lest perchance to judgment and condemnation to you it-come, — which for the faithful for a remedy divine providence has prepared.*

**In imitation of this deed the *Synod of Warmiense*** (c. 25) thus says: *often it happens that in monasteries thefts are perpetrated: — and those who commit these, are unknown. — Therefore we determine: that when the brethren themselves ought of such matters to expurgate themselves, — Mass by the abbot is celebrated, — or by someone whom the abbot has commanded, — with the brethren present. And thus at the ultimate celebration of the Mass for expurgation their-body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ they receive, — insofar as themselves of that crime they show themselves innocent* — which words of the *Council* are repeated in the *canon law* — indeed *decret. cause* 22 q. 5. *si perchance contingit*.

The same *Synod* c. 10 — commanded *bishops or presbyters* accused of homicide, or adultery, or theft, or another maleficence, — to purge themselves of it at the *celebration and communion of the Mass*.

Concerning *Gregory VII Pope* homily is-said also by *John Stumpfius* lib. 1 c. 14, — that through the reception of the consecrated *host* he wished to prove — that he had not invaded the *seat of Peter*, — but had been *legitimately elected*.

**Even now sometimes such speeches of the *vulgar are heard*:** *I want the Eucharist to receive in testimony of my innocence*: — *if I lie I want the sacrament to me not to be salutary*: — *thus God helps* — and other things — which — as many other things without doubt — are *remnants of Papist custom*.

**Since therefore the minister knows** — that any one accedes to this end, — and this manner of *probation of his innocence* institutes — this one in *confession* to examine, — and with the truth of the matter having been found, — from this institute to dehort-him, — and to the *use of coena not to admit* he ought.

**For to this end this sacrament is not instituted** — but is *confirmation of faith*, — not attestation of innocence: — nor is it done with commemoration of the Lord's death, — nor are the benefits of Christ sufficiently pondered, — but *external only some advantage* is respected.

**Wherefore this depraved custom of the vulgar** — is to be gravely blamed in sermon, — as *inexcusable levity and temerity*, — which not to the *honor of Christ*, — but to the *profanation* of his most sacred sacrament goes.

**For since this end Christ in his institution** — neither expressed, — nor tacitly proposed, — the addition is *to the word*, — which is prohibited (Deut 4:2; 12:21). — And it is to be remembered that the *Apostle Paul* said: *not to be wise above what is written* (Rom 12:5; 1 Cor 4:6).

**Christ prohibited swearing** — either by heaven, — or by earth, — or by the temple etc. (Matt 5): — do you think that oath or attestation through the sacrament of his body can please him?

**Nor also does such *probation of innocence* have any *substance of robustness*** — since many *unworthily accede*, — who from this sacred Lord's table make *palladium of iniquity*, — whose *nequities* God sometime manifested, — when the *occult of hearts* is *opened* (1 Cor 4:5).

**The *Romans* saw this: — therefore that canon of the *Council of Reformation* was abrogated** — as testifies *Bartholomew Carranza* in *summa Concilii* p. 785. — *Thomas* p. 3 q. 80 art. 6 ad 3. attributes the abrogation to *Stephen the Pope* — and with this reason: — *because this would be to tempt God* — whence he infers: — *by no means ought the body of Christ to be given to anyone for-purpose-of-crime, — as if for examination*.

### Casus IV. How the minister of the Church ought to act towards those who through *some years*, — or otherwise for long from use of the sacred coena — have abstained

*Reply.* There are not-few — who without loss of piety or of eternal salvation — can abstain from the sacred coena of the Lord, — provided *others they love and hear diligently the word of God*, — pray diligently, — and their life, — as far as it can be done, — rightly-institute.

**To all these the minister of the Church** — much must be admonished, — first indeed *privately*, — because if for a long time he winks-at the salvation of his own, — he seems now to profane and-then-to-put-them-out, — and to seek his own advantage. And when *privately* he ought to admonish them, — that the *use of Sacraments* is not *ἀδιάφορον*, — but *divinely instituted*, — since Christ not only wills us to hear the word, — but also to use the coena, — as in the institution of this sacrament he commands: *this do in remembrance of me*: — to which command who does not obey — is not from the *sheep* of Christ: — for concerning these he himself said: *my sheep hear my voice* (John 10:4). Thus *Paul* in the place of Christ enjoins us: *But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.* (1 Cor 11:28). — He does not leave this in *our power*, — but bids to *eat and drink*.

**Then he should show them their disease** — that so deeply in sins they stick — that they are — omnisly-not-themselves — nor can-they-recognize, — how *inclined our flesh in believing the promises of God* — which in the word are proposed, — of all which — God through the use of the sacred coena wishes to lift-up.

**Whoever recognizes this candidly** — the *gravity of his disease*, — and *its cause* — with greater desire will seek that medicine.

**Third:** he should attentively-admonish them, — how many *scandals* they cause, — since they think it suffices for piety only *the word, prayers*, and *honest life*. — This example by-their-example — could-instill to others: — for what reason briefly no one would-use — the *sacred coena*: — since however *D. Paul* wills — that *even to Christ's ultimate advent* — in the Church it be usurped (1 Cor 11:26).

**Fourth: let him inculcate to them** — that it does not suffice — the other cults-of-divine parts, — unless also *sacred coena's use* diligently attaches, — for both *to hear the word* — and *to use the sacraments* — *both are divinely instituted*, — and if we wish to be not only hearers, but also *doers of the word* — all Christ's *ordinations* faithfully are to be observed. *Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.* (James 4:17).

**Fifth: how much such a contemner damages the sacraments** — while himself of the *salutary remedy*, — of the food of his soul, — and of *most-firm strength against Satan's darts* deprives. — For — as rightly writes *Cyprian* (super Ps. 108): *not only the *body of the Lord from vices is-cleansed and adorned* — but also filled with virtues — but also against all persecution is supported*. *Chrysostom* homily 46 in John: *as lions breathing-fire: — so from this table we depart *terrible* to the devil* — and homily 15 in prior *ad Corinth.*: *the very table is nerve of our soul, — strength of mind, — bond of confidence, — hope, — salvation, light, life. If from here-with-this-sacrifice we depart — we shall pass, — with the greatest confidence into the *sanctuary* ascending, — as *golden with certain vestments-clothed*.* — All these things — either they ignore — or do not weigh, — or nakedly-contemn — who *use of this sacrament* contemn, — since a-double-of-souls of theirs-suffer.

**Sixth: it is finally indicated to them** — that with these habits they *from every consortium of true Christians* eliminate themselves — of whose among-others external usage is sign, — communion of sacraments, — which *animadversion of pious magistrate* they incur, — who *contemners of Sacraments* — without fear-of-divine-wrath — in his Republic tolerate cannot: — that finally *ecclesiastical censure* also — is not to be found — for the true piety of the remaining forces of the Christian-immunity to be preserved.

**If someone should say** — that they only are *contemners of the sacraments* — who think, — speak, — or *blaspheme* against them: — one is very much deceived. — For this too is to contemn — when one does not wish to use those things which for his salvation are divinely ordained. — Therefore *B. Luther* in preface of the *smaller catechism* those simply among contemners of the sacraments enumerates: *who at least three or four times a year do not use them* — because *what is neglected on-purpose* — is thereby *contemned*.

**What indeed you should do among those** — who *body and blood of the Lord fed* — now sleep in-dormitories: — that of resurrection to glory they may expect, — who *by that most-illustrious pledge — for years many* — or *rarely enough have used it*.

### Casus V. Whether the minister of the Church can *distribute the sacred coena* to those, — who *to his Church do not pertain*, — but have their ordinary pastors

*Reply.* Those who seek the *use of the sacred coena* from *foreign pastors* — are in multiple difference.

**Some are of faithful, — who from their sedeis expelled**, — in foreign places sojourn, — and thus by necessity forced left their pastors: — to these the *ministry of the word and Sacraments* — in those churches to which they take refuge — is not to be denied — provided they are conformable in faith to our churches. For all we are *members of one mystic body*: — therefore to each other we ought *not to deny aliments*.

**This is what *D. John* in his epistle to Gaius wrote** (3 John 1:5): *most dear, faithfully you-are-doing, whatsoever you-work in-the-brethren, and-this in the pilgrims — as testimony they-gave your-charity in-sight of church, — whom-well-doing you-are-leading — worthily of God, — for-the-name of him they-set-out, — nothing-accepting from the gentiles. — Us therefore we-ought to-receive such, — as fellow-workers of the truth*.

**A great certainly sin it is, — to deny bread to the hungry**, — of which the Prophet complains (Lam 4:4): *the tongue of the suckling stuck to his palate for thirst — the infants sought bread, — and there was none who broke it to them*: — far more gravely a crime is, — to deny the *aliment of souls* to those anxiously seeking. **The Lord threatens gravest** *woes to nations, — who live-luxuriantly*, — and *are not saddened over the contrition of Joseph* (Amos 6:6). — This also pertains to those, — with whom the *word of God is opulently dwelling*, — who nevertheless to *exiled and languishing* — of this divine benefit deny: — nor for that reason think themselves that they-not-expelled by peril: — since God perhaps on account of those *pilgrims* preserves-his-churches-so-that they-have-*halcyonia* — some of their souls.

**Nay we ought to those miserable ones** — to our assemblies to *re-aggregate* fearing-them, — with love-to-summon we ought — since indeed the *Spouse of Christ* — or the *church* (Rev 22:17) — others invites, — *Spirit and Spouse say: come. — Also who-thirsts, come, — and who wills, — let-him-take water of life gratis*: — much more with joy we-ought to-receive them — who *spontaneously come*, — communion of our sacred-rites they seek.

**Thus Christ ejected no-one coming-to-himself** (John 6:37): — in the persecution *of Herod he seceded* together with the Apostles into a *desert place near Bethsaida*, — which when the *crowds recognized*, — they followed him, — and *he received them, and spoke to them of the kingdom of God* (Luke 9:11).

**Apostle Paul debtor-of-himself both to *Greeks and to barbarians*** (Rom 1:14), — that is, of all — who of ministry of his need, — because *God is God of both Greeks and gentiles* (Rom 3:29).

**Here pertains that beautiful saying** — which from lib. contra Parmen. is cited in *canon-law* cause 24 q. 3 c. 39 fol. 143: *concede to God — that his garden — which extends far and wide is-diffused. Do not exclude of the-Orient and North, — of the-West and southern regions of all — and of innumerable populations Christ-blood-drinkers.*

**Under the persecution of *Huneric Eugenius Bishop*** — by mandate of the king edict-issued, — that not only he himself from the *public office of teaching* should abstain, — but also whatsoever-sex-persons of any *vandal habit* — if the temple he-should-see-entering, — from-that-place he-should-repel. — Truly that pious man such response gave, — which of that person was most decorous, — and to the ministry honorific: *the house of God, to no man is closed, — all-open to-going-forth. — Who-from-that-forbids-them-going-in — whence he-will-expel* — referring the *centuriators Magdeburgenses* by-authors cent. 5 c. 6 fol. 623.

**By which reasons and examples** — the ministers of the Church admonished are — that those, — who from abroad expelled — to them themselves adjoin — sacred rites — should not be denied — even if by an impious foreign magistrate has been forbidden: — for *and in this God more to be obeyed* — *than men*.

**Then, since in some Republic** — with-negotiate this can happen, — then from some other pastor they-can-seek-the-sacred-coena, — even if of his parish they-do-not-belong, — nay repulsed he-is from-the-communion of sacred-rites, — but as a *sheep lost and found* — with joy is-to-be-taken-up: — because now-no-more to *Pontifical* — but to *orthodox church* he-is-to-be-referred.

**If however a pastor orthodox** — as foreign should-reject-him, — with-fault of pastor in salvation-of-his-own would-be-impeded, — and his *idolomania* — in which hitherto he-lived — would-be-confirmed, — which nowise can-be-excused.

**Third, if anyone from *infirmity of health*** — is oppressed, — his even of place-of-that pastor as-much bound to have-of-him as of-his-own, — because here is not contempt of some of *ordinary of-his minister* — but *necessity has no law*.

**In which case however the pastor is-to-be-circumspect**, — and of *confession and antecedent life diligently to-inquire* — decet: — lest *sanctum* to dogs is-given.

**Fourth, if perhaps a pastor to some one from-his-hearers** — from hatred, — or from cupidity of vengeance, — or from whatever similar cause — the sacred-coena in-advance-denied, — and-the hearer fears — lest already deprived of the medicine of salvation for-a-long-time — he-remain, — for-us-Christians *God more to obey — than men*.

**Then, since in some Republic** — this happens rarely, — then from some other pastor he-can-seek-the-sacred-coena, — if previously the pastor of that crime as guilty — to the ministry or the consistory to which that business pertains, — has been-informed, — and-not-yet been-brought — that henceforth confessing he-should-admit-him. — For vehemence and injury of the ordinary pastor to the salvation of the hearer for-loss should not be.

**Fifth, if the minister of any church** — has-notoriously-been-wicked and-impure, — an *adulterer or homicide*, — with scandal blasphemer and perjurer, — who long-since not-only *removal-penalty*, — but a graver punishment had-merited, — and-in that occasion either the pious *patron* or some other of the hearers — from-the-sacred-coena would-horror, — a foreign pastor not-immediately admits, — but *cognition of this cause* to the *consistory refers* — with-whose is the power of judging and permitting, — whatever for the *reason of circumstances* — of that church useful he-shall-have-understood.

**For even if the efficacy of the sacrament** — does not depend on the impiety of the minister, — nevertheless not to every one is-given, — to such a notorious wicked minister with-due reverence and devotion to-approach, — and himself of-the salvation of his own soul to-commit — since he *properly of his own soul care plainly does-not-have*.

**Finally there are others** — who *neglected of-their pastor of-their-own ordinary*, — of a foreign's work in *auscultation of the word or in use of Sacraments* they-use — only from *insatiable hatred* against their-ordinary pastor, — otherwise pious and inculpable enough, — but who from *foreign to the nod of all live cannot*, — but with some in *lite* lives.

**Him a foreign pastor to-his-own sheep with good conscience to-conjoin**, — or in his church to the *sacrosanct coena* to-admit cannot, — but rather to his ordinary pastor of-use to-remit, — and how gravely by this his *contemtu* he-sins, — with *meekness* to-teach ought — for the following reasons:

**(1) Because no one *dissensions between pastor and his own sheep-ones should-nourish*** — but rather *should-cut-off*, — and to-exhort — an-especially-*contumacious hearer* — that hatred he-should-lay-down, — and with-his pastor *reconciliation* he-should-admit; — and-that-to-every brother in-us delinquent, — much-less to-our pastor we-owe, — according to admonition of Christ (Matt 5:23-24).

**(2) Each minister of the Church is-given to *one only Church***, — for-which alone at some time also *reason to render he is*: — this diligently let-him-care, — others to their pastors let-him-leave, — according to admonition of *Paul*: *attend to yourselves and to the whole flock, in-which you Holy Spirit has-placed bishops* (Acts 20:28); — and-*Peter*: *tend the flock which to-you has-been-committed* (1 Pet 5:1-2).

**(3) It would-be *ἀλλοτριοεπισκοπία*** [meddling] and *φιλανθρωπία* [misdirected-love] — prohibited in Scripture, — if anyone of others' pastors' sheep-ones to himself would-drag, — or *conniventia* his would-make, — that at some *rougher word* their pastor their own ordinary they-would-leave, — since indeed so-easily by another are-admitted, — the-thing which in *most-certain contempt of ministry* would-go. — Mindful therefore here let-be-pastors each of the rule of Christ: *what to you not wish, to another do not do* (Matt 7:12); — and-in the *Council of Arelatensis* was-cautioned c. 17: *no-one of bishops another bishop should-tread-upon*.

**(4) A foreign pastor knows** — how great crime he-himself-binds, — who *pertinaciously hates his pastor*, — especially innocent: — those however, — who *pertinaciously other people hate*, and-not *repent*, — to the sacred coena to-admit no one with-safety-of-piety can — unless *knowingly and willingly against his conscience judgment and damnation temporal and eternal to-incur* wants.

**(5) God enjoined the ministers of the church** — that each of the hearers of theirs — if impious he-were — should-*dehort him from-his-way, — otherwise the blood of him from-the-hand of ministers of him should-require* (Ezek 3:18). — But when a pastor of-another impious of some one from *hatred of-his ordinary pastor to himself as fugitive*, — admits, — vehemently to-be-feared, — lest the foreign pastor should-suffer of-that penalty, — which to-that other minister of-his-own ordinary through-connivance to-negligence-of-being — was-owed. — Wherefore may-there-not-be-easily-fickle, — to whom *aures of fugitives* — whom more-freely to-their ordinary he-should-remit, — according to *praxin* of the ancients. — In the *Council of Carthaginian* is-had a decree ap. 20, — that: *no bishop should-usurp of-fault sheep-ones alienated, — nor any of bishops of another to-flow — into diocese-of-another for a walk*.

**In the Council of Elvira canon 51 was-cautioned**, — that bishops to sacred things of theirs a foreigner — should-not-admit, — without *communion-letters*, — which are-called *formatae* and *communicatorias*, — and by their own no one is-to-be-caught-different from the-others: — for this the reason indeed is: *what does-Osiander* (in notes on this canon) *is-called-known — with-the-tomb of ecclesiastical history c. 9*: *since some-time, — since discipline of ecclesiastical-with cared-for and-not — for-external causes had-emerged, — of some-place they-had-taken, — pass-abroad they-began. — For which cause the bishops of some others had-remitted*.

**In this sentence not-few has *Cyprian* (lib. 1 epist. 6)** — *ceases whoever-perverse and lubricous and superb spirit-of-suo of God knew, — or however-with a bishop by him himself constituted*, — as-*iterum* epist. 8: *for individual pastors of the flock a portion is-inscribed, — which* rule *each and-render* rule *to the Lord. — Does-not-therefore behoove — of proper spouse-of-hers not to-circumvent* — nor *concord-of-episcopal cohering fraud-suo and-perfidious insinuation-of-temerarity to-collide*.

**Who to all these consenting have** — see-in-*Consilio Dedekenniano* p. 2 fol. 104.

### Casus VI. What is-to-be-done at time-of-plague, — in-what-manner pious pastors ought to-administer *sacred coena* in-house-of-that pertaining, — if perchance ecclesiastical assemblies be interdicted

*Reply.* Pastors without fear of their sheep-ones the-care to-have they-ought, — for they-are in *the-vocation of God*, — and under shadow of *wings of the-divine defense* they-can-be-safe. But on-account-of the-people they-ought to-take-care, — lest by *importune terror* — at-least of-conspicious-pastor's example be-terrified.

**Therefore also the people is-to-be-admonished** — that in-time-of-plague more-they-prepare themselves for-death, — and *sacred coena they-should-receive* while yet in-*health-they-are*, — lest afterwards at-time-of-disease on-account-of one man the-whole church into peril be-thrown.

**If however anyone falls-sick**, — and the-minister of-the-church implores help, — this is-not-to-be-denied: — but concerning the-mode-here it-is-worth-questioning. **Some think** — the-pastor *the-consecrated elements*, — that-is, — bread and wine consecrated — through another to-the-sick may-send: — and this-in-genus they-provoke to-example of-*Serapion*, — who moribund to-the-minister sent, — and from him sought sacred-coena, — the-minister then also lying-down-sick — showed to-a-boy — who-with came-summoned — a-little of-the-Eucharist for-a-sick person to-be-brought — as-writes *Eusebius* lib. 6 c. 44. Confer *Chytraeus De Morte Regis*, c. 65, p. 133, 4.

**But this by no means can-be-approved** — because this matter has-species of-the-*intrusion of Pontifical* — that from-a-sacrament *bare-work* be-*opus operatum*, — as-though no-one, — unless with-received-sacrament in-the-Lord to-die, — could — and-the-sick — especially in-the-villages, — where they-are-more-uncultivated — even with-the-consecrated-elements received, — of-consolation would-be-destitute — since-a-minister absent-would-be, — nay if he-had-not-eaten *bread and-drunk-wine* — in-doubt would-be-left. — Others also occasion would-give, — that access to-the-sacred-coena for-contempt they-would-have, — if with-similarly to-the-house they-could-be-sent, — and-because Satan is-a-perpetual tempter, — with-thoughts those, — that-with the-sick if-he-had-not-received them-really and-actively — would-suggest, — but from-a-private-house-of-one communion *redundant to-put* — And this *private of-one-person communion* which is-in the *private masses* — to-the-institution of-Christ to-agree they-say in-council of-*Trent* sess. 3 c. 22 canon 30.

**But rightly *Luther* felt** — in-articles Smalcaldicis art. *of-the-Mass* p. 1, — himself-to-self to-communicate is-*human persuasion*, — destitute in-the-word of-God, — uncertain if-not to-be-shunned to-do.

**For that *Chemnitz* rightly observed** — such communion of-priest does-not-agree with-the-description of-*Paul* 1 Cor 11: — for he-says: it-cannot properly *coena of-the-Lord to-be-celebrated*, — if anyone from-his own private, — proper, — or *peculiar action*, — as-if by-no-one-of-himself would-be-said, — should-preoccupy.

**Or the-treatment is of-ministers *in-solitary-place***, — who *colleagues and-of-neighbor pastors* are-destitute, — from-whom sacrament to-receive they-could: — these in-defect that, — while others communicate, — also from-the-same *bread to-eat* — and-from-the-same *cup to-drink* they-can, — provided not only in-time-of-necessity they-use, — and-indeed by-difference-of-person, — which is-in-ministry-ordinary constituted, — in-which sacred-things to-this Sacrament necessary, — even by-one person of-different-respect to-be-made can-be, — in-the-manner-in-which-in other sacred actions and-profane occurs.

**Or finally the-treatment is of-ministers**, — who *colleagues or-neighbor pastors have*. And here again difference *is-to-be-admitted*. Either such a-minister does-not-anymore function of-ecclesiastical office, — but either he-was-*deposed*, — or he-himself renounced, — and-now lives as *private*: — and-here in-no-way sacraments to-administer can, — not-even to-others, — much-less to-himself, — because the vocation of-him to-ministry expired. Or he-lives in-that church of-the-ministry, — where already through-long custom prevailed, — that anyone in-communion of-others himself-also from-the-consecrated-bread *should-eat*, — and-from-the-*consecrated-wine* *should-drink*: — there even-if better it-were, — if from-*colleague* or *neighbor his sacred-coena would-receive*, — nevertheless — lest by-changing custom, — in-self not-evil scandal of-weak-ones-to-cause, — without scruple the-custom of-Church he-can-retain: — provided that-custom is-not to-the-*institution-of-Christ* contrary, — which nowhere he-prescribed or willed, — that always be in-the-administration-*of-two-persons*, — one giving, another receiving.

**In these matters, — which neither against a-command nor against the-will of-God** — to-no-one is-scruple to-be-caused.

**Third finally remains, — who in-churches live**, — where *colleagues are-several* — or *neighbor-pastors*, — nor ever that custom of-communicating himself-to-himself prevailed: — there no-one this-let-do, — but *another let-him-seek* to-whom-to-confess, — and by-whom-to-be-absolved, — and the-sacrament of-the-coena to-receive. — No-one indeed himself from-sins can-absolve, — which-of the-communion of-sacred antecedes: — nor let-him-be-scandalized by-that *new innovation*: — nor can-anyone in-*temptations* himself-*sufficiently to-console*: — but *here need is of-ministry as of-the-workshop of-the-Holy-Spirit*, — who-through his ministers *efficacious to-be is-accustomed*.

**In-the-manner therefore in-which a-*physician* — even-if in-doctrine and-experience excellent** — even-in his-own disease, — not-only his own-*judgment follows*, — but from-another *physician medicine receives*: — so a *Theologian* also most-learned from-another of-the-ministers of-the-church, — whom he-has, — the-sacred-coena to-seek — more-safely-must, — than to-himself to-give, — lest the-*ministry-of-the-Holy-Spirit* — he-himself by-his own-deed contemn seem.

### Casus VII. Whether the minister of the word to himself the *sacred coena* to-give-can

*Reply.* To this question not-simply to-be-answered can, — but with distinction of subject.

Either the-treatment is of-*Pontifical* ministers or *priests*, — who in-*private masses* alone communicate, — with-the-populace-looking, — from-whom-food-to-them anyone-of-their private communion to-redound they-suppose. And this-private of-one-person-communion which is-in *private masses* — to-the-institution-of-Christ to-agree they-say in-council of-*Trent* sess. 3 c. 22 canon 30.

**But rightly with *Luther* felt** in *Smalcald art.* about the Mass p. 1, — *himself to himself to communicate is a-human persuasion*, — destitute of the word of God, — uncertain — if not to be shunned to do.

**For what *Chemnitz* rightly observed** — such communion of a priest does not agree with the description of Paul 1 Cor 11: — for he says: it-cannot properly *the coena of the Lord to be celebrated*, — if anyone from his own private, — proper, — or *peculiar action*, — as if by-no-one of himself would be said, — should preoccupy.

**Or the treatment is of ministers *in solitary place***, — who are destitute of *colleagues and neighbor pastors*, — from whom-of-a-sacrament to-receive they-could: — these in-defect of this — while others communicate — even from-the-same *bread to-eat*, — and-from-the-same *cup to-drink* they-can, — provided not-only in-time-of-necessity they-use, — and-*indeed with-diverse person* — which is-in *ministry-ordinary constituted* — in-which-*sacred-things to-this-Sacrament necessary*, — even by-one person of-different-respect done can-be, — in-the-manner-in-which-in other sacred actions and-profane occurs.

**Or finally the treatment is of ministers**, — who *colleagues or neighbor pastors have*. And here again difference is-to-be-admitted. Either such a minister *does not anymore function of ecclesiastical office*, — but either he was *deposed*, — or he himself *renounced*, — and now lives as *private*: — and here in-no-way sacraments to-administer he-can, — not-even to-others, — much-less to-himself, — because the *vocation of him to ministry expired*. Or he-lives in that church-of-the-ministry, — where already through-long *custom prevailed*, — that anyone in-communion of-others *himself-also from-the-consecrated-bread eat*, — and-from-the-*consecrated-wine drink*: — there even-if better it-were, — if from *colleague or from neighbor his-sacred-coena would-receive*, — nevertheless — lest by-changing-custom, — in-self not-evil *scandal of-weak-ones to-cause*, — without-scruple the-custom-of-Church he-can-retain: — provided that custom-is-not to-the-*institution-of-Christ contrary*, — who nowhere prescribed or willed, — that always be-in-the-*administration-of-two-persons*, — one *giving*, another *receiving*.

**In these matters, — which neither against a-command nor against the-will-of-God** — to-no-one is-scruple-to-be-caused.

**Third finally remain, — who in-churches live**, — where *colleagues are-several* — or *neighbor pastors*, — nor ever that *custom of-communicating himself-to-himself prevailed*: — there no-one this-let-do, — but *another let-him-seek* — to-whom-to-confess, — and-by-whom-to-be-absolved, — and-the-sacrament of-the-coena to-receive. — No-one indeed himself from-sins can-absolve, — which-of the-communion of-sacred-antecedes: — nor let-him-be-scandalized by-that *new-innovation*: — nor can-anyone in-*temptations* himself-*sufficiently to-console*: — but here *need is of-ministry as of-the-workshop of-the-Holy-Spirit*, — who through-his ministers *efficacious-to-be is-accustomed*.

**In-the-manner therefore in-which a *physician* — even-if in-doctrine and-experience excellent** — even-in-his-own-disease, — *not-only his-own-judgment follows*, — but from-another *physician medicine receives*: — so a *Theologian* also *most-learned* from-another of-the-ministers of-the-Church, — whom he-has, — the *sacred-coena to-seek more-safely must*, — than to-himself to-give, — lest the *ministry-of-the-Holy-Spirit* — he-himself by-his-own-deed contemn seem.

### Casus VIII. What is-to-be-determined of-that minister-of-the-church, — who perhaps in-consecration *some word* omits

*Reply.* This-deed by-some is-excused when — not from-*place-of-him is*, — but from-*too-much attention of-minister* as-if-*to-another-place-transferred*, — and-then, — that he-said or-did *he-does-not-observe*. Usual indeed rule-is: *for-*sin *not-to-be-held*, — *fluent-in-will*, — *thought*.

**But-questionable is** — of-how-much-force is in-this excusation. For in-all actions, — even in-those-which *religion-touch*, — *due moderation of-attention is-to-be-adhibited*. In-the-manner in-which too-*severe towards law is-strictness in-Micha* (Judg 17-18) *nimia towards-Paul is-observance in-Peter* (Gal 2:11) is-reprehended: — thus even *too-attention-lax is-to-be-blamed* in-treating-of-sacred-things: — for it-not-only ought-to-happen or-of-what-loco-us or-suggestion-of-fantastic — that-either we-act-or we-speak in-things-divine.

**And-this-is *true-attention*** — which the-*divine-thing well-weighs*, — and-to-with-*true-conscience treats*.

**Then-that-axiom, — *for-sin not-to-be-had, — what-not-happens with-will-conformed*, — in-things-political has-force**, — where-*cogitation-about-something-else-*with-nobody-harms*, — in-things-spiritual however, — and-especially in-*distribution of-sacred-things* — no-place-has. — For also *sins-of-ignorance and-youth* are-punished-in-Scripture (Lev 4:2; Ps 25:12; Ps 19:12-13). — Who-therefore *distributes-Sacrament*.

**(1) *Contrary to institution of Christ*** — sins, — whether-by-slip-of-tongue, — whether-by-inadvertence he-does: — but-if he-added *desire-to-purpose designated*, — the-sin-graver was, — and-of-greater-penalty *worthy*, — because *voluntary-was*.

**Then the *omission of-word-of-institution* in-the-very-act of-Eucharist grave-is sin**, — and-*condemnation-worthy* — (1) because he-*violates the-institution-of-Christ*, — of-which good-substance came-those-words.

**(2) The-other-part of-*sacramental-elements* is-not-consecrated**, — that-is, — with-institution-of-Christ *is-not-separated*: — for that vehicle is-of-the-mystery, — but *remains-naked-element*.

**(3) The-dispensation of-the-Sacrament is-not a-*private-action***, — where error easily and-without-scandal to-be-corrected can, — but *public to-the-whole church pertaining*, — which in-the-same-place at *prayer of-the-Sacrament comes-together*, — where-if not-*without-maximum-scandal in-face-of-them* something *otherwise-happens than as-ought parts*.

**(4) This-deed either of-*inexcusable temerity is***, — or of-lightsome *drowsiness*. In-*dispensation however of-sacred-things not-only of-communicants*, — but-also-of-*dispensers-of-them*, — in-*religious-attention required*.

**Which-things-so-are** — doubt none-is, — that-such-a-pastor of-grave-penalty *worthy is*: — before-*all-however he-himself before God should-flee*, — whose *sacrament he-profaned*, — then-of-the-church, — which not-lightly he-offended, — third *pardon from God and church he-should-seek*, — fourth by-*obedience of-pastor of-his-own*, — how-*mild-be*, — if-*more-often to-this-lapses* — of-total-*removal be-punished*.

**The Church however to-be-admonished is**, — lest that-deed to-whole-they-impute-ministry, — as-*man's-heart to-scandal much-inclined tends*: — therefore *most-be moved with-diligence and-serious-of-cause of-ministry-should-take*, — lest in-any-way in-word or-in-deed *heard should-offend*. — *Faithful indeed teacher of-church edifies, — as-much-as by-prayers Deum implorat*.
