## Chapter X. Cases of Conscience concerning the Use of the Keys of the Church

*De casibus conscientiae circa clavium usum ecclesiae.*

### Preamble

The keys of the Church are nothing other than *the power which the Lord conceded to his ministers in the Church for blessing and cursing men*. — For God is who *proposes to his people life and death, blessing and cursing* (Deut 30:19) — and that through the ministry.

And in the manner in which there are *two contrary effects* of ministry — namely *benediction and malediction* — so also there are *two-fold keys*, — one *of loosing*, — the other *of binding*, — which *Christ* committed not only to *his Apostles* (Matt 16:19), — but also to the *whole Church* (Matt 18:18), — which exercises its right through the *ministers of the word*.

**Church of Christ as spouse of Christ.** — For the Church of Christ is *spouse of Christ* (John 3:29), and *bride* (Ps 45:10), — and in his household *mother of families* (Ps 68:12). — As therefore *the master gives keys of the house to his wife*, — that she in his stead should administer, — so also *Christ the Lord* gave *keys of his own house*, which is the Church, — to his own spouse, — which she commits to her ministers, — who are called *dispensers of God's mysteries*.

Without these keys entry to the *kingdom of heaven* would be closed to us, — into which by baptism we have been received, — but through sin we again close heaven; — which, — to *penitent sinners* — through the *loosing key* is opened, — and eternal salvation announced, — but to *impenitents* — through the *binding key* — heaven is closed and hell opened, — announcing to them God's wrath owed to their sins.

**Rejection of contempt of Church's keys.** — Nor are keys of Church, — on account of penitent sinners without God, — to be neglected, — as though anyone could without them be reconciled to God; — for if this were so, — in vain would keys of the Church have been given.

Hence is that saying of *Job* (7:20): *I have sinned, — what do I confess to thee, O keeper of men?* If therefore my sin no one condemns except me, — cursing this way, — no one can absolve me from sin unless I have believed the announcement of *ecclesiastical grace*: — therefore why then without cause would those *keys of the Church of God* [be]? — In vain would be Church, — in vain the words of Christ.

To these keys pertain the *confession of sins* and *absolution*, — likewise *satisfactions*, — and above all *excommunication*: — all of which also lack no doubt, — of which now with God willing we shall speak.

### Casus I. Whether the minister of the Church has absolute power of the keys — so that he can absolve or bind whomever he wishes

*Reply.* By no means: — but that power is *limited*, — *restricted* to the mandate of the Lord, — that penitents' sins be remitted, — that impenitents' sins be retained.

**That power presupposes the key of the *word of God*** — namely the *key of knowledge, discretion, and piety* — lest what should be closed be opened, — or what should be opened be closed.

That power is given by Christ to ministers, — but *not absolute*, — but *ministerial*. — He himself has *the key of David* (Rev 3:7): — therefore to Christ's nod and mandate is she exercised.

**The Lord of the house gives the keys to the steward of the house**, — not that at *his own arbitrary* he should let-into or exclude-from, — but that *at the Lord's mandate* he should discharge his function of stewardship. — The stewards of divine mysteries do nothing in this genus outside the *prescription of Christ*, — who is *Lord of his own house* (Heb 3:6). — But the will of Christ is: to loose penitents, — to open kingdom of heaven, — and again to bind impenitents, — closing to them the same.

And when the keys thus according to Christ's prescription by the stewards are moved, — then that action itself is *ratified*, — as it is written: *whatsoever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; — and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven* (Matt 18:18) — of which words *Augustine* writes in homily 50 of 30 homilies: *what is not sought is certain, — that neither the mandate of a king or prince, — nor the ministers of the ministry: — since long-else in the Pontifical concerning power of keys otherwise it is taught: — there to bishops is attributed power of *dominion* — or as Bellarmine says, — jurisdiction of loosing to their arbitrary — not to the prescription of Christ, — but to the nod and arbitrary of the Pontifical Roman.

**Papist abuse of the power of the keys.** Whence it is — that *indulgences are sold at a price* even to impenitents — in prohibited degrees, — matrimony is permitted — dispensation is granted, oaths are relaxed, — under whose obligation many magistrates are bound, — the thunder of *excommunication* is vibrated without consent of the Church, — chiefly against those who resist avarice and injustice of *bishops-becoming-Papas* — and by the *absolute power* which they usurp for themselves, — of binding and loosing at pleasure, — treasures of heaven they close and open, — with the Church resisting — and God himself in heaven: — therefore no pious man believes that such use of the keys in the Papacy is-obtained-there, — which is by the *word of God* declared contrary.

**Bellarmine's arguments answered.** — The *Romans* have moreover a pretext of this abuse of the keys — in the *sacred Scriptures*, — which *Bellarmine* proposes (lib. 3 *De poenitentia* c. 2), — to which now response must be made.

**First he seeks from Matt 16:19** — and Matt 18:17-20 — where in *power of the keys* is committed the *solid duty* given by Christ to Peter. *He says: — the words of Christ suffice not only to declare-and-teach that heaven is closed and opened, — but truly to close and open, — that is, to bind and loose the ministers of the Church, — as much as-to-the-thing-signified: — otherwise* — he says — *those words of Christ would be inefficacious*.

**Reply.** — We conceded certainly the minister of the Church has the power of the keys, — but not absolute, — but *bound to the word of God*. — For that penitent whom God wishes to loose from his sins, — from impenitents-and-secure-ones sins are bound. — Solution from sins moreover is nothing other than *announcement of grace of God through the word of penitents-of-Christ believing*. — Which is the same manner in which binding is announcement of wrath and punishments — which God threatens impenitents. — Thus explicated the *key* loosing and binding is truly given for *remission of sins* (John 20:23). And this announcement is not naked-sound-of-words without effect: — but he to whom this is announced — really is loosed or bound, — for God so speaks. — And this announcement is only for-consolation of afflicted-consciences to be perceived, — because verily-they-open-mouth of remission of sins: — otherwise tender consciences will feel — that God still stands angry, — until they do penitence.

**Words of Christ don't fail**: *whatsoever ye shall bind* etc. — But we have said, — the minister of the Church who exercises that ministry-of-loosing-and-binding is *promulgator and as-it-were executor* of the divine sentence, — in the manner the judge is not author of the sentence against *adulterers and homicides* (for the *sentence* already is-in-the-laws), — but only its minister and executor, — not by his own arbitrary and *absolute power*, — but *according to the prescribed law he judges*.

**Nothing else says that canon of the Apostles** (whom Bellarmine as-many enumerates by name) — none of them gives absolute power to ministers of the word — over-sinners-of-what-he-wishes-at-pleasure, — but as it in the word already has been *decided*. Ministers indeed *remit or retain sins*, — as ministers-not-lords of the Church: — the *sentence of the Lord* in the word announced to sinners they announce, — and thus Christ through them looses or binds.

**Nor is this a small power** — as Bellarmine speaks with-contempt-enough: *to remit sins*, — he says, — *to faithful, — from infidels to retain — is not a great thing, — for anyone can do this, — provided he can read the Gospel and know the difference of faithful from infidels of some sort by external signs*.

But these are injurious to the *ministry of the word*, — whose office is to announce remission of sins to penitents, — retention to impenitents: — the great matter this is, — and worthy of admiration; — this power gave God to men, — not promiscuously to all, — not to heretics, — not to laymen, — much less to demons, — but to *his disciples*, — the Apostles, — and to *successors of Apostles the doctors*. — In the manner therefore *reading to all pertains not*, — but only to those who have learned to read, — thus what to penitents is *remitted*, — to impenitents however *retained sins are*, — to read indeed can anyone in Scripture, — but *to announce to sinners and apply* — is not of anyone-whatever, — but *ordinarily* God has committed this to those whom he willed to be *stewards of his mysteries*.

**Third Bellarmine reasons** — that if *sacerdotes* only judged, — nor truly *sins remitted*, — but only announced sins-remitted, — no one would care whether from a sacerdos he-had-recognized-himself-having-remission-of-sins, — since anyone could do this at home, — provided that only the word he attests. Thus writes *Augustine* also (in epist. 180 ad Honeratum) openly: *some receive reconciliation of the dying — and thus believing in Christ from this life migrating, — what does it matter — from whom pretty much they receive, — if the priest could not-be present to absolve them*.

**Reply.** — Most true is Christ's sentence: *He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.* (John 3:36). Therefore a faithful man through the word of God has *remission of sins*, — even if he could not have a *priest* — who from-sins would-absolve, — and would announce those words, — as-happens in *case of necessity*, — where minister cannot be had: — for-so does-not-depend *remission of sins from tone of words*, — which the minister at some time announces, — but *from the promise of the Gospel* which each believer to himself can apply. — If however anyone contemned the ministry, — and yet thought himself to be saved, — even if he did not hear it, — he would without doubt perish, — not indeed on account of defect of those words, — which the minister of the Church announces to the sinner, — but on account of *contempt of ministry*, — which redounds unto Christ himself, — as it is written: *he who despises you, despises me* (Luke 10:16).

**Augustine in the passage cited** treats of *ordinary case*, — and no absolute necessity — nay through defect of few pertaining to *ordinary ministry*, — that in most other places-in-which is-found-place: — is-taken-away. But through the word, — which anyone can read and meditate — either we-are-loosed or we-are-bound, — as their-heart is-formed. In the word indeed God himself even to the heart-speaks, — provided they do not contemn — what with others in ordinary manner is dispensed. — Hence *Augustine* (in the place-praised) those who are of *desperation-of-himself* — speaks-of, — that is, — through *force of disease put beyond themselves*, — not through *sacerdotal confession* — as-*Bellarmine* would-suppose, — but through *baptism*, — while there penitents-yet-reconciled-to-Christ, — are-said-to-be. And it is added, — if from that despair *restored* they-could-live, — *is-worthy to be treated-longer-of, — that indeed baptism is-required only from contemners of the sacraments, — since that already is baptized* — like *concerning adultery-of-spouses* c. 18.

**Fourth Bellarmine argues** — that if sacerdotes not-truly *remission* announce of sins, — is-vain and *temerarious*, — nay in a minister of the word *audacious*, — if he *positively pronounce sins remitted*, — or if from hypothesis you believe, — then *absolutely temerarily pronounces*, — if he-does-not-know, — whether-truly he believes, — who forsooth demanded — that his-penitence *truly*, — but if only he saw — that also, if he-were-scoffing at, — of not-being-known: — therefore not-*absolute the ministry's* — nothing is-added-punctuated on the-thing, — either through the-signs of a-good animal, — either truly through his part-of-faith.

**Reply.** — We do not deny absolution to be a certain judicial-act, — but not such — in which absolute power of judging is-*at-pleasure*: — but this judgment is-acted according to the prescribed of the laws, — according-to-which either they-absolve or they-condemn.

**In the manner therefore in which civil-laws** can be-read by all, — yet not all publicly pronounce sentence, — but only-those, — who in-order judge is-constituted: — thus sentence of sins either *absolutorial* or *condemnatorial* all read in the word, — but only publicly promulgates, — the-one-who in *legation acts for Christ*.

**Then distinction must-be-made between the *right of the Church and its execution*.** — The right of announcing remission of sins to contrite-of-heart is *general*, — that-is in-case-of-necessity, — or in-defect of *ordinary ministers*, — anyone the-*afflicted proximum and tempted* can-console, — with-remission of his sins publicly-however not-so, — for *general the-right*, — which is *from the-Church*, — from-the *particular the-executio* however with those alone-God the-preaching of-the-word, — administration of-Sacraments, — and-power of-keys committed.

**Finally very much cries out** *Bellarmine* on-the-efficacy of-words, — as-if those words, *remitted-are your-sins*, — pronounced-to-any-repenting sinner — by-a-minister of-the-Church, — do-not-more-have weight, — than-if from-a-lay person or-from-an-unfaithful-man or-even from-the-devil they-were-said. Great certainly is-the *irreverence* of ministers of-word — to-whom the-Lord speaks in-the-person of *Jeremiah*: *behold, I-have-given my-words in-thy mouth* (Jer 1:9), — and-through *Isaiah*: *my Spirit which is in-thee, — my-words which I-have-put in-thy mouth* (Isa 59:21) — from-not-uncertainly speaks the-minister by-reason of-office, — not-so-much *words of-man*, — but truly *words of-God*, — as the-Apostle teaches (1 Thess 2:13) — which is by *words of-lay-person* or of-infidel, — much-less by *words of-devil*, — to-be-said cannot without blasphemy.

**Experience also of most-afflicted sinners** — the-most-penetrating force of *absolution* pronounced by-a-minister — which they-say to-be-of-such-vigor as-if-they-heard from-the-mouth of-Christ per authentic saying John 20:23.

Discussed therefore all-these, — which *Bellarmine* to-prove *absolute power* of-*sacerdotes* in-absolving and-binding gathers, — we-conclude: — ministers of-the-Church have-indeed *power of-keys*, — but not *absolute* — and-*at-pleasure* to-be-usurped, — but to-the-law and-*prescribed* of-the-*divine word* determined, — that truly-*contrite* — and-in-the-Gospel *faith having* — with-the-purpose of-*emending-life* — absolvable-are; — impenitents however-so *secure ones* — are-condemned.

### Casus II. Whether *private confession*, — which is-made to-a-priest, — and-*vulgarly called auricular* — is-necessary for-those-approaching to-the-sacred-Supper, — and-can they-be-*deprived of-sacred-communion* who-shall-not-have-confessed

*Reply.* The-word of-*confession is-taken twofold*. **Either for-*attestation of-faith*** — which-of-*confessing* is-called: — as-when *fideles* confess *Christ* — from-Christ before-*Pilate*: *I-came into-this-world, — that I-should-bear-witness to-the-truth* (John 18:37). — With-this confession we-are-not-here-treating.

**But of-*confession-of-sins*** — which-is-*threefold*:

**(1) To-God** — or-in-the-secret of-our-hearts — as *David* (Ps 32:5): *my-sin I-have-*confessed to-thee*, — and-the *publican* (Luke 18:13). *If we-confess our-sins* (1 John 1:9), — or *publicly in the-common-confession of-the-Church*, — where-God is-most-holy — and-all-*of-the-whole-church* sins we-confessed (Isa 9 + Dan 9); — and-in-our-churches at-*end-of-sermon*. Such confession *simply* is-necessary to *true penitent*.

**God-knows all-things certainly** — but *awaits your-voice*, — if-you-are-not-punished, — but-*acknowledged*. *Anticipate the-judgment of-God with-*confession*, — and-*if-so-anytime-you-desire-of-crimes-of-transgression* if-thou-shalt-*accuse-thyself*, — thou-shalt-have Christ-as-*helper-not-fearing*, — says *Ambrose* (lib. 2 *De poenitentia* c. 7).

**Hence in the-Prophet** it-is-said: *Put me in remembrance: let us plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest be justified.* (Isa 43:26); — and *Solomon* (Prov 28:13): *he-that-hideth-his-sins, — shall-not-prosper, — but-he-that-confesseth-them shall-have-mercy*.

**(2) To-*neighbor* whom-*we-have-offended***, — of-which *James* (5:16): *confess-your-*sins to-*each-other*. — This also is-necessary, — because without *reconciliation with neighbor* no *reconciliation with-God* can-be-had, — which Christ teaches (Matt 5:23-24; Matt 6:15; Matt 18:35).

**(3) *In-the-ministry-of-the-Church* placed-by-God**, — in-the-manner in-which *Saul* confessed his-sins to *Samuel* the-Prophet (1 Sam 15:24), — *David* to-*Nathan* (2 Sam 12:13). *Ahas* is-called to *Isaiah* (Isa 19:17); — where many of-*believers are-said to-be-*coming-to-Paul and-confessing-their-sins*.

**Of-this confession is-not** *absolute necessity*, — since it-lacks *mandate of-God*: — nevertheless are-cases *not-few*, — in-which *use of-that confession* it-is-persuaded to-be-retained, — even-if this from *liberty* is-done, — because:

**(1) By-the-remission of-confession**, — is-*taken-away also absolution*: — for-these-two are-conjoined: — and-in-that-manner *maximum-part of-*consolation, — with-which *afflicted conscience*, — nay is-*taken*: — for a-great is-*solace to-hear-from-mouth of-minister in-place-of-*Christ *absolution* of-*sins*, — and-*special application* of-grace, — which-else in-the-word announced to-be-had we-*of-have*.

**(2) Occasion is-given to-the-pastor** — of-*acting with-*communicants separately and-*in-species*, — that terrified consciences are-*erected*, — impenitents however, — and-in-*singular sins* deprehended, — are-taxed, — and-to-*serious penitence* are-*re-called*. For-not without *judgment* to-the-keys of-the-Church must-be-used.

**(3) Not less-occasion presents *confession*** — of-*exploring the-*proficience — especially-of-*studies in-the-articles-of-faith*, — and-above-all-that *the-*sacred-Supper are-treated *soundly*, — if any *defects* were-to-occur, — in *right they-may-be-formed*.

**(4) It-serves also *cognition of-worthiness or-unworthiness* of-*communicants***, — whether-*rightly-prepared they-approach*, — since it-is-*certain*, — those, — who-do-not-*prove themselves*, — worthy for-*sacred-food* are-*to-be-mandated*.

**(5) By-these causes** *Luther* also *made-much of-confession*, — and-*used it-freely*, — as-it-is-clear, — from t. 1 *ien. germ.* fol. 174, *ejusdem eiusdem* fol. 100, 164, 611, *iuris articuli Smalcaldici* art. 3 §  8 writes: *nowise in the-Church confession and absolution to-be-*abolished, — chiefly for-*tender and-*fearful consciences, — and for-*juveniles who-*are-to-be-educated, — and-*taught, — and-*examined, — as-what-*doctrine-of-Christ*: — and-in *epist. ad Francofurten.* 3 he-writes: *if a-*thousand and-again-a-thousand *worlds* were-mine, — I-would-*prefer to-lose-all, — than to-*permit even-a-particle of-this-thing to-*perish*.

**And on-*account of-these signal usefulnesses** — *even-now in-our-churches with-liberty of-the-Church retained*, — nor without-*rashness*, — and-*most-scandalous*-*singular-of-*things, — if-any among-us before-*Supper wished-to-use, — is-neglected: — the-thing-which against *Papacy of-*some *Calvinists* is-noted, — who this-*private confession*, — as *Papist* explore, — this itself testifying, — that *Augustinae Confessioni* — which-of-them expressly admits — the *addition* they-were-not-*added*.

**Ours it-is, to-remember**, — that even in-*Interim things which-are-things-of-*things, — in-*any-*however *ancient of-the-Church* obtained, — is-*not to-be-*temerariously *overturned*.

For as-in-*any Republic* one-must-live, — according-to-the-laws of-each-place: — thus also-according-to-the-*custom* of-*any Church* citizens of-the-Church must-act, — as *Augustine* (*epist. Ianuar.*): *in-that-time you-are-mine*, — where the-*utility* helps, — for-*where you-are-not-of-us*.

### Casus III. Whether in the-*private confession* the-*special enumeration* of-*all and-of-single sins* is-*necessary*

*Reply.* Thus teach the-*Romans*, — who all-and-*single mortal-sins* — which after-*diligent examination* come-into-*memory*, — from-*all* who to-*years-of-discretion have-come*, — into-*ears-of-priest narration* they-require, — and-that from-*divine-right necessary* they-teach, — and-*meritorious* they-make, — by-*which sins are-*expiated, — which-*sum-of-*doctrine of-*this-matter* in *Council of-Trent* (sess. 14 c. 5) — from-*canon of-*penitence *omnis utriusque sexus* is-*contained*, — which *Bellarmine* (lib. 3 *de-poenitentia*) repeats — and-*this confession they-call *sacramental*.

*Bellarmine* (lib. 3 *de-poenit.* c. 3) writes: *most-*certain-is*, — as *individual sins* to-be-*confessed for-*regeneration*.

**Our sentence** however is: — this-sort-of-*confession* in-*no-way to-be-*from divine right.

**(1) Because *enumeration of-all* mortal-sins is-*impossible***, — as *David* says (Ps 40:12): *sins have-*surrounded-me *above-*number-of-hairs of-my-head*.

**(2) Because it-is *contrary to-*religious-Chytraean-method** — as it-*follows from-*our-*Christian's *sanctifying-*sin-of-*Chytraean.

**(3) *Many* are the-*hidden delicts***, — as-*David* says (Ps 19:12): *above-*number my *iniquities* have-*surrounded-me*: — Who-knows *his errors*? — *Cleanse-*me from-*hidden ones*.

**(4) Very-often *sins-are so-*many** — that they-*escape one, — nor-can we-know-them, — without-which *nothing consecutive* to-*be-imposed*: — nay *example we-*have from-*Peter*, — who-*hardly one-of-his-*sins recognized: — and *Christ therefore-*specially-showed to *Cornelius*.

**(5) Not all-Church-*fathers acknowledged this-sort of-*confession**. In-*Canonic-*right of-*penitence *praise-*honored *Theodore of-Canterbury Bishop* says: *some-*teach that-*only-*God is-to-be-*confessed*. *Doctors of-*Greek, — *Glossator* (dist. 5 c. *in-*poeniteret) *this-*old-*Testament*, — but-not by *authority of-*church*.

**We-*conclude therefore**, — *auricular of-*all-and-single sins *enumeration* not-*to-be-required from-*true penitent, — and-from-*no-one to-be-*exacted: — praise it-is, — if-any *in-*general acknowledges, — himself-*seriously-*often against *law of-*God *manifoldly-*sinned; — if-however *singular-*some-*sin* itself-*presses in-*conscience, — *nothing prohibits*, — that opening-*it to-*minister-of-*church *consolation* he-*seek, — but that this be-*done, — from-*no-one *morosely* to-be-*exacted.

### Casus IV. Whether the minister of the word has the power of imposing satisfaction on the penitent

*Reply.* Even this-in-*churches of *Romanists usual is*, — who *many-*things dispute of *satisfactions*, — spontaneously *undertaken or-*imposed by-*priest: — which disputes may-*be-*seen in *Bellarmine* (lib. 4 *de-*poenit.).

**Of *satisfactions spontaneously undertaken*** we-*here-*treat not, — but only of-those, — which the-*priest imposes after-*confession: — and-that *certain-part-of-*penitence* they-*constitute, — of-which *Bellarmine* (lib. 4 *de-poenit*. c. 5).

**We-*concede however**, — true *penitence* also *these-*worthy-*fruits* to-*follow-*must (Matt 3:8), — and-that *certain-*and-*compensation-*of-somehow *for-*sins* — can-*be-*named, — not as-*sins* that-*way-*expiated, — or in *judgment-of-*God make-*satisfaction, — but-because *strictly-*repentance-*signs are*.

**In-*power however of-*minister** is-*not, — *satisfactions any impose on-*penitents (1) because through-*Christ already-*abundant satisfied it-is for-*sins and *punishments of-*sins*, — as-he-himself (Isa 53:5): *chastisement of-*our-*peace on-*him*.

**(2) Christ to-*ministers of-*church commanded to-*absolve believing from-*sins**, — no-*where however-*willed, — that *certain and-*definite of-*single sins *paying* — or by-*money, — or by-*works of-*satisfaction* from-*penitents to-*demand.

**(3) Is-*made by-*this reason *confusion*** *of legal and *evangelical*. For-*absolution from-*sins to-*legal-*part pertains, — whence true-*penitents *consolation* draw, — imposition of-*satisfactions to-*law pertains, — through-which as-*wound in-*flesh, — the *heart of-*penitent is-*again *contristated*.

**(4) *Absolution* is-of-*any kind*, — to-*which nothing does-*satisfaction imposed**: — for-if by *satisfactions understand-*good-*works divinely commanded, — those *spontaneously follow* after-*absolution in-*true penitents*, — nay it-is-*not needed, — that they-*be-imposed: — sufficient-*admonition, — that those whose-*sins are-already-*remitted, — henceforward *sinning cease*, — worthy-*fruits produce-*of-*penitence.

**But-if *ridiculous*-*things are-*instituted-*works** — as-*abstinence from-*cheese and-*butter, — *pilgrimages to *certain places*, — which-are-done with-*bare-feet, — and-*similar things in-*Papacy for *sacred-*things are-*commanded, — of-*no-*things are-*to-be-*had, — as-of-*absolution *cunning-*presented-*sanction *unworthy*.

**(5) *Satisfactions* either *peace and-*tranquillity of-*conscience take-*away**, — or *hypocrisy give-*birth-to: — for-*either penitent, — who by-*satisfaction they-*want, — always in-*doubt they-are-*left, — whether they-*have-compensated *reatus of-*owed-*punishment*, — and-thus to-*themselves-*never *satisfy*. Others in-*light *satisficinuis* rest, — which — because *priest imposed* — sufficient they-*think for-*taking-*away all *reatus*, — and-by-*this reason themselves-*multi-many *deceive*.

**Bellarmine opposes to-*satisfactions imposed** (1) saying-of-*Christ (Matt 18:18) — where keys-are-*given for-*loosing and-*binding: *in-*same manner sacerdotes penitents-*absolve, — thus-also can and-*ought them to-*penalties impose. But-*this objection is-of-*no-*moment, — nay sentence of *Jesuits utterly overturns*. If-*indeed penitents from-*sins are-*loosed, — why then-*imposed-*satisfactions again are-*bound? Nor-*ever-*did *Christ, — or *Apostles to-*penitents, — whom from-*sins absolved, — works-*satisfactorial imposed. — *Christ to-*paralytic said: *be-*of-good-cheer, — remitted are-*your-*sins* (Matt 9:2); — others *with-*peace *dismissed, — not-with-*punishments some *afflicted*: — disciples however in-*his name *penitence and-*remission of-*sins to-*announce, — *no-*satisfactions however to-*impose *commanded* (Luke 24:47).

**(2) Bellarmine urges *examples of-*fathers**, — who *commonly *satisfactions of-*this-*sort *preached*. — We-*do-*not-*deny, — fathers in *commendations of-*satisfactions often-*to-be-*excessive-*were, — chiefly in-*homilies, — where *rhetoricize themselves*: — much however-*differed *their satisfactions from-*satisfactions of-*Papacy*: — those *make-*satisfaction to-*church only, — which *part-of-*ecclesiastical discipline, — of-which-*we-*later say-*more chap. 42. — These however-*also *satisfaction to-*God* are-said-*to-*make for-*sins and-*their-*punishments. — Those required *good works* even *in-*law of-*God commanded*; — these *works often *ridiculous*, — and-*by-men invented*, — as *hair-shirt, — fasting, — pilgrimage*, — etc. — Those *were imposed to-*establish of-*true and-*serious penitence*, — that scandalous of-*church were-*averted, — that other from-*scandalous made were, — this-way be-*deterred: — these however to-*tribunal of-*God are-*referred, — that-*before-*absolution: — these follow: — and-*others are-*differences, — which see in *Chemnitz* (part. 2 *examinis Concilii Tridentini* cap. de satisfaction.).

**On-*these therefore-*causes *minister-of-*Church** is-*not bound to-*burden penitents with-*satisfactions, — to-*admonish them-*sufficient is, — that they-*give *signs of-*true emendation*, — and-*worthy-*fruits of-*penitence *produce*. If-*however some *more-*grave crime in-*any find, — with-*him before *absolution ecclesiastical-*discipline* is-*to-*proceed, — of-*which-*more later.

### Casus V. Whether the minister of the Church may accept something from the confessor

*Reply.* Even if in-*some places this-*plainly-*not permitted-*is, — nothing however in-*itself has of-*impiety or-*injustice. From-*no-one is-*exacted, — as *debt*, — nor-*from-that-*of-*someone denying therefore is-*upset-*ipso: — but *spontaneously offered is-*accepted, — not as *price of-*absolution*, — but as-*such-*whatever *compensation of-*labors in *ministry* — and-as-*sign of-*grateful animus of-*hearers toward *pastor of-*themselves*.

**General indeed *rule is-of-*Apostle**: *let-*him-*communicate the-*hearer of-*word, — with-him who-*catechizes, — in-*all *good* (Gal 6:6). — And-*it-*is-*proper *hearers*, — for-*doctors of-*themselves to-*provide *honest sustentation*. *Worthy indeed *worker is-*of-*his-*hire* (Luke 10:7), — and *the-*Lord ordained* — says *Paul* — *that they-*who preach *the-*Gospel from-*Gospel live* (1 Cor 9:14).

### Casus XI. What is-*to-*be-*done with *excommunicated *penitence-*doing? — and-*how into *church *received-*must

*Reply.* Above we-*have-*said, — *end of-*excommunication is-*not *interitum, — but *conversion of-*sinner: — therefore *Paul* of-*incestuous *excommunicated *writes: *sufficient to-*him *repraise this, — which is *from-*more* (2 Cor 2:6), — and-*exhorts *Corinthians, — *pardon him, — lest by-*chance *abundant-*more *sadness *absorbed-*be* (v. 7), — adds *himself-*also-*to-*him already *pardoned, — in-*person of-*Christ, — lest *pre-*occupied *he-*be by-*Satan* (v. 10-11). — Persuades therefore *this-*sort-of-*man *restitution into-*whole, — or *reception into *church.

**In-*that *however-*genre *anciently *many *observed-*were *grades**, — of-*whose *five *established-*are in *Synod-*of-*Antiochene:

**Second was *ἀκρόασις***, — when within *thresholds of-*temple *admitted *stood in *fixed *place, — after *catechumens, — that *would-*attend to *listening of-*word.

**Third was *γενυκλισίς***, — when *penitents into *sight of-*church *led-*were.

**Fifth *μέθεξις*** — when-*they with *others to *sacred *communion *admitted-*were. Of *similar *procedure *read *History Tripartita* lib. 9 c. 35.

**Today, — where *many-*modes *relaxed-*is *severity of-*ecclesiastical *discipline** — a-*little-*otherwise in-*receiving *penitents *proceeded-*is, — of-*which *matter *let-*consulted-*be *constitution ecclesiastical of-*Electorate *Saxonici *article-*general 11 fol. 32.

**Summary is-*this**: — when *manifest *signs of-*penitence *appear, — *pastor this *indicates *ministry; — to-*which *called *excommunicated *delict-*his *ingenuously *confesses, — *just *himself *punished *acknowledges, — *absolution and *restitution *submissively *asks, — and-*purpose of-*emending-*life *public-*and *deprecation *serious *promises.

**Which-*done *pastor *excommunicated some *day *Dominical to *temple *calls**, — there-*and-*in-*peculiar *place *knees *bends, — as-*publicly *deprecatur-*about-to-*be.

**Pastor to-*people *signifies**, — *man *before from-*church *cut-*is *seriously *acknowledge and *deprecate *delict, — and-*that into-*bosom of-*church *received-*is, — humbly *asks. Since *therefore *consistory *judged-*hath, — him-*receivable to-*be, — *exhorts-*self *people, — that *penitent *this *sinner *pardon, — and *serious for-*him *pray, — that *God chiefly in-*grace him *receive, — and-*to-*us far to-*be-*commanded.

**Then *pastor to-*excommunicated *customary of-*confession *formula *reads**, — from *sins *absolves, — and-*to *sacred *σύναξιν* one *with *others *communicating, — *admits.

**These *all however *sermon to-*this *action *fit, — *premises**, — partly *legal about *wrath of-*God against-*atrociously *delinquents, — and-*in-*sins *pertinaciously *perseverants; — partly *evangelical, — of-*gratuitous *remission of-*sins and-*mercy of-*God, — for-*all *seriously *penitent *to-*be-*expected.

## Chapter XI. Cases of Conscience concerning Decorum and Order in the Church

*De casibus conscientiae circa decorum ac ordinem in ecclesia.*

### Preamble

To the office of the minister of the Church pertains also to observe a *decent order in sacred things*; — for those things which *in their own place and time are done, — well are done*: — for which cause *D. Paul* admonished — *Let all things be done decently and in order.* (1 Cor 14:40), — *with decorum and order*. — Decorum is opposed to *levity*; — order to *confusion*. — No levity, — no confusion is to be borne in the house of God, — of which the minister of the word is another steward.

**Order is God's ordinance.** *God* — says *Gregory Nazianzen* (orat. 32) — *has constituted and bound all things: — order contains heavenly and earthly things: — order in those things which by reason and mind are understood, holds place: — order in those things which by senses are perceived: — order in angels, order in the motions of the stars, — magnitudes, — mutual relation and splendor* etc. *Order in the Church also constitutes, — so that some are sheep, — others pastors, — some preside, — others are subject, — some obey: — some as it were are the head, — others feet, — others hands, — others eyes, — some some other member of body for the whole Church's fitness and utility, — either inferior or more excellent*.

**Order here regards chiefly *rites of the Church* in sacred offices**, — in which there ought to be no scandal, — no confusion.

Concerning this part of the ecclesiastical function also one and another doubt occurs, — of which now with the Lord's assent — briefly we shall treat.

### Casus I. Whether the minister of the Church can at his own arbitrary change the *ceremonies of the Church*

*Reply.* Divine worship cannot be without *ceremonies*, — although ceremonies are not part of the worship, — but only certain *helps and ornaments* of it, — as when in *sermon a white vestment* is used or omitted; — in the administration of baptism *sprinkling* is made or *immersion*; — in the use of the *Lord's Supper* bread is broken or not broken, — *hosts* — which they call — are used, or bread in other form; — sung is in the German or Latin language, — in *figural music* or *choral*, — and many things of this genus.

**Concerning these Augustine's rule is to be observed** (epist. 118): *in matters which are used in the Church, — which are not against the faith, — nor against good morals, — but have some exhortation of a better life, — wheresoever pious we see, — or if we know them instituted, — not only not disapprove but even praise, — with imitation embrace, — if any others' infirmity does not so impede, — that more damage be*.

**But you find some pastors**, — who to themselves make it a matter of praise, — and put in it part of their authority, — if they change in the church their rites — which anciently had been in use, — introducing new ones, — either because elsewhere they have seen thus used, — or because they themselves wish to appear to have invented something new.

**These I prove to gravely sin thus:** **(1) They are not lords, — but *ministers of the Church***, according to the Apostle's saying (2 Cor 1:24): *we do not lord it over your faith*: — therefore with them it is not, — with new and unusual rites to impose a new yoke on the Church.

**(2) What touches all**, — from all also worthily is treated. — If therefore in rites, — with which the whole Church should use, — something to be changed is judged, — worthily be this with consent of all Church-orders.

**(3) What once pleased the whole Church**, — and long quietly were used, — not without temerity by one are changed, — since it is uncertain whether that change with equal tranquillity can be tolerated: — for according to *Nehemiah*'s saying — *every change is perilous*.

**Add that this sudden change** by one man's instinct is done, — not lacking scandal. — For as *Augustine* speaks (epist. 118 ad Ianuar.): *the very mutation of custom, which by utility helps, — by novelty perturbs: — which if for perturbation is unfruitful, — often is noxious*.

**Wherefore what against good morals**, — or against faith is not, — nor easily one man corrected, — but what he shall find in some Church, — that let him retain: — every novelty is suspect.

**Where the use of *white vestments* is for sermon**, — let the minister himself also use them, — who has newly come; — thus and in the use of *hosts* and of *choral or figural song*, — of *certain wax candles* in the use of the sacred Supper and similar things which have nothing of either impiety or scandal. — *Total this genus* — says *Augustine* — *free-observations has, — nor discipline is any in this better with grave prudence-both of-Christian, — than that in which manner acts, — you-see acting-himself, — to-which any place you-come*.

**It can however happen** — that *change of some rites* be necessary — **(1) when the rite labors with manifest impiety**, — as is *religious veneration of images and statues*, — *processions with the sacrament*, — *rosaries*, and similar things. **(2) When the rite conflicts with the articles of the faith**, — or with the ordination of God, — as is done in the *sacrifice of the Mass*, — and in the mutation of *sacramental symbols*. **(3) When the rite is *superstitious***, — as is the *consecration of foods, — of waters, — of wax candles*, — which have nothing of utility, — but of superstition, — and on the side of *impiety much*. **(4) When the rite conflicts with Christian liberty**, — which is done, — when what by itself is *indifferent*, — is obtruded as necessary, — that in no way can be changed, — this is against the nature of rites, — which even if not temerariously to be changed, — in themselves however are *free observations*, — which — when it seems for the matter of the Church, — and consent of all orders has acceded — can be changed. **(5) When the rite our conscience or of neighbor either wounds or burdens**, — as it happens, — when rites bear some species-before-themselves, — or by which (for fleeing persecution) is simulated, — as if our religion from *Papacy* were not much distant, — or certainly as if our mind from it not much abhorred.

**In all these things the faithful minister of the Church** ought to instruct his hearers diligently, — and how by many modes the change of that rite may be necessary and useful, — admonish, — and that all orders about abrogation or change should consider, — exhort ought; — but he alone and by *private daring* should not do this: — for if from solid foundations he goes, — applauders of his sentence, — who to abrogation consent, — easily he shall find.

### Casus II. Whether at the mandate of the magistrate the minister of the Church must immediately consent to the change or introduction of some ecclesiastical rite

*Reply.* In the manner in which the minister of the Word can change nothing in ecclesiastical ceremonies at his own arbitrary: — thus neither the magistrate alone, — or with a few others, — to obtrude new rites on the Church, — especially impious and superstitious ones, — ought. For the *magistrate* also is not *Lord of the Church*, — but a *member*; — and through the word of God is he governed, — as others: — therefore orthodox have always resisted such magistrate, — who wished to bind the Church to his mandates, — of which weight was conscience-heavy, — as *Athanasius* had it, — as *Constantius, Valentinian*, and similar contradicted, — of which within the memory of our fathers, — under the time of the pious *Interim* under *Charles V*, — is chosen.

**Well this understood pious *kings in the people of God***, — like *Joshua, Solomon, Josaphat, Ezekias, Josiah*, and similar, — who taking up *reformation of the Church*, — did not themselves prescribe for command, — whatever seemed to themselves, — but common counsels held, — and with *counsel and consent of all orders of the state*, — which they were of the Church, — concluded, — as is clear from Josh 24, 1 Chr 14 [15?], 1 Sam 7, 1 Chr 18 [19?], 2 Chr 30 and 34.

**On the contrary there are not lacking examples of other princes**, — who, — when at pleasure they changed ceremonies not without scandal of the people, — most grave they incurred punishments, — as the example of *Gideon* attests, — making an *ephod of linen*, — and instituting *private worship in his father's house* (Judg 8). — *Saul* who sacrificed against the prohibition of the Prophet *Samuel* (1 Sam 15). — *Ozias* the king, — who *burned incense* against the prohibition of the priests (2 Chr 26). — *Ahaz* — who removed the altar of the Lord and-in-its-place substituted the *Damascene altar* and-*worshiped-it*, not without species of idolatry (2 Kgs 16:14-15). — *Jeroboam* electing priests from the most contemptible of the people, — and instituting a *hitherto-unheard-of feast* (1 Kgs 12). All these on account of these *sins gravely were punished*; — into which punishments *zeal-of-novelty* into it cast them.

**On-account-of which cause, — useful and-well-nigh necessary it-*is**, — that, — when some change of rites is-to-be-undertaken, — it-*is-attempted neither by-the-ministry alone, nor by-the-magistrate alone, — but with-*ecclesiastical *orders convoked, — deliberations on-that matter are-*to-be-instituted, — in-the-manner *the-Apostles-*themselves, — pious-*Emperors, *Constantine-*the-Great, — later *Theodosius, Marcianus, Charles-*the-Great, and-*similar in religion-*negotiations *councils convoked, — nothing however for-*proper *of-conscience through-*novelties those *snare *inserted.

**On the contrary, — when the-*decrees of-Council *Tridentini, — which about *religion and-*ceremonies immutation-of-*Church-*German to-*obtrude wished, — were-*published**, — the-*Electors, princes, and-*orders-of-*Empire *Augsburg *Confession embraced, — publicly by-*writing opposed in-*year 1563, — indicating most-grave *reasons, why-*that Council neither *acknowledge nor *approach *want*.

**If however the magistrate through abuse of his authority** violently introduces new rites, — no-one is-*bound to-*observe them: — but those innovations humanely are-*to-be-*refused, — and in-*the-matter-*itself is-*to-be-*attested: — that we *God *more, — than *men-*ought to-*obey.

### Casus III. Whether in-*favor of-*adversaries anything in-*used *rites may-*be-*changed with-*good conscience for-*tranquillity of-*Church-*preservation

*Reply.* Much *agitated was-*once this-*question at-*time of-*Interim*, — where *Charles V* Emperor *some ceremonies already-*long-*ago in *Augustan *Confession *churches *abrogated, — *re-integrated *wanted: — in which-*genre of-*Caesar *some *thought *bowing was-*to-be-*done, — provided-*only *religion *in *chief *of-*doctrine-*Christian *chapters *safe and-*sound *left-*would, — which else *easily *jacture *would-*bear, — if-*not-*bowed-*would. Question-*indeed was-*then only about *rites, — in-*themselves *indifferent, — about *linen *vestment, — about *wax-*candles, — about *abstinence from *flesh, — about *use of-*salt in-*baptism, — about *feasts and-*similar, — in-*which *sufficient *thought to-*yield to-*adversaries, — especially *Caesar *commanding, — than *whole religion *periclitari.

**Others however to-*this-*opinion *masculine *opposed**, — persuading, — even *in-*these adiaphoris not-*even *smallest to-*be-*yielded, — because *question is-*not *only about *adiaphora those, — but about *chief *article of-*faith, — namely about *liberty of-*Christian, — which even in *adiaphora *yoke *imposes *consciences. Nor-*even *question is of-*mere adiaphora, — but *under this *name also-*many *articles of-*faith, — which without-*safety of-*piety *nothing *orthodox to-*adversaries *yield-*can, — *were-*contained, — as of *iustification, — of *reinstitution *Massae, — of *seven *sacraments, — and-*similar: — where *certainly *many *more-*meticulous, — *fearing *wrath of-*Caesar, — too-*much *conceded, — as *Synodica acta *Leipsii *year 1549 *edited *testify: — which *later *occasion *gave for *scandalous *σχίσματος among *Theologians of-*Augustanae *Confessionis, — where *many for *liberty of-*Christian against *impious *that *of-*some *meticulosorum *concession, — with-*reasons *solid *contended.

**Renovated *was *later this *disputation at-*time of-*Calvinismi**, — where *ceremonies *many by *Calvinists *were-*abrogated, — as *exorcism, use of-*hosts, *images in-*temples, — and-*similar, — and-*that *others, safe *articles of-*faith into *this-*sort of-*abrogation *consent, — was-*postulated.

**Whence-*same *question is in-*general *moved as-*much by *Papists as by *Calvinists**: — *whether at-*time of-*persecution and-*edenda *confession in-*mutation of-*rites *used to-*yield-*is to *adversaries*?

**Question this *treats *Formula Concordiae**, — and-*into *part *denying *concedes in-*Epitome, — with-*these words: *we-*believe, teach, and-*confess, — that *at-*times of-*persecutions, — when *perspicuous and-*constant *confession from-*us is-*demanded from *enemies of-*Gospel, — in *matters *adiaphoris not-*is-*to-be-*yielded*.

**Reasons of-*this *assertion these are**: **(1) *God *must-*be-*obeyed to-*mandate** (Deut 12): *God however-*mandated, — that *what *necessary *are, — *rites of-*church not-*are *necessary. — If therefore *rite of-*any *abrogation *or *usurpation is-*urged as *necessary, — then *made-*is *addition to *mandate of-*God in *word *prohibited: — and-*therefore *obligate *me *cannot, — nor *conceded *of-*that *anything.

**(2) *Repugns *this *concession to *liberty *Christian**, — from-*which *he who *rite of-*any *immutation *urges as *necessary, — *yoke of-*servitude *makes; — *forbids however-*this *Apostolic *Paul* (Gal 5:1): *stand in *liberty, — with-*which *Christ *you *freed, — nor-*again *yoke of-*servitude *subject-*yourselves*: — and-*this-*admonition *himself-*by-*example-*his-*approved. — For when *false *brothers *urged *circumcision of-*Titus, — to-*explore *liberty, — which he-*had in-*Christ, — that him into *servitude *reduce, — not to *hour *yield-*wished (Gal 2:5), — even-*if *earlier *Timothy *circumcised had (Acts 16:3).

**(3) *Authentic is-*Apostle *Paul's* (2 Cor 6:14)**: *do-*not-*carry *yoke with *unfaithful, — what indeed *participation *justice with-*iniquity? — Do-*not-*join with-*yourselves in-*fruitless *works of-*darkness, but *rather *reprove-*them*. — This however *do, — whoever *enemies and-*persecutors of-*truth, — whether in-*abrogating *ceremonies, — whether in-*receiving *already-*long *abrogated, — in-*whatever-*mode *they-*yield.

**(4) *Concession in-*abrogating *pious *ceremonies**, — or in-*receiving *already *abrogated, — *conflicts with *truth *evangelical, — in-*which *us *stand *commands *Apostle* (Gal 2:5). — For *consciences not in-*their *liberty *left, — but by *shameful *yoke of-*servitude *burdens, — and-*with *simulation *conjoined *is, — while in-*grace of-*adversaries *made-*is, — who-*under-*this *cover of-*meliorization *impious *doctrine into *church-*brought-*strive, — with *yielding this *not-*only *not-*hindered, — but *rather *helped.

**(5) *Concession this *fights also with *confession of-*doctrine *orthodox***, — which from-*all *required-*is. — For while *yield-*they to-*adversaries of-*Gospel, — no-one *easily *understands, — whether with *adversaries in-*religion *consent or *not? — *Christ however-*requires from-*his *open *before *men *confession* (Matt 10:32).

**(6) Who *yield-*they in-*this-*genus to-*adversaries**, — those by-*this-*itself in-*impiety-*their *confirm, — and to *persecution of-*church *animos-*their *add, — with-*contrary, — if with-*animos-*of-*resistance *resisted-*they, — evil *this *avert *could.

**(7) *Concession this *not-*lacks *suspicion of-*collusion, — chiefly among *simpler**, — who-*greatly *offended-*are, — and-*doubt of-*religion *begin-*to. *Woe however-*him through-*whom *scandal *comes* (Matt 18:7).

**(8) *Accedes finally *authority of-*Luther***, — who in-*same *manner about *this-*question *disputes p. 3 Jenensis Germ. and-*his *example our *sentence *proved. — For when *elevation of-*bread in-*celebration of-*S. *Eucharist for-*some-*time in-*grace of-*infirmer *he-*retained, — and-*already of-*abrogating this-*rite *thought, — with *Carolstadius *interim and-*others *sacramentarii against *this-*rite *tumult-*making not-*even to-*hour *yield *wished, — but *rite *that *longer *retained, — lest in-*grace of-*adversaries *consciences, in-*matter *free, — *yoke *impose *seem: — For also *those things, — which by-*nature-*their-*own *are of-*free *observation, — in-*state of-*confession, — when from-*adversaries their *change *postulated-*is, — *become *necessary, — which *Paulus by-*example of-*circumcision *proved. — *Timothy indeed *circumcised, — when-*infirm on-*account of-*his *circumcision *omitted *were-*offended (Acts 16). — *Titum however-*not-*circumcised, — when *false *brothers *circumcision as-*necessary *urged* (Gal 2).

### Casus IV. Whether one should labor for *complete conformity of-*rites in all and-*single churches*

*Reply.* Uniformity of rites in the-*Church is *diversely from-*some *urged. From *Papists indeed as *necessary means of-*preserving *order in-*Church, — nay, — as-*certain *note of-*true Church. — Thus writes *Bellarmine* (lib. 2 *de-*sacramentis* c. 31): *if *liberty *were of-*ritual *observation, — no-*way *stand *could, — that *some *order and *uniformity in-*Church *served-*is*. And-*a-*little-*after: *Epiphanius* (says) *in-*end of-*books against-*heresies *reciting *ceremonies-*of-*Church, — that *indicate, — *some as-*if *notes, — with-*which *Church from-*all *seats *discerned-*is*.

**By others however is-*thought** — uniformity of-*rites in all *particular *churches much-*conducing to *consent in-*doctrine *conciliating.

**But *frustration in-*both about *conformity of-*all *ceremonies in-*every *church is-*labored**. — Distinguished-*must-*here-*be, — between *ceremonies *divine and-*human. — *Divine are, — which from *Christ and *Apostles *origin *have, — chiefly *around *Sacraments, — where *some are from *Christ *commanded, — as, — that *commands *baptize with-*water, — that *commands *manducare *bread, — and *drink *wine, — adding *prayers, — and *similar, — which from *words of-*institution known-*are. — And *these *ceremonies are-*called *necessary and *substantial* in *administration of-*Sacraments, — therefore *changed *cannot-*be, — but in *all *churches uniformly *are *retained-*to-*be, — because *are in *institution *prescribed. — *Some however-*have *Scripture *testimony, — that above-*all in *Church of-*Apostles *were-*usurped, — as *explications of-*doctrine of-*Sacraments, *exhortations, *prayers, *thanksgivings, *hymns, *singings, and-*similar. — *These also *retaining-*are, — thus-*however that *themselves-*doctrine be *conforming. Not indeed *are *Sacraments *as *spectacles-*instituted, — but *institutes, — that *faith *confirm and *promise *plainly *propose.

**Human ceremonies again of-*two genera-*are***: some *of-*old added to *substantials, — and *conform *either to-*word or *examples *external. — Ceremonies of-*word *are-*retained, — when *words of-*Scripture *added-*are *conform, — as-*when in *baptism *employed-*is *exorcism, — *abrenounced by *godparents *Satan, *interrogation and-*response, *confession-*of-*Symbol, — etc. Ceremonies of *thing *retained-*are, — as *bring-*ordinances of-*adiaphora *all, *free, — since-*nothing *have of-*impiety, — nor are *otiose *games, — but *serve *order and *decorum of-*church, — as-*same-*have *admonition, — and *edification of-*people. — Others however from *Papatu *originum *have and-*of-*superstition-*full-*are, — as *many *impious, with-*which *Sacraments of-*Christ into *other are-*transformed *action, — as it-*is in *Mass *Papistical: — hither *pertain *paschal-*candle, *consumption of-*salt, *commixture of-*water with-*wine, *consecration of-*water *baptismal, *unguent, *candles, and *of-*this-*genus *other *many, — which neither *mandate nor *example in *sacred *Scripture *have, — and-*which *not-*only, — as *significations or *admonitions *retained-*serve, — but truly *efficacy *some *peculiar to-*them *attributed. — Such *ceremonies, — although *some *of-*them *testimony of-*antiquity *have-*seem, — for *superstition however and *impiety, — into *which-*today *degenerated, — from *churches *eliminated-*are, — with-*else *rite of-*church *pure *not-*is *proponible.

**Made-*however *this *emendation *free-*is-*indeed, — but *not so, — as by-*any *private**, — nor by-*pastor, or *magistrate alone, — but with *consenting all *church-*orders, — for *peril of-*schism: — with-*informed also-*church for *pulpit of-*causes of-*emendation, — lest *precipitately *action *seem.

**As to-*difference of-*rites of-*human, — which in-*every *church *instituted-*is**, — of-*that *not is-*to-be-*strived, — since *matter neither *necessary is, — nor *useful. Unity indeed of-*church *not-*consists in *unity of-*rites, — but *doctrine and *sacred-*rites. Nor *ever *damned *are *any-*church for *diversity of-*ceremonies: — but *free *were-*of-*those *observations, — with *some *fasting, *some *not, — as *pre-*tasting of-*milk, of-*honey and-*wine etc.: — same, — that *some *fast on-*Sabbath, *some *not-*fast: — that *some *communicate *daily-*to-*body and-*blood *Dominical, — others *certain *days *receive: — and-*something-*else of-*this-*sort-*noted-*is.

**Total this *genus *free *observations-*is**, — nor *discipline of-*any *better with-*grave *and-*prudent-*Christian *is, — than, — that in-*that manner *act, — in-*which sees *acting-*self, — to-*which-*church any-*ever came.

**And *Formula Concordiae* art. 10 writes**: *we-*believe, teach, and-*confess, — that *church other other *damn *ought-*not, — for-*that *this or *that-*more *observation of-*external ceremonies, — which *Lord not *instituted, — *observes, — if in-*doctrine, and-*its *articles *all, — and in *true *use of-*Sacraments *consent-*be. — For this-*ancient and-*true said-*is: *dissonance of-*fasts *not-*dissolves *concord of-*faith*.

### Casus V. Whether the minister of the Church addicted to false religion, — if from error he-*passes to *the-*orthodox faith, — should-*be-*accompanied to *sepulcher-*just-*as *other *orthodox

*Reply.* To *order in-*church *pertains also *sepulture of-*men, — of-*whose *care above-*all-*is with *ministry. — And-*even if-*according-*to *Augustine's* saying (lib. 1 *de-*civit. DEI* c. 12): *care of-*funerals, — and *pomp of-*obsequies *more *are of-*solace of-*living, — than of-*sustentation of-*dead-*prayers, — *honest however-*sepulture is *witness of-*departed, — that *were *true of-*church-*ours *members, — in *unity of-*faith to-*us *conjoined, — and-*same in *Christ *resurrection to-*life *eternal to-*us with *expecting-*is: — for-*which *end *of-*old *patriarchs and *pious *kings to *fathers of-*themselves *collected *demanded, — with-*whom in *unity of-*faith *lived.

**Thence *follows**, — that, — who *confessors of-*true doctrine, — which in *churches-*our-*sounds, — not are, — but *rather *hostile of-*it, — and *persecutors, — *honest even *among *ours *not *to-*be-*buried are.
