## Chapter XII. Cases of Conscience concerning the Political Magistrate

*De casibus conscientiae circa magistratum politicum.*

### Preamble

The *second hierarchy* concerns the *political magistrate*, who agrees with the ministry in many things, but differs in most on account of the diversity of objects — of which the one treats *sacred matters*, the other *civil*.

The magistrate is one of the most-ancient ordinations of God, — which, if man had persisted in the state of integrity, — would then have had its place. — For even if then there were only two men in the world, — who, on account of the narrowness of family, had no need of political power: — nevertheless if human society had been fuller, — on account of the order necessary in every society, — some *head* would have been needed, — to whom the rest of men, without any molesting, — would have been subject in *friendly association* — in the manner in which among angels also there is order of *archangels and angels*, — and among spouses in the state of innocence the man would have been *head of the wife*, — without all *despotic dominion* or *servile subjection*.

**In the manner in which not of anyone it is** to bear magistracy, — for to not all is it given, — either to command others in the *due mode*, — or to devour all the molestations of subjects; — whence commonly it is said: *magistratus ostendit virum* [magistracy shows the man]: — thus the praxis of this office does not lack difficulty, — which those experience who wish to run this course with unstained conscience.

Of these things therefore which can arm the conscience of the magistrate and of subjects, in this chapter, — with the Lord willing, — we shall treat.

### Casus I. Whether one can with good conscience desire and undertake the magistracy

*Reply.* Absolutely, — for the following reasons:

**(1) Because God himself acknowledges himself author and preserver of this ordinance**, — not only permitting kings to be adorned with title of God, — as at 1 Chr 29:23; 1 Sam 8:8, and passim elsewhere; — but also attributing empire of the magistrate to himself: *By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.* (Prov 8:15). *There is no power except from God* (Rom 13:1). *Hear, kings, from the Lord to you is given judgment* (Wis 6:1). — Moreover, that magistrates be established, God mandates and communicates his name with the magistrate: *I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.* (Ps 82:6), — nay whatever tends to God's displeasing.

**(2) Because great anarchy follows from defect of magistrate**, as it is written (Prov 11:14): *where no governor is, the people falls*; and in the time of the Judges, — since there was no king in the people of God, — *each did what seemed right in his own eyes* (Judg 17:6; 21:25).

**(3) Without magistrate neither church nor ministry would be preserved pure**, — therefore God preserves magistrate and political order, — that the Church may have tranquil *halcyon-days*, — whence also kings are called *nurses of the Church* (Isa 49:23).

**(4) Without magistrate no Church would flourish**, — no laws would be vigorous; — as in a great river smaller fishes are devoured by greater, — so in the world *the more-powerful would suppress the weaker*.

**(5) Without magistrate no distinction between men would be**, — no public safety; — therefore *Beatus Luther* writes on Gen 2: *political and economic-life is necessary to us — as bread and water*. — And *Paul* commands us to pray for every magistrate, — that under him we may lead a *quiet and tranquil life* (1 Tim 2:2).

**(6) Scripture attests to holy and glorious men who dominated in their powers, and had empire over the people** (Sir 44:3).

**(7) Not to mention *examples of holy men*, who were kings, princes, generals and judges**, — like *Abraham* (Gen 14:14), *Joseph* (Gen 41:43; 42:6), *Moses* (Exod 7:1), *Joshua* (Josh 1:2), *David* (1 Sam 16:13), *Solomon* (1 Chr 29:23), and other similar ones, of whom that whole cloud (Heb 11:32-33) commends.

Certain therefore it is, — the magistracy is a *holy office*, — *conceded to the pious*, — *necessary to the Republic*, — *divinely ordained*.

**But the holier and more useful something is**, — the more it usually has adversaries. — So the magistracy has contradictors *Manichaeans*, *Photinians*, and *Anabaptists*, — even to this day. — Of whom some do not indeed deny the necessity of magistrate among Christians, — but the office of the magistrate — that is, to govern well, to decide causes, to strike malefactors with the sword, to hold public judgments, and similar things, — to no Christian they concede: — others transmit the magistracy itself as *human invention*: — since indeed they see man by nature more inclined to dominate than to obey, — many vices they think are in the magistrate, — like tyranny, pride, ambition, violence, avarice, unmercifulness, — they think the magistracy not of God but of the devil.

**But here always the *vices of the magistrate* must be distinguished from the *office*** — because always he is going to abuse of the ordinance-worst. And so therefore *tyranny and injustice of the magistrate are not of God, — yet the magistrate himself, — even if a tyrant, is from God*, — who even permits bad princes to reign on account of the sins of the people, — as it is said in the Prophet: *I gave thee a king in mine anger, and took him away in my wrath.* (Hos 13:11).

**Some think magistracy is from God only through permission**, — like no evil in the city is without God, but by permission and punishment of men's sins. To which thoughts must be opposed that Apostle: *the powers that be are ordained of God* (Rom 13:1); — God therefore *justly* ordained and constituted man; but what are ordained by God, less rightly are said to be only permitted, — since permission is only of things that displease and are disapproved, — as God is said to permit sins, — which he neither wills nor approves: — but ordination is of those things which he has willed and approved.

All these strongly confirm the magistracy, — that it is in-general a life pleasing to God and useful, — since God orders nothing that he does not approve — and knows to lead to the human race.

### Casus II. What should we believe: is the power of the political magistrate to depend on the Roman Pontiff, as though a *lieutenant* of Christ

*Reply.* If we follow the leader of sacred letters, — the decision of this question is easy. For she nowhere shows that Peter has power over secular princes; — nor therefore does their power depend on the Pope. — For as *Bernard* excellently teaches (*De consid.* to Pope Eugene): *ecclesiastical and political power are by divine right so distinct and separated, — that each enclosed in its own bounds, — cannot with its own right invade the terms of the other, nor of both empire in the other*.

**In the Papacy however this question found various opinions**, — which nothing else at present than to render it doubtful, perplexed, and uncertain. — One is of *the canonists*, who either from ambition, — or from *love of gratitude* toward the benefits of the Pontifices — from whom they knew themselves oppressed, — or because they aspired to greater or similar goods, — did not fear terrestrial to Roman Pontifex the fullest power *not-only in spiritualibus, but in-summa mundi capita, principes, dukes, kings, ipsum even Emperor and all kingdoms of the world* attributed, — so that himself, — as *supreme lord of the world*, — kingdoms and principalities, — *to whomever and when he wishes*, — could give or take away, — although no one knows the cause, why he acts thus, — perhaps according to that: *he to whom all is given*, — has no reason.

This opinion is followed by *Alvarus Pelagius* (lib. 1 *de planctu eccl.* c. 13), *Panormitanus* on c. *Novit de iudiciis*, *Silvester in summa* verb. *Papa* § 2, and others whom *Bellarmine* recounts (lib. 5 *de Papa* c. 1).

**To these have been-adjoined more-recent some**, — among whom excels above others *Franciscus Bozius* of the congregation *oratoria* presbyter, — who many for that opinion motives-brings (lib. 1 *de temporali ecclesiae monarchia*) — where perversely-turning-all-things — he extends: *every royal force, — of all things which in the-earth are power and domain given is by the great Pontiff to be-vindicated, — which as-if Sejanum, — the-brother of the friend, — the very Sun, — will-defend the-things itself* etc. — All-these will be false, — if from *the sole God's power alone* the political depended: — for they-would-have some superior after God, — who himself both to-coerce and to-subject to his-own-laws could subdue at-pleasure.

**Old therefore against these opinion of *canonists* even more-ancient was error of *Ostiensis*** (in *summa*), who first with this new and unheard-of opinion — *cardinal-hats* to man peer-full-of-glory-desire-full — no-less than-with new torches of-ambition — beyond-measure inflamed appears to-have.

**Read also in the sanctions of *Boniface VIII*** that *the temporal sword is under the spiritual*, — because as-the *Apostle* says (Rom 13:1): *there is no power except from God: — the powers however that are, — from God ordained are: — not however ordained-would-be, — unless the sword were under the sword* (see in *Clementinis* lib. 2 tit. 9 *de maioritate* and in *extravag. Bonifacii* VIII *unam sanctam*).

**In the manner in which this opinion made many *Popes bloody***, — thus it much harmed many emperors, kings, and princes, — whom that, which the *Papa* to himself fashioned, — power made-tributaries-of-kings, — dissolved-subjects-with-oath-of-fidelity, — and cast-into-most-extreme miseries: — reciprocally however to the *Papacy itself* through defection of many from that tyranny inflicted-not-a-little detriment, — as *Marsilius* in preface of *libellum* against *Papam Iohannem XXII* wrote: *see, most-serene father, — how expedient it-is for the church, that empire be-defended, — which as-Sejan, — the-brother of-the-*of-the-friend, — those-things, and-lest that-opinion be avoided, uses two machines: — one is, — because *Peter* and the-remaining Apostles at that time had no right over any private subject, — much less over the magistrate, — nay to the ethnic magistrate itself they-were-subject: — Christ indeed did not come — of-nature or of-nations rights to-take-away, — or to-strip anyone of temporal dominion of-his-own-things. — But not thus is-it, — that the *Papa* now has greater power over Christian political princes, — than at-that-time *Peter* over any private-person. — The other reason is, — because none of the ancients this power of-the-*Papacy* has-made-mention; — much less did *Gregory the Great*, — who was so eminent, — a man with-*sanctity* and-*zeal-for-*governing-the-church burning, — used-that-power over heretical emperors, — whose-thing-however he-had frequent occasions convenient: — nay rather, — whatever anyone in-*doctrine* and-*holiness* excelled, — the-more he-was subject to the Emperor, — and-observant of-him, — as *subject and servant-of-him*, — as *Gregory* to Emperor *Mauritius*: *your-servant to your piety* (lib. 2 *Ep.* 61).

**Bellarmine (lib. 5 c. 1)** exhausts himself in refutation of this error. First he teaches (c. 2 *de R. P.*) *the Papa is-not Lord of the-whole world*: (1) with-*authority* of *Iohannis de Turrecremata* (lib. *summae* c. 3) *the Papa cannot judge infidels*. — And-to *ejusdem dictum* of *Apostle* (1 Cor 5:12): *what to me of-those-outside to-judge?* (3) because *infidel princes* are-only truly-supreme princes in their-own-kingdoms. — (4) Because *dominium* is-not-founded on *grace* or on *faith*, but on *free-will* and *reason*, — and-*descends-not from divine-right, but from *right-of-nations*. — Further he-teaches (c. 2) that the Papa is-not Lord of-whole *Christian world*. — (5) Because *nothing on-that-matter is-clear from-Scriptures*, — nor from *tradition of-Apostles*. — (2) Because *Christ did not come to-destroy or to-take-away *kingdoms of-those*, — to-whom divinely they-were-given: — but rather them he-*perfects*, — when-indeed *some king infidel becomes Christian*. — (3) Because *bishops are-not Lords of-cities*, of-which they-are-bishops. — But as-*Papa is in-*church universal, that-is any bishop-in-particular. — (4) Adduces testimonies some of-Popes, who this-opinion contradict, — as of *Leo*, of *Gelasius*, of *Gregory-the-Great*, of *Alexander III*, of *Nicholas III* etc. — Third he-teaches (c. 4) *the Papa has-no *temporal* jurisdiction directly *by divine right*, — because Christ himself was-not temporal king, — much-less the Papa, — chiefly-since he-not all-power has, — which had-Christ, — as mortal-man*.

**With these arguments themselves the *Jesuits* have-overturned** the first opinion of the *canonists* concerning the *temporal power* of the *Papa*, — which was *Canonistarum prima*.

**The other is of some Theologians**, whom in-great number *Bellarmine* recounts (lib. 5 c. 4), — among whom he himself-also names-himself. — It is-this: — that the Papa, — even-if he-has not merely temporal power directly, — nevertheless has it *indirectly in-order-to *spiritual-good*, — of-disposing about temporal things among Christians*: — in-the-manner in-which flesh and-spirit in-man are two as-it-were Republics having *diverse acts and-objects*: — flesh is-below, spirit presides: — and-although spirit does-not immix-itself with-all *actions of-flesh*, — but lets flesh exercise all its-actions, — like in-brutes it-exercises: — nevertheless when *from-office-of-*itself of *spirit*, — then spirit commands flesh, — chastises-it, — and-if needful is, — indicates *fasts, *afflictions, — also with-lessening and-*debilitation of the *body itself*, — forces tongue not to-speak, eyes not to-see: — this his (which he-calls of-*Theologians*) sentence with-these very-words proposes at-c. 6, — and-proves in-labor c. 7.

**But although this seems enough to-prove**, *Barclay* however with-many-most-solid-reasons impugned-it, — and to *Bellarmini* arguments has-responded (lib. 3 *De potestate Papa*) — up-to the end, — where (1) he-shows, — that *indirect that power of *Papa* by the-same-arguments can-be-refuted, — with-which *Bellarmini* himself judged direct one to-*conquer. — For his chief *conclusion against the direct power is-this*: — *If-can *supreme Pontifex* differ from *kings* and-*Emperors of-*power, — as *himself as supreme king or-Emperor*, — great can-be. — If *can*, therefore *is-greater than-Christ*. — If *not-can*, therefore *himself-not-truly *power *regal**. — Nothing matters, — that of-*indirect that power *Papa* the-same we-conclude: — for both *direct and indirect not in *faculty of-*judging*, — but only in-*mode of-acquiring temporal-power difference is-made.

(2) *Reasons of-*Bellarmini five, — with-which *indirect power of-*Papa in-temporal things to-prove he-tries, — prolifically responds *Barclay*. — To reason first (c. 15-16), to second (c. 17-19), to third (c. 20-23), to fourth (c. 24), to fifth (c. 25). — To this most-erudite work of *Barclay* I-refer hearers, — and-not lacking-them will-be *solid also of-second opinion refutation*.

**Third finally opinion is of-some in-*Papacy* politicians**, — who to-*Papa* indeed concede power in-*spiritual-things*, — but *no plainly in-*temporal-things, — among whom was once *Occam*, Franciscan monk, — *Marsilius Patavinus* (in *Defensore pacis*): — today however *Wilhelm Barclay* and *Ioannes Beckerus*, both Theologians and-Politicians *very-learned*, — to-whom, — as-to negation of *temporal power* fully we-subscribe, — even-in *spiritualibus* also *Papa* no-right in-*church have-relinquish.

**Truly *heresy* he-calls, to-say**, — that the *Roman Pontifex* by no *divine-right has temporal power*, — nor can in-any way command secular princes, — much less deprive them of kingdoms and principate, — if-else worthy of-that they-were.

**But this-very assertion**, which he *Bellarmine* holds for *heretical*, — rests on *solid foundations*: **(1) *heretical it-is that sentence***, — as we above showed, — where *directly* and-*indirectly* that power of *Papa* over secular princes in-*temporals* — we-refute directly.

**(2) *Kings and *princes have their-power from *God alone***, — according to that of-Apostle: *there is no power except from God* (Rom 13:1). — Therefore not lawful for *Roman Pontifex* — either to-say directly or indirectly, — that power and-empire, which kings and-princes divinely have, — to *human hazard* to-be-owed, — or to-be-transferred to-others.

**(3) The Papa, — even-if-maximally *vicar of-Christ* he-is**, — more indeed something he-could not, — than what from *Christ* as mortal-*man* he-*received. — With-*respect however to-*this-*neither *Christ himself either had *worldly kingdom*, — or *Emperors or *magistrates other, — even-*ethnic and-abusing-of-power-of-*themselves, ejected from throne, — but *himself to *magistrate subject was, — pay-tribute-Matt-17. *Give to *Caesar what-is *Caesar's, — to *God what-is-of *God* (Matt 22:21). — To-which certainly *argument much attributes *Bellarmine* in refuting *direct power* (c. 3): — why the same against *indirect* not-can-be, — nothing-hinders.

**(4) None-is of-*this-*sort-of-*temporal-power of-*Pontifices** either *use, or example, or mention, in-thousand-*years or-so in-*church*, — with meanwhile many Christian princes lived-impiously enough. — Verisimilar therefore *not is, ancient *pontiffs of-*church not-faithfully *presided: — but *follows *rather*, — them this power to-*themselves-not-*pertaining, — to-*have-acknowledged. — In-*following however times, — when from *superstition, *Papa as *successor of *Peter and-*vicar of-*Christ too-much was-honored, — and-*such to-him *sanctity was-attributed, — as-if *neither by-word, *nor by-deed *could-err, — (which-to-the-matter *flatteries of *canonists* with immoderate their-*praises meat-*sought, — much did) — *Papa more-*courageous *this with-great *swelling of-*pride to-*themselves-*claimed — that, which to-him *vulgus spontaneously gave, — and-*princes their-*kingdoms rather-*abandon *wished, — than *Pontifex angry, — and-*fulmen of-*excommunication on-*disobedient thundering, — as *enemy have: — whence all with-*internal seditions, and-public *incendio easily *filled could-*have-been. — *Had-therefore *Pontifices some in-*last centuries *temporal that *power over *secular princes, — which *no-one *to-them gave, — but they to-*themselves *seized, — and-which *none of-*earlier times *Pontifex *affected, — or *usurped: — *sole *God ancient *kings *from-*subjection to-*themselves *had-*subject, — *human *laws-only, — *no penalties temporal *subject or *coerce could. — Thus *Tertullian: *God alone (of-Emperors) *concerning I-*know, — to-whom *sole *pre-*after-*the-*first-*place is-*second*. *Ambrose (*de Nabot* c. 3): *Emperor withdraws himself if-*good*: — *David*: *unto-thee-alone I-*have-*sinned*, — since-indeed *king was-himself, — and-was-*subject to-no-one, — but to *God alone*. — *All these will-be-false*, — if from-*Papa alone their-*power *depended: — *would-have they *some *superior after *God, — who them and-*coerce and-*to-his-*laws at-*pleasure *subject *could.

**(5) *Add**, — that *some *Pontifices *confess: — *political-*king has-*no *superior in-*temporal-things, — as-*is in-*right *Canon* c. 4. — *Whence therefore is *that *power, — which *Pontifices to-*themselves in *political-*magistrate *usurp? — For what they-*say, this-only *indirectly to-*be-*done, — that *nothing-*diminishes, — but *rather it-*modifies: — for-also *he-who *directly-*acts *concerning *temporal-*power *princes *reduces, — some *superiority to-*self *arrogates.

**By-*these *causes therefore already-of-*old against *this-*sort-of-*power *Pontificum many were, — who to-*them-*only *subject-*themselves — but wished only in-*things spiritual: — those-*however *dishonored *cruelly *afflict the-*magistrate, — who *his-*power thus *subjects *himself of-*power of-*Papa, — that *this in-*that at-*pleasure *transfer *could: — this is-of-*those, — whom *Scripture calls *bond-*slaves of *Popes* (2 Pet 2:19).

### Casus III. Whether it is lawful to *infidel* or *heretical Emperors* to command Christians

*Reply.* We must here consider the age both of the Old and of the New Testament. Under the Old Testament *Iudaei* often had *ethnic magistrates*, — as under the Egyptians *Pharaoh* — under the *Assyrians Salmanassar* — the *Chaldeans Nabuchodonosor* — and-in-*hand of the *rebels of *Iabin king of *Canaan* (Judg 4). — Concerning whom the *Iudaei* — commanded to *sacrifice on-account-of *life of the *king* — to *pray* (Jer 29:7).

Under the New Testament also Christians for the most part had *ethnic magistrates*, — and yet were commanded to offer them *obedience and reverence*, tribute and *duty*, — nay to pour forth *prayers* for them (Matt 22:21; Rom 13:1; 1 Pet 2:13; 1 Tim 2:1-2).

**After Apostolic times also** the Church of God — kings *infidel and heretical* — trying to destroy — submissively bore, — not only for wrath, but also *for conscience' sake*: — not because in-force they were weak to resist them: — but because they knew that *God* required from anyone honor and obsequium *toward whatever magistrate*, — as *Constantius, Iulian* his successor, *Valens* and-others-of-*this-*kind tolerated the ancient Christians, — even-if then Christians had sufficient strength to repel them, — only because they were *magistrates*, — to whom if anyone resists, — he resists God's ordination.

**If therefore anyone lives under the yoke of a *tyrant***, — or under *Papist magistrate*, — or of another sect, — he does not deny obedience in those things which do not impugn religion or the faith of Christ: — but if he violates religion, and wishes to persuade *heresy* or *unfaithfulness*, — no one of the subjects consents to that: — nevertheless he-does-not renounce the magistrate on-that-account, — but in-those-things-which are-not against piety and honesty, — willingly subjects-himself, — praying for him, — that God even in religion-matters may-bend his soul, — lest anything harder in-that-name against subjects he-decree.

**Far otherwise on-this-matter is-taught in-Papacy.** For *Bellarmine* (lib. 5 *De Roman. Pontif.* c. 7) writes: *if the king from Christian became heretic, — or utter enemy of the Church, — he-*is not-permitted for-Christians *to-have-him for-king, — chiefly if peril subsist, — to-be-*drawn to *his heresy or unfaithfulness*.

Others, especially the *Jesuits* — chiefly *Mariana* (lib. 1 *De rege*) and *Suárez* (in *Def. fidei*) — teach that *heretics not-only not-*to-be-tolerated, — but in-*any-way, — by-force or fraud, — from-*midst to-be-taken-away, — if forsooth on-account-of *political dominion of-*them peril *life of-*souls, — turbulence of-*church, — jugum *of-*it violent — this their-*doctrine chiefly in *France and *England has-*confirmed *severely.

**Two therefore statutes against our assertion**: (1) *magistrate infidel* or *heretical* Christians to-command cannot, because him to-tolerate they-deny. (2) *Such magistrate*, — because it hinders the-*kingdom of *Papa*, — cruel slaughters to-take-away-from-*midst.

**Reply to-both.** Both (which you-may-wonder) from *Scripture affirm-*they seem. — To-*proof of first assertion — cites *Bellarmine*:

**(1) Deut 17** where the *people* forbidden to-choose king, — *who not-from *brothers thine-is, not foreign*, — namely lest *pertrahat *them to *idolatry*. — Therefore (says) *also *Christians *forbidden to-choose king not-*Christianum*.

**Reply.** Nothing this-*against us. — For if concerning *free-election through *votes it-*acts, — always *preferred is-to-be *faithful to-*infidel: — provided the-*rest-*gifts to-*kingdom-*necessary he-*have. — Because *religion and *unity of-*minds of-*magistrate and-of-*subjects all-*maximally and-*firmly *binds, — *disparity however of-many *suspicions, — *simultatum and-*diffidence *occasion is. — If *however *magistrate to-*some alien from-*true religion, — by-*right of-*suspicion according-to *laws-*fundamental and-*pacts-*agreed *transferred, — likewise on-account-of *religion-*diversity by-*right *tolerating is, — since the-*church does-not-abolish *politics or-*rights *human, — in-*which sentence-*with-*feet *transfers *Melanchthon* c. 10 art. 10.

**(2) Bellarmine cites** *of-*same peril and-*damage inflicts Christian *magistrate infidel to Christian, — as *conjunx-*fidelis to *unfaithful*, — and *however *fidel conjunx dismissed-can be by *infidel: therefore also *fidel people dismissed *can *magistrate *infidel*.

**Reply.** Not-is *the-same *right where-*the-*same is peril and-*damage: — for whether from *unjust invasion or from-*unjust *magistrate-*intention *both *damage-*receive, — the-*same is *damage, — but not-*the-*same *right. — For into *invasor manifest to-*rush lawful-*is: — into *magistrate however-*unjust not-*likewise, — on-account of-*office, which he-*bears, — of-*continuity. — If-therefore *the-*same *feared is-*peril and-*damage, — *if *magistrate *infidel or *heretical *already-*elected not-*deposed, — as-if not-*elected, — not-however *equivalent *magistrate *heretical *already-*elected *deposed is-to-*be, — because from-*just *causes *elected could — either on-*account of-*right of-*succession, which him *disparity of-*religion not-*abrogates, — or on-*account of-*consent people *provoked, — who *of-*such kind *virtues in-*him observed, — which to *Republic *useful are, — not-*obstant of-*impious him *religion. — Because *empire of-*him not-*founded is in-*grace or *faith, — but in-*free-*will or *reason, — as *Bellarmine himself c. 4 confessed. — If *mutation or *abrogation of-*true *religion he-*attempts on-*account-of-*this not deposed-*is, — but *by-prayers to-*him *resist, — and-if *nothing *is-*profited, — by *open *confession of-*truth *crown of-*martyrdom *seek: — thus of-*old in-*primitive *church Christians *did *not-*deposed *Nero, *Diocletian, *Decium, *Iulian *Apostata, *Valentem *Arianum, and-*similar, — who even with *tortures exquisite subjects to *religion of-*themselves either *ethnic or *heretical *compel wished: — but *patiently them *tolerated, — for *tranquillity of-*empire *prayed, — and *martyrdoms *patiently *bore.

**Kings *Roman-*Christian *not-*because-of-*that *deposed the-*ancient Christians, but because *not-could — patet from 1 Cor 6**, — where *Paul commands to *constitute new judges by-Christians of *temporal-*causes, — nor were-*constrained *Christians in-*forum to-*speak of *Christ persecution.

**Second argument, — which * Mariana adduces**, — is: *tolerating *is *tyrant, — either *infidel or *heretical *trying to-*drag men to *sect-*of-*his, — is *to-*expose religion to-*most-*evident peril: — such indeed there-*are-*sitting-*rectors-of-*empire in-*various *lands, — where *when *evening-*populace-*religion continuous *begins to-*worship idol. — But not-*held-*are Christians to-*tolerate, — but *not-*ought, when with-*evident peril of-*religion, — *magistrate to-*tolerate *infidel. — For when *right *divine and *human *fight, — of-*divine we-*must *observe rather: — of-*divine however-*right is, — to-*preserve *true faith and *religion, — because *of-*natural is, — not much: of-*human however-*right is, — that *have they *him for *king*.

**Reply.** We-*concede, — religion *true peril to-*expose not-*ought-*to-*be: — we-*deny however, — that from-*that, that *heretical or *infidel king, — who *tries men to *sect-*his *perverted-*to-*draw *is *tolerated, — religion our peril *self *exposed-*is: — but *periclitates only *religion, — no-*fault of-*people, — which no-*just *God-*of-*fear *this peril has *remedy, — since *of-*them not *is *election of-*king, — but *into *them *fall *elected-*by. — If *however *some-*here *fault at *people, — the-*same-*also would-*reside at *ancient those Christians, — who under *Domitian, *Nero, *Iulian and-*similar impious *Emperors *lived, — whom with-*great *patience *tolerated: — and-*no-one *however-*them by-*this name *accused, — as-if *religion true *most-*patient of-*tolerance to-*peril *exposed. — Then *however *peril *exposed-*is *religion true, — when *people, — with-*no-*right *forcing, — no *necessity *demanding, — *king or *magistrate to-*themselves *presides *heretical or *infidel, — which of-*none *pious *unquam *was-*done.

**Furthermore what in-*this argument *Bellarmine right divine to-*human opposes**, — not indeed we-*impugn: — but with-*this addition: — while *king *heretical *already from-*election or from-*succession we-*have — that-is, *because-also *now we-*have — our it-*is, — to-*him *by *right *divine to-*obey, — even-if *something *against *religion *true *contriving to-*rise-up we-*can, — nay we-*must.

**Third *Bellarmini argument is:** *if *conjunx *fidelis *heretic *quando-*not *wants to-*remain with *conjuge Christiana; — therefore *people *fidele *reject can *jugum *king *infidel, — and *reject him from *kingdom*, — as-*from *sequence *appears at 1 Cor 7:15.

**Reply.** The-*example not-*makes to-*the-*point: — the-*question is, — *whether *people *faithful *infidel or *heretical *magistrate to-*heresy or-*infidelity *inclining *depose can. — *Apostle *however teaches, — that *fidel *conjunx by *infidel *husband *deserted, — freed from *his *yoke: — which two are *most-*different from-*themselves *clear-*is. — Else *not we-*deny *people *fidele *can *freed from *yoke of *infidel *magistrate, — not however *necessary is, that *itself the-*magistrate *such *depose, — or *obedience *ei *all *derogate; — but *can-*happen *this *liberation, — either by *war, — or by *conversion of-*magistrate, — or by *another some-*means to-*God not-*difficult. — By-*no-means therefore *proves *Bellarmine his *assertion, — namely *heretical to-*be — or *infidel *magistrate Christians to-*tolerate to-*be-*not.

**From this first error stands another**, — namely *magistrate heretical* not-only-*not to-*be-*tolerated, — but *by *Christians to-*be-*taken-*away*: — in-*which *genus the *Jesuits often-*enough *great *aid *bestowed, — for-taking-away by-*assassins their-*own — *kings and-*princes, — whom to-*church of *Papa Roman resist they-*saw. — This *deny some, — from-*themselves to-*happen: — others however-*even, — as-if *well-*done, — from *Scriptures sacred *this *egregious deed to-*defend *dare. — *Mariana provokes to *examples, — teaching *leprous *Oziam from *temple *ejected, — of-*kingdom deprived, — and-of-*son *succession *induced (2 Chr 26).

**Parricide of *Henry III* king of *Gauls (Gallia)** committed year 1589, — 12 Sept., — comparing that *deed* with the-*deed of *Phineas priest slaying *Zambri and *Chusbi in *fornication *found (Num 25:8). — *Judith slaying *Holofernes* (Judith 13:4). — *Mariana (lib. 1 c. 6) provokes to *example of *Aoth, — who *Eglonem king of *Moabites *hidden dagger in *belly *thrust* (Judg 3). — Others *example of *Iahel *killing *Sisara* (Judg 4). — *Samuel *killing *Agag* (1 Sam 15). — *Iehoiada *killing *Athaliae queen* (2 Kgs 11). — *Sauls *killing *fair* (?). — And *what harder in *heretical kings *shall we-*think? — Them *God to-*prayer *reduce we-*cogitated, — as *Saul *sparing king *Agag* (1 Sam 15) *and *Ahab *sparing king *Benhadad* (1 Kgs 20).

**But truly *most-*base-*this is *abuse of *Scripture**, — of-a-*man *Christian *utterly *unworthy. — For, since *Romans in-*most things *Pontifex their-*own *conform to *pontifex of *Old-*Testament, — let-them-*show, where-*ever *Pontifex *Iudaicus to-*himself *such power or-*right of-*life-*and-*death over *judges or *kings of *people of-*themselves *assumed?

*Oziam* indeed *leprosy-*struck priests from *temple *ejected (2 Chr 26): — but *that *king by-*leprosy divinely and-*miraculously *struck, — pro-*office *sacerdotal — by-*law of *God-*declared-*is: — *proffered however by-*sacerdotes from-*temple *ejected, — by *divine *law, — of-*leprous from *rest-*of-*people to-*be-*shut-off (Lev 22). — *Deposition therefore that *made-*is by *God, not by *Pontifex, — not for-*heresy, but for *ambition and-*invasion into-*other *office: — the-*thing-which with *houses *royal *heretical *no-*commerce *has.

*Phinees deed *happened at-*special *mandate of *God*, — with-*which he-*enjoined then-time to *Israelitis, — that anyone-*was-*to-*kill *neighbor-of-*self who himself to *Baal-*Peor and *idolatry-of-*it *had-adjoined (Num 25:5). — Which *mandate *special, — likewise earlier against-*worshippers of *calf-*golden *promulgated (Exod 32). — What certainly *Iudaei from *special *privilege and *mandate *granted, — today by-*no-one to-*example to-*be-*drawn *are, — in-*the-*manner *neither *spoils of *Egyptians *nor *sacrifice of *Isaac to-*imitation are-*proposed. — Vulgarly *is-*said: *heroic *deeds *do-*not-*law*.

**From-*same *foundation *response *is-*to-*be-*given to *example of *Aoth**, — who *express-*mandate *word *had for *killing *king *Moabiticum* (Judg 3:19-20), — and-*by-this-*deed *finished *immediately-*added-*is: *delivered *Lord the *Moabites, — enemies of-*sons of *Israel in-*hand *ours* (v. 30). — *Have *not *such *word of *God for *killing *princes, — in-*their-*opinion *heretical, — and-we-*say, — us *Lord *delivered *them into *hands *ours-of-*themselves.

*Iahel-*also *specially *stirred-*up *Lord against *Sisara*, — as *others *heroes against *Canaanites, — with-*whom *land-*populations he-*long-ago promised, — therefore *drivers-*out of-*people *called-*they-*were. — Since therefore from *homicide of *Moses* (Exod 2) *no-one *can *conclude, *homicides *promiscuously *lawful-*to-*be: — thus from *these *heroes' deeds not-*lawful to-*gather *slaughter of-*princes *heretical *to-*be *lawful.

**The-*same is *reason of *Samuel *killing *king of *Amalekites**. — *Amalekites indeed to-*kill *God had-*commanded (Exod 17:14; Deut 25:17; 1 Sam 15:2-3, 8) — in-which *last-*place also *God had-*commanded to *Saul: *go therefore, and *strike *Amalek, — and-*to-*him-*not-*spare*. — Etc.

**From *law also *special, of *killing *idolatrous, and *seducers to *idolatry (Deut 13)**, — with-*command of-*supreme *magistrate, — *Athaliah *idolatrous impious was-*killed by *Ioiada.

Which all-*things-*however-not simply *touch all, — but *them-*only, — who among *cities of *Israel *idolatrous *dwelt, — badly *drawn are to *slaughters of *Pontifices.

**Conclude therefore**: any *bishop's-office *is, — to-*beware, — lest *magistrate *false religion *nourish, — and in *provinces *of-*his *promote, — but if *anything *otherwise-*done *is by *magistrate, — not with-*arms *carnal, but with-*sword of *Spirit against *him *animadvert. For *no *right has *power *spiritual over *temporal, — of-*taking-away or *evacuating, — but *both power to *preservation of *political *ecclesiastic *necessary is: — as *two arms to *integrity of-*one *body *pertain, — where *however *neither of-*them into-*other *right has *destroying, *breaking, — or-*even *plainly from-*body *cutting-*off.

**Whence follows those with-*greatest *injury *afflict the *magistrate**, — who *his *power thus *subject to *power *Papal, — that this *into *that at-*pleasure *transfer *could: — that-*is-of-*those, — whom *Scripture *calls *bond-*slaves of *masters* (2 Pet 2:19).

### Casus IV. Whether the magistrate may do whatever he wishes, — because vulgarly is-said by politicians: *the prince is above the laws*

*Reply.* Trite is that axiom of politicians: *the prince is loosed from the laws* — which also *Ambrose* in *apology of David*, where of David-adultery he-treats: *the kings law of-them not-held, — for *freed are *kings from *bonds of *delicts*: — but not by-*all rightly-*understood.

**Some indeed think prince or king thus loosed from laws** — that himself all-*things at-*his-*will can-*promise, — as-if the-same-*is, — whether *thing to-*prince with-*honesty *agrees; — whether not-*agrees. — And-*this by-way-of-*kings of *Persians thus loosed-*from-*laws were, — that *whatever to-*them-pleased, — even-if-*base-*it were, — as-*Herodotus* (lib. 3) refers of *Cambyses, — who having *own sister as *wife, — asked his *magi, — whether *lawful *is *sister to-*take as *wife, — responded *magi, — of-*this indeed we-*have-*no *law, — that-*however we-*have in *laws of *Persians *find, — of-*king-*lawful, — *whatever *pleased.

*Sigonius* thus regal empire *loosed-*from-*laws called (lib. 1 *De republica Hebraea* c. 4), — and *king called, — who *all-*things at-*will *bears; *of-*which-*matter *proof *cites from 1 Sam 8:11: *this-*is-*right of-*king, — who *ruling-*is over-*you: — *sons *your *he-*shall-*take*, — and-*shall-*put in *chariots-*his, — *shall-*make to-*self *horsemen and-*forerunners of-*quadrigas-*his, — and-*shall-*establish to-*self *tribunes and *centurions, — and-*plowers of-*fields-*your and-*harvesters of-*harvests, — of-*fabricators of-*arms and-*chariots-*his: *daughters *your *shall-*take to-*self as *ointment-*makers, — and *cooks, — and *bread-*makers: *fields *also *your, — and *vineyards, and *olive-*groves *best *shall-*take, — and-*shall-*give to-*servants-*his*.

**But these are-*not sentence of *axiom *political**, — nor-*that in-*history *Samuel *contained. — There indeed (as from v. 5 and v. 22 is-clear) not-are-*described *rights of-*majesty, — but how *kings by-*right-*their-*own *habitually-*abuse is-indicated. — For *God saw *insanity of-*people of *Israel *fury, — who *rejecting *God's *empire, — which through *judges *appointed *administered, — *king *wished, — of-*whose *manners also-*most-*unquiet to-*bear-*necessary would-*be to-*have, — nor *yoke *once *imposed easily to-*shake-off.

**And-*this interpretation words first in *sources *Hebraic *equivocal render probable.** For in-*Hebrew *is *mispat *Samuelah — the-*LXX render *dikaiōma basileōs — with-*which vocabulary *misbath even *of-*that, which *most-*unjust *is, — but for-*just *held, — is-*used, — as *right *adulterated in Ezek 16:38: — so-*also here *right of-*king *called, — *whatever to-*king *just *shall-*seem, — even-*if in-*itself *is *none.

**Then *accedes *people's *response**, — who-*not with-*so-*great *impiety could-*deny, — *rights by *God to-*king *prescribed. — He-*denied *therefore *such *shall-*be the-*manners of *kings, — and-*that from *example of-*rest *of-*peoples wanted to-*confirm, — and-*show, — how *comfortably-*lived under *kings, — and-*that *comfortableness (which is-*in *peace of-*time *clement *judgment, — in *war of-*subjects *guardianship) *by-*all *proposed-*difficulties *far *superior *is-*to-*be.

**When therefore the-*prince *loosed-*is *from-*laws is-*said**, — *considered-*is as *prince, — not as *man, obliging *himself to *laws of *God and-*nature, — but as *prince, — *lives indeed by *laws, — but *not obliged. — For to-*live by *laws *political, — not-*is *opposite to-*that, which-*is to-*be *by *laws *obliged: — nay *loosed-*to-*be from *laws, and-*obliged to-*be to *laws — these two are-*opposed.

**Prince therefore**, as *prince, lives by *laws either by-*himself or *predecessors of-*his *politically *constituted, — and-*into *tyranny *degenerates, — if by *laws *not lives. — For *most-*true is, what *Ambrose to *Valentinian Emperor wrote (epist. 32): *when *laws prescribe to *others, — thou-*prescribest to-*thyself: — since-*indeed *natural *right *requires, — that *same *right to-*all *equal *rendered-*be, — because *diversity of-*right in-*same Republic *breeds *discord, — *discord *overturns Republic — therefore *necessary *is, — that *prince *by-*same *right *live, — with-*which he *lives*.

**If you-*shall-*say prince therefore is-*loosed from-*law, — because *many-*enjoys *privileges**, — which *to-*rest of-*subjects by-*no-*means *compete, — know we-*must, — that *here-*considered-*are *rights of-*prince, — from *which any of-*princes *is-*determined, — and-*distant-*are *rights of *privileges, — which *are *rights *singular, — and, — from *certain *causes, — as *prerogatives of-*chief *merits to *princes *reserved: — of-*which *respect *Iustinian Emperor (l. fin. *C. de professoribus*) said: *those who-*for *free *studies, — with-*labors-*proper for *whole-*world *terrestrial *made-*have, — laboring however-*not *received *dignity of-*right *prerogative of-*fortune?* — Prince therefore not in-*all *is *privileged, — but only in-*some by-*peculiar *right *uses, — in *rest lives by-*common *right.

**And-*even-*if *prince *according-to *laws to-*live *held*, — not *however *himself by-*laws *obliged is, — but *loosed: — for-*no *Republic *stand *could. — Certain *indeed *is, — from *no-*one to-*be *sanctions of-*laws *mutable, — but from-*him, who from-*laws *loosed *is: — for *whoever *under *law *is, — the-*same-*obliged-*is, — from-*observance of-*law *withdraw *cannot. — Neither *therefore *would-*promulgate *new *laws, — old *abrogate, — since *not *would-*have *of-*laws *establishing *authority: nor-*yet *would-*keep. — Certain-*and-*this-*is, — *laws *sanctioned *look-to *Republic — likewise, — and-*this for *times and *circumstances *variousities *notably *vary, — and *therefore *laws to *times *to-*be-*obnoxious, — with-*which *one *law *only *civilly-*noted *scarcely-*is-*found — for-*all *times *accommodated.

**What in-*peace *statute *are, — most-*of-*them *not *valid in-*war**, — and-*what in-*war-*valid, — *hardly *place-*have in-*time of-*peace. — In-*order-*therefore *laws for *salvation of *Republic *changed-*can-*be, — necessary-*is *prince *loosed-*to-*be from-*laws, — nay and-*not *other-*is *of-*that *political *axiom-*sentence. — Thus at *Dio (lib. 58) we-*read, — that *senate *Roman *Octavium *Augustum from-*all *laws-*necessity *loosed, — that truly with *full *power, — perfectly *of-*his-*own *right, — and-*loosed-*from-*laws *acting or-*not-*acting *all *could of-*his-*own *at-*will.

**Summary therefore of-*response *this-*is**: *prince, as *man of-*good-*faith and-*truth, is *below the-*law, — nay and *himself to-*self-*fixes, — which to-*subjects *he-*sets-*before, — himself *first *observes: — but *prince, as *prince, — politically-*considered, — is *loosed from-*laws, — that himself-*for *salvation of *Republic *laws *other *bring or *change *can.

### Casus V. Whether the magistrate can with good conscience hear and-*decide *laws, — even-if unjust

*Reply.* This deny the *Anabaptists* on-account-of the words of Christ: *he who wishes with-thee in judgment to-contend, — and-tunic-thine to-take, — remit to-him and *pallium* — walk with-him thousand-*paces, — do-not-return* (Matt 5:40). — Also that of-*Apostle* (1 Cor 6:1): *are-you *unworthy — since concerning the-*minimum you-*judge?* Absolutely: *there-*is-*a *fault therefore, — because *judgments *you-*have among yourselves. Why not-*more *injuries *you-*accept? — Why not-*more *harm *you-*bear?* (1 Cor 6:7).

**Of the *Fathers* also some judgments and *forensic *causes have-*deemed *iniquer**, — of-*whose *testimonies cites *D. Chemnitz* (part. 3 *E.C.* loc. de vindicta, dictated fol. 178 no. 26 seqq.).

**Our sentence however is: — chief part-of-*office of *political magistrate**, — to-*hear and-*decide *causes of *subjects in *judgment, — because it-*is *just *defense, which he-*owes to *goods, *reputation and *existence of *subjects. — In-the-*manner in-*which *legitimate *defense of *harmed *reputation *asked from *magistrate *lawful-*is, — so *asking, — that he-*of-*our *cause *acknowledge, — and-*us *by-*just *decision from *calumnies and-*harms *free.

**Scripture clearly teaches, — the-*judgment of *political *magistrate not-*to-*be of-*men, but of-*God** (2 Chr 19:6), — and *God himself in-*congregation of-*gods, — or in-*midst of-*judges *stands, — and-*causes *judges. — He-*commanded also, that *disputing-*ones their-*causes to-*judgment *bring* (Exod 21:22). — *Under him *judge cause *reader-*to-*be before *God (Deut 1:17) — in-*sight of-*judges (Deut 25:1). — And-*lest anyone *such to-*Judaic then *people *pertaining *think, — noting, — that *God in *eighth *commandment of-*law *moral *forbade *false *testimonies, — which to *judicial *forensic *pertain: — in *New *Testament also *are *examples of-*those, — who their-*cause before *ethnic *magistrate *conducted, — as *Christ himself before *Pilate (John 18:36), *Paul before *Festus (Acts 25:8), — with-*accusers to-*his *responds (Acts 23:12), *implored *against *ambushes of *Jews (Acts 23:16-17) — the-*defense of-*public *power, — nay *appeal to *Caesar *himself-*instituted (Acts 25:10). — Which *examples *teach *all *remedies-of-*right, — that-*is, *exceptions, *objections, *appeals, and-*similar, — that-*they *rightly *can *be-*used *even *by-*Christians.

**To *this *doctrine not-*to-*be-*opposed are *words of *Christ**, who-*wills he-*with-*thee in-*judgment to-*contend, — say. — For not-*disapproves *he *actions *forensic, — but *opposes-*are to *private *revenge, — and-*commend the-*patience of *Christian. — For-*wishes to-*teach *Christ his-*own, — lest on-*account *earthly *things too-*much wrangle, — but *live *peacefully, — nay-*even-*works of *magistrate *cannot *at-*times *safe. — What-*else *tolerate rather-*part they-*shall-*want, — than *many-*more, — that *harm to-*themselves *afflicted-*with themselves-*avenge. — Not *therefore *prohibits in *judgments-*and-*legitimate *defense of *magistrate, — but in-*defect of *justice, — of-*injuries rather-*patience — than *of-*revenge *desirous us-*to-*be — he-*willed.

**The-*place of *Apostle *Paul also nothing** hinders our sentence. *Apostle *judgment not *simply *prohibits *judgments of *political *magistrate, — with-*which he *himself-*also-*used, — and-*magistrate *God-*minister *calls *for *good-*to-*thee* (Rom 13:4) — that-*is, *for *thy *good, — that thou-*hast *legitimate *self-*defense: — but was *something *other, — for-*which *Corinthians *rebuked *he: — (1) that *temerariously some *others *harmed, — and-*thus of-*harmed-*part *occasion *gave-*litigate with *brother. (2) That *harmed-*part of-*injuries was-*impatient — all *even *slight *matter *to *judge *ordinary *bore, — since *however *Christians *mutual *ought-*to *pardoning, — from-*precept of *Christ: *remit, and-*shall-be-*remitted *you* (Luke 6:37). **Donaria** are-*those, which to *judge *privately *offered-*are, — to *promote *cause. These from *no-*one *are-*to-*be-*exacted: in *offered however-*accepting *great *is-*to-*be-*given *caution. *Before *judgment *accepted *not-*to-*be *ought*, — lest *anyone *think *sentence *to-*have-*sold, — that-*is, *not-*according to *truth, but from *affect *pronounced *is *by-*gifts-*corrupted, — of *which *matter *the-*Lord in *law *says: *thou-*shalt-*not-*take *person or *gifts, because *gifts *blind *eyes of *wise, — and *change *words of *just* (Deut 16:19); and *again: *cursed, who *accepts *gifts, — that *strike *soul *of *blood *innocent* (Deut 27:25); — and at *Isaiah* *rebuked-*are *princes of *people, that *all *love *gifts* (Isa 1:23), and: *woe, who *justify *impious *for *gifts, and-*justice *of-*just *take-*away from-*him* (Isa 5:23).

### Casus X. What are-*to-*be-*observed by-*magistrate *waging *war*, that *good *conscience *he-*retain

**Therefore *worthy *is, to-*note *cautions to-*be-*observed *both by *magistrate*, who *war *indicts, — and-*by-*rest, who *him *serve, — that *soldiery *well *treated-*be with *conscience.

**[To *just *war *three *requires *Thomas* (1.2 q. 40 art. 1): *authority *of-*indicating*, *just *cause, and *right *intention*.]**

**First of-*all *let-*see the-*magistrate, *by-*what *jurisdiction of-*his *indicating of *war *is-*founded**; — for-*if *inferior *magistrate *war *indicts to *superior *not-*consenting, — *not-*is *war, but *sedition.

**Then *cause of *war *just *he-*have**. *Just *war *cause* — per *most-*studied of *Franciscus de Victoria* (in *Relect.* 6 q. 2): *not-*is *diversity of *religion: — for *neither *Iews nor *gentiles *lawful in *war *to-*attack, — that *faith *Christian *undertake: *not-*is *just *cause of *war *amplification of *empire; — for-*not *lawful for *temporal *goods *men *to-*kill: *not *just *cause of *war *proper *glory or *convenience of *prince *private: — nor *whatever *injury by *war *to-*be-*vindicated *is, — lest *penalty of *measure *exceed *delict*.

**Of *just however-*causes of *war *all-*most-*of-*all from *Scripture *judged-*can-*be**, in *which *many *of-*just *wars *examples *occur. *All *war *is *species *public *vengeance*. *Vengeance however *is of *sins either *of-*first or *second *table.

**In *first *table *just *cause of *war *was of-*old *idolatry and-*manifest *blasphemy**, — for *which *magistrate *war *indict *could, — lest *perhaps *teach *gentes *people of *God *abominations *of-*themselves (Deut 7:2,4,10; 8). — But *this *cause *pertained *only to *republic of *Hebrews. — As *said-*is (Deut 13:1): *if in-*one of *cities of *thine *exercised-*idolatry [is]. — *Iews *else *special *mandate *had of *extirpating *gentes *idolatrous* (Deut 7:1-16).

**In *second *table *just *cause of *war *occurs*: **(1) *Violation of *pact*, as *Iosaphat *king of *Moabites *withdrawing from-*pact, *war *indicted* (2 Kgs 3:7). **(2) *Violation of *right of *nations, and-*notorious *contumely*, — for-*which-*reason *David *war *pursued of *king *Ammonites, because *contumely *afflicted-*had *legates *his* (2 Sam 10:4). **(3) *Rapine *violent or *unjust*, — as *David *war *waged against *son of *Saul *aspiring *kingdom* (2 Sam 2 seqq., 3, 4). **(4) *Liberty of *fatherland*, to *which *pertain *wars of *David against *Philistines. **(5) *Auxilium to *allies *brought*, of *which *cause *David *war *moved against *Syros* (2 Sam 8:5). **(6) *Neglected *vengeance against *deed *notorious*: — for-*that *cause *war *he-*waged with *Beniamitis* (Judg 20). — And *these *are *causes of *war *offensive*.

**Of *defensive however *war *example *supplies *Abraham**, — who to *liberate *Lothum *war *went-forth against *five *kings (Gen 14:14). *Maccabaei*, who *fought for *law of *Lord for *souls, for *wives and-*children *of-*themselves against *multitude *contumacious and-*proud* (1 Macc 3:10). — This therefore *second-*is, to-*magistrate *wars *waging *to-*be-*observed.

**Third *let-*see *magistrate, — that of *war-*his *just *have *end and *right *intention**, which *directed *is to *peace and *tranquillity: — for-*for *peace *undertaken *is *war. And as *Augustine* (epist. 205) *speaks: *peace *have *of-*will *is, *war however *ought to-*be of *necessity, — that *free *God from *necessity, and *preserve in *peace. — Not indeed *peace *sought, — that *war *exercised-*be: — but *war *waged-*is, — that *peace *acquired*.

***Perverse however-*intention is**, when from *cupidity of *harming, *cruelty of *avenging, *ferocity of *rebelling, *lust of *dominating, and-*other *perverse *affects *war *inflicted *is and-*waged. — *No-*one therefore *seek *occasion of-*warring, — *no-*one *attack *another, — but *peace, as-*of-*that *possible *is, *have with *all: — even-*attacked *peaceful, and *all *earlier *try than *to *arms *come, — and-*nothing-*else than *peace and *tranquillity *public *seek.

### Casus XIII. Whether *even *ecclesiastical *persons for *crimes *under-*political *magistrate *lie-*subject

*Reply.* Absolutely. *Double indeed *is *power, *spiritual and *temporal*, of *which *the-*other in *matters *ecclesiastical, — the-*other in *civil *is-*occupied. — *Kings *subject *are to *bishops in *spiritualibus*; *bishops to *kings in *temporalibus*: — *under *bishops however *name *understood-*are *all *clerics.

**That *clerics *are *under *power of *political *magistrate**, — *most-*clear *words *attests *Apostle *Paul*: *every *soul, *he-*says, *to *higher *powers *let-*be-*subject* (Rom 13:1). — In *which *words *this-*manner *comments *Chrysostom* (hom. 23 ad Rom.): *what *to-*all *these *precepts, *both *sacerdotibus and *monachis, — not *secularibus *only, *immediately *initio *manifest *this *made, — thus *saying: *every *soul *powers *higher *subject *let-*be, — even-*if *apostle *were, — even-*if *evangelista, — even-*if *prophet, — even-*if *anyone *finally *were*: — nor indeed *piety-*this *subjection *overturns*.

**Then *Solomon by-*his *example *teaches**, — *magistrate *power *has in *temporalibus *even in *sacerdotes*, — and *pontifex *himself. For as-*when *Abiathar *pontifex to *treason of *Adonias *consented-*had, — *declared, — him *to-*be *man of *death, and from *office *deposed* (1 Kgs 2:27).

*Bellarmine* indeed *contends*, — *Solomon *this, *not as *king *did, but as *Prophet *did, — and *executor of *justice *divine, — sicut *pium *loquitur (Rom 3:19). — But *no *is *of-*this *interpretation *reason*, *no *anywhere *of-*this *Prophetice *executionis *is *mention, — but to *power-*his *regal *this *himself-*refers: *lives *Lord, — he-*says, — who *confirmed *me, — and *placed *me on *throne of *David *father-*mine* (v. 24).

***Kings *even *Bellarmine* (in *old *Testament *summa *power-*themselves *temporal, in *new *spiritual*, because in *old *Testament *promises *only *are *temporal, — in *New however *spiritual and *eternal*).

**But-*also *this *false-*is**. For in *both *testament *power *temporal and *spiritual, in *its *remaining *sphere, — that-*neither *temporal *power *sacerdotal *jurisdiction, — nor *spiritual *temporal *invade.

**Third, *privileges of *clerics**, — with-*which from *indulgentia of *political *magistrates *enjoy, *argue, — that *magistrate *right on *those *has, — because *common *auxilio and-*proper *right *fortified *exempted *no *privilege or *extraordinary *auxilio *need *is.

**Add-*that *Christ himself *to *political *magistrate *subject to-*be *willed***, — even-*if *he-*were *doctor of *church-*his-*own, — that-*both in *real-*things, because *tribute *gave* (Matt 17:24-27); — as-*and in *personal-*things, — because before *Pilate *judged-*was, — whom *and *power *divinely from *high *have *said (John 19:11).

**To-*be-*noted however-*is, that in *churches *evangelical *magistrate *right of-*self on *clerics *executes through *consistories *ecclesiastica* in *reverence of *ministry, — unless *perhaps *were *criminal*, where *person of *cleric *not *attended, but as *layman before *magistrate *accused, and for *matter-*of-*fact *punished.

**Against *this *doctrine *stand *Romanenses**, — who *clerics *all from *jurisdiction of *judges *secular *exempted *to-*be *establish, — both in *criminalibus, and-*in *civilibus, as *is-*clear from *Concil. Trident. sess. 24 c. 10 De reform. and-*from *dist. 96 c. 1, and-*most-*many *places.

**But *Bellarmine* himself *confesses* (lib. 1 *De cleric.* c. 28), *exemption *this by *right *human *introduced *is, *not *divine, — and *no *can *proffered *be *word of *God, with *which *this *exemption *confirmed-*be*: which-*and *most-*true-*is: — nay *word of *Apostle *Paul *express-*contrary *has, with-*which *every *soul to *powers *higher *subject *to-*be *teaches* (Rom 13:1). — And-*of-*old *laws *imperial *constituted and *observed *is, — that *clerics of *civil-*things *respond before *judges *secular, and *from-*those *condemned *were, if *criminal *were *found, as-*is *in *Novella *of-*clerics 85 § *if however*. — What *however *later in *reverence of *ministry *exempted *were, — that from *emperors *done, — and *by-*itself *certain *is *judgment, — that *with *magistrate *political *power of-*judging *clerics in *civil and *criminal *was; — which *more-*at-*large *deduced-*has *Wilhelm Barclay* (*De potestate Papae in principem Christianum* c. 15).

### Casus XIV. If *clerics *are-*under *power of *magistrate *political, *therefore-*and-*they *held-*are to-*pay *magistrate *tributes and *taxes

*Reply.* *Distinguished-*must-*be between *persons and between *goods of *clerics*. **Persons are-*exempt from *contributions**, with-*which *other *citizens *are-*burdened: — because *stipends of-*themselves *hardly *else *suffice to *necessary *aliments. — Of *stipends however-*their *as *aliments *necessary, *tribute to-*give *not *held-*are: — therefore Num 18 *read-*is, *God to-*have-*given to *sacerdotes *decimas, — that *themselves at *altar *serve; — of *decimis *therefore *those, which *given-*were *for *that, *that at *altar *served, — *no *paid *tribute, because *given-*are for *aliments.

**If however *extrema *forces *necessity, when *perhaps *exhausted *fisc *is, and *peril from *enemy *impends**, — then anyone *understands, — himself as-*much *needing *defense as *others, — therefore of-*self also *something into *common *to-*bring not-*grievously-*would-*bear. *Necessity indeed *not-*has *law, — nor *cares *privilege.

**Goods of *clerics are *double**, — either *private, as *house, *field, *vineyard, which anyone in *own-*and of-*self-*themselves *use *acquired; — or *ecclesiastical *common, which to *whole *college *pertain, — as-*are *estates, *fields *rents-*and *others of *whole *convent, *college, or *treasury *ecclesiastical.

**Of *private *goods *deservedly *paid-*are *tributes**, because *respect of *those *clerics *equally *citizens *are of *Republic as *others, — and-*same *goods *finally into *inheritance of *children *pass: — *therefore *professors of *same with *others *loads *deservedly *bear.

**As-*to *goods *common, — those from *tribute *are *exempt**; because of *no *person are-*proper, and to *common *sustentation of *clerics *pertain. *Therefore *Joseph, when *whole *Egypt *land *obliged-*had, and *tributary *made-*had, *sacerdotum *land *excepted, which *wished to-*be *free* (Gen 47:22). — And when *paid-*were *tributes to-*king of *Persarum, *excepted *were *sacerdotes and *Levitae*, as-*read-*is at *Ezra 7:24.

### Casus XV. Whether laws made by the political magistrate bind the consciences of subjects

*Reply.* *Not-*here *of *question, — whether *magistrate *has *right on *consciences of *subjects*: — for-*this *belongs to *God *alone, who as *searches *hearts and *reins, so *alone-*also *consciences *bind *can: **He alone-*is *lawgiver, who *can *save and *destroy* (James 4:12). — But *this *asked-*is, — *whether *subjects *laws by-*magistrate *enacted *knowingly and *willingly *transgress *can, — even-*if by *no-*one either *charged-*or *punished, — from *sole however *conscience *convicted-*may-*be.

**Thus *proposed *question *decision *has in *authentic *of-*Apostle *Paul* (Rom 13:5): *by *necessity to-*subject-*be, — *not *only for *wrath, but *also for *conscience*, — that *this-*sound and *inviolate *may-*be-*left; — and in *that other (v. 4): *magistrate *is *of-*God *minister, — *who therefore *of-*power *resists, *of-*God *ordination *resists*.

**But *here-*of *distinction *there-*is-*need**, *partly *as-*to *laws, *partly *as-*to *obligation *of-*them.

**If *laws *shall-*be *impious**, — *leading to *those which *are against *true *religion, *piety and *good *morals, *conscience *by-*no-*means *bind: *behooves indeed *God *rather *to-*obey *than *men* (Acts 5:29). — **If *laws *are *manifest to-*all**, — so-*that *even *sense of *law *no-*one *escapes, — *transgression-*of-*them *not-*is *without *wound of *conscience, — *species indeed *has of *contempt both of *laws and of-*magistrate-*himself. — But if *any-*one *such *law *made *to-*have-*been, — or *this *its *sense *invincibly *were-*ignorant, — *such *ignorance *excuses, and *transgressor in *conscience *his on-*account *not *bound-*is. — **If *laws *most-*grave *some, to *state of *Republic and *tranquility *public *pertaining, *should-*prescribe**, — those *altogether *conscience *bind, — because with *right *natural *agree, and *right of-*nature with *right *divine (which *without *controversy *binds *conscience) *coincides. — **But-*if *however *laws *contain *some-*things *slighter, *order *perhaps or *decorum in *Republic *concerning, — *these-*if *someone *transgress-*should with *public *scandal, — *without *doubt *conscience *violate; — if *however *without *evident *some *scandal *should-*be, — *transgression *not *violates.

**As-*to *obligation, — **(1) *some *laws *bind *simply*, so-*that in *no *mode either *with *respect from *their *prescription to-*depart *may-*be-*allowed, as *laws *natural and *divine; **some however-*from *hypothesis*, — if *of-*any *violation-*of-*them *should-*happen from *contempt, in *evil *cause, or *not *without *scandal. **(2) *Some *obligation *direct*, when *law *immediately *is from *God; *some *indirect*, when *law *not indeed *immediately from *God *is, but *only from *person *such, to whom *God *power of *laws *enacting *has-*given. — To *this indeed *obedience *owed-*is on-*account-of *God, whose *ordination *resists *who *such *person, as *vicar of *God, *resists.

**Plain therefore *is, — how *laws of *civil *magistrates in *conscience to-*bind *said-*are, *not *directly by-*respect of *magistrate-*himself, but by-*reason of *God, who *wills, — *ministers and *vicars-*his in *every *life-*kind *reverently to-*have-*us. — *More on *this *question *see at *Meisner* (*Lib. 4 De iure* sect. 6 quaest. 11) and *Gerhard* (L.C. tom. 6 *De magistratu politico* art. 1 th. 167 *seqq.*).

### Casus XVI. Whether the magistrate can with good conscience arrogate to himself alone the right of hunting, so that on those who invade this right he-*have *power of *punishing

*Reply.* *God in *first *creation *fishes, *birds, *beasts of *earth-*first *subjected to-*man, without *any *distinction of *honor or *dignity*, as *written-*is (Gen 1:28): *have-*dominion over-*fishes of *sea and *birds of *heaven and *all *living-*things, which *move *upon *earth*. — And *this *dominion *was *part *secondary of *image *divine, to *which *man *was *created, *which *though *much *diminished, *remained still *after *fall (Gen 9:2). *Hence *also *huntings *were *first *common*, which *anyone *at *pleasure, — not-*only in *his-*own but also in *another *territory-*was-*instituting, — as *Esau (Gen 27:5), and *today still *among *Turks and *some *other *peoples *free-*is *to-*anyone, in *any *estate *to-*hunt.

**But-*when *human *race *multiplied**, so-*that *some *into *kings and *princes *were-*elected, *certain-*things either *for-*right-*sake or *for-*recreation-*sake *ceded from *dominion *common into *use *proper, which *customarily *regalia *called-*are, — as-*are *vectigalia, *salt-*works, and-*others.

**Can therefore *magistrates *higher, that-*is, *kings and *princes, *and *who *any *part with-*them *participate, this *right-*of-*their-*own (*not indeed of *Christ *their-*own is, *his-*own from *princes to-*strip *regalia*), but *observing *certain *cautions.

**(1) *Let-*be *hunt *legitimate for-*ends***: (1) *of-*honest *recreation-*sake, (2) *for *diminishing *noxious *beasts, that *men and *crops of-*earth *may-*be in *safety, (3) *for *procuring *food for *table of *princes, as in *court of *Solomon (1 Kgs 4). — *Pernicious however-*is *hunt, which *is-*done with *destruction of *subjects.

**(2) *Let-*not-*be in *hunt *too-*much *neglect of *justice**, with *groan of *widows and *orphans, whose *causes *not-*known-*are, with *destruction of-*whole *Republic.

**(3) *Wild-*beasts *multiply *not to-*permit, with *maximum *of-*their *detriment*.

**(4) *Huntings in-*just-*time to-*be-*instituted**, *not under *sermon-*hour, from *which not-*only *magnates themselves, but *also *most-*many of *subjects, whose *work in *hunt they-*need, *are-*drawn-*away.

**(5) *Let-*happen *huntings *without *damage of *subjects**, *not *trampled-*be *crops, and *by-*tears of *subjects *of-*princes *pleasures *fed*: — but *if any *detriment to-*anyone even from *unwilling *made *shall-*be, — *it by-*just *compensation *repaired-*be*: which *most-*religiously *prince and *Elector of-*Saxony *Frederick III* to-*have-*done *writes *Luther* on-*chapter 27 of *Genesis: *thus he-*hunted (says-*he), — that to-*no-*one he-*was-*hurtful, but to-*many *profitable, and-*whenever *even *little *damage *someone-*inflicted, — *paid *double. *If-*even *rustic *some *measures of *grain *strewed-*out, that-*was, — which *wild-*beasts *fed-*upon: — *that *worthy *is of *good and *praiseworthy *prince to-*believe*.

**These *rules *ought *moderate *huntings of *princes**.

**As-*to *penalties on *violators of *forests, or on-*those who *beasts *contrary-*to *prince *hunt*, — of *these *certain what *jurisconsults *determine.

**In *general *we-*say**: **(1) *not-*to-*lack *species of *theft, if *anyone *those which from *reasons *above *praised *belong to *prince, *contrary-*to *prince, *to-*wild-*beasts *seizes: — *therefore *grave *penalty to-*inflict *not-*is-*able. **(2) *to-*be-*seen whether *this *fact *is from *ignorance or from *contempt of *magistrate, — whether *once and *again, or from *purpose, or *by-*chance: — for these *and *similar *circumstances *lessen or *increase *deed. **(3) *for-*pious *princes *more-*praiseworthy and to-*consciences *safer *is, *penalty *that *not-*to-*make *capital, but *even if-*most *civil *laws *it *such *to-*be *order, *for *equity-*sake however *it to-*mitigate and into *mulct *pecuniary, or of *prison to-*change *fitting-*is*: for-*of-*man to *image of *God *made *life *much *more-*excellent-*is, than *thousand *stags or *hares. — *More on *hunting *see at *Dominicus Soto* (lib. 4 *de iust.* q. 6 art. 3), *Azorius* (part 3 moral. lib. 5 cap. 26), *Gerhard* (L.C. tom. 6 cap. 3 seqq.), *Loricchius* (in *thesauro Theol. novo* voice *fera*).

### Casus XVII. Whether the magistrate may with good conscience tolerate brothels in the republic

*Reply.* *Brothels *are *places *public, where *harlots and *prostitutes with-*body-*their-*own *gain *make*. So-*called from *harlots, who *among *Latins *were-*called *lupae* (she-*wolves), as-*at *Livy* (*Livy* dec. 1 lib. 1) *Larentia* by-*common *body-*prostituting *she-*wolf *among *shepherds *called-*is, — and *at *Plautus* (*Epidicus* 3.4.7) *wolf* *contrasted-*is to *virgin*: *diverse *are-*morals, — I-*say, — of *virgin from *she-*wolf*. — *Called *also *Romans *brothel *summenium*, as-*if *sub-*wall (sub-*moenia); *therefore *also *summeniana-*women at *Martial*. — *Among *Greeks *these *places *various *names *bore*, — *casaria*, *casalia*, *casauria*, *casoria*, — for *harlots-*themselves *were-*called *casoreides*.

**Such *impure *places *tolerated-*were *among *gentiles*, who either *sin-*not-*counted-*it in *youth, or *public *this-*flagitious *profession as *penalty-*place *had; — **among *Christians however *such *not-*even *heard *ought-*to-*be**, — according-to *admonition of *Apostle: *fornication however and *all *uncleanness or *avarice *let-*not-*be-*named among *you, as *fitting-*is among *saints* (Eph 5:3). — **Well-*therefore *does *pious *magistrate, that neither *prostitutes and *she-*wolves *these, nor *brothels or *inns-*their-*own in *republic *tolerates*.

**Arguments**: (1) *what *manifestly *are *contrary-*to *law of *God, *not *to-*be-*fostered, *not to-*be-*promoted *ought: — but *fornications and *adulteries *contrary *to *law of *God, *undoubted *truth-*is: — *hence *not to-*be-*tolerated impiety-*is, that *those, who *this *do, — *dwellings *conceded-*are, in *which *such *things *unpunished *they-*perpetrate. (2) *Brothels for *certain *money (which *vectigal *bordello *called-*is) *let-*out-*are, which by *prostitutes *paid-*is to *magistrate, and to *fisc *common *carried-*is. — But *God in *law *of-*old *forbade*: *offer-*not the-*hire of *prostitute in *house of *Lord thy *God* (Deut 23:18); — and *civil *laws *sanction, that if *anyone *dishonest *gains *shall-*have, *them to-*restore *he-*be-*compelled. (3) *Civil *laws *infamous *pronounce *woman, who *herself *prostitutes*: — similarly *Iulianus *Emperor *wills *prostitutes *utterly to-*be *banished from *cities. (4) *Every *fuel of *lusts from *sight of *Christians *far to-*be-*removed*: — but through *brothels *certainly *lust *inflamed-*is, and-*many to *this *sin *enticed-*are, who of *it *else *not-*even *would-*think. *Who indeed *can *foster *coals in *bosom-*his-*own, — that not *burn*? (Prov 6:27) *Chrysostom on Ambrose: *who *may-*deem, that *prostitutes fostered-*can *be in *city, if *young-*men *fornicate-*not? (5) *Holy *fathers-*also *abhorred *brothels*. *Tertullian* *them before *God *execrable *calls, *farms of *foul *called-*they, — as *shameful *places (*De civitate Dei* 14.18; 18.28).

**Which *since-*so-*are, *marvelous-*is *bold-*wickedness of *Roman *Pontiff and *whole *clergy *papistic**, who *public *brothels in *most-*ample *cities, — even in *very *city *Rome *tolerate*, — which *houses *often not-*far from *sacraries *have, — with-*permitted *diction of *bishops and *prelates *Papal *watching-*over, — so-*far-*is *of-*profit *hunger, and *good *of-*gain *smell from *thing *any*.

**Reasons of-*Jesuits *defending *brothels**: (1) *between *two *evils *lesser to-*be-*chosen: *tolerable *thus-*seemed *brothel, lest *young-*men *even-*more *heinous *evils *dared. — *Reply*: *not-*is *doing *evil, that *may-*come *good* (Rom 3:8), which of *every *evil of-*guilt *true-*is. Nor-*ever *let-*us-*think, as *Augustine* (*De mendacio* c. 9): *by *minor-*ones *committing *major-*ones *may-*be-*avoided; *rather-*abandon *limits and *all *terms-*removed, *into *infinite *space *all *will-*enter, and *reign*. *There-*are *modes, by-*which *insolent-*men *violence from *honest *matrons *repelled-*can-*be*: not *tolerated-*are *idle *bellies in *republic, *prison and *hunger *coerce their *wantonness, *adultery according-to *laws *punished-*be, and *not-*will-*be, *whence *honest *matrons *for-*themselves from-*those *fear-*need. (2) *That *God *himself, — *lest-*graver *evils *permit, — *letter of *repudium *permitted to-*Jews. — *Reply*: *God of *deed-*his-*own *without *doubt *just *reasons *had, which to *investigate-*ours *not-*is. *Not *therefore-*must-*be-*seen, what *God *has-*done, but *what *he *us to-*do *has-*commanded: for-*us, — *not himself, — *law *he-*gave. (3) *They-*produce *some laws *civil, by-*which *brothels *conceded-*are. — *Reply*: *Even-*if *thousand *laws *were, *of-*greater-*ought to-*us to-*be *authority *word of *God*. *Jerome* writes on *Fabiolam*: *other-*is-*what *Papinian, *other-*is-*what *Paul *writes. (4) *If *tolerated-*are *harlots, *an *occasion-*of-*conversion-*of-*them *would-*be*. *Christ *says to *Pharisees*: *harlots and *publicans *precede *you in *kingdom of *God* (Matt 21:31). — *Reply*: *But *badly *hence *inferred: *therefore *tolerated-*are *brothels. — *Tolerated *indeed *harlots*, but *not *that in *sumptuous *dwellings *live, *not *shining *pomp in *public *go-*forth, *much *less-*that in *sins-*their-*own *continue: — *such-*ones *no *place *have, *nor *precede *others in *kingdom of *God: — *but *cease-*let-*them *to-*sin, *seriously *repent*, — with-*all *body-*ornament *cast-*off, in *garb of *penitents in *public *go-*forth, to *sacred *assemblies *let-*join-*themselves, *word *divine *studiously *hear, — *thus perhaps in *way *recalled-*may-*be. (5) *In-*time of *Solomon *two harlots *were in *one *house (1 Kgs 3:16). — *Reply*: *From-*that *not-*can-*be-*collected *that *Solomon *tolerated *brothels, *nor *proved *that *house *was *brothel: *not *here-*asked, *what *done, but *what to-*have-*been-*done *ought. *God *of-*old *had-*forbidden *harlots to-*be in *his *people (Deut). — *If in *time of *Solomon *this *discipline *collapsed, — *not therefore *permitted-*it *God to-*be-*done. (6) *Augustine* (*De ordine* 2.4): *take *harlots from *human *affairs, — *thou-*wilt-*disturb *all *lusts: *put-*them in *place of *matrons, *taint and *dishonor *thou-*wilt-*mark*. — *Reply*: *Augustine there *not *orders *harlots together with *brothels in *city to-*place, but *where-*already *they-*are, *them also *order *pro *its *modulo to-*take *teaches, — as-*also *those things which *are *noxious or *deformed, to *order *pertain in *body or *republic *some. — *Moreover *also *forbids, *that *where *are, *in *place of *matrons *substituted-*they-*be, but in *place *most-*vile *left-*they-*be, — which-*all *us *by-*no-*means *strike, who against *brothels *fight, — which *Augustine *also *disapproves.

**Magistrate therefore *fearing *God, — by-*whatsoever *modes and *means *he-*can, *these *useless *earth-*cattle together with *filths-*their-*own from *bounds *of-*his-*own *republic *will-*ban**. *Absent indeed from *piety of *true *Christians, *either *species of *evil to-*have, or in-*any-*way *occasion of *evil to-*present: *let-*fear *rather *all *woe-*that of *Savior, — *who *against *all *scandals-*giving with-*great *severity *thundered* (Matt 18:6).
